items.sentence_translation: Please ask at the reception desk.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -ion are always feminine.

items.sentence_de: Ist diese Antwort richtig oder falsch?
items.sentence_translation: Is this answer correct or false?
items.grammar_tip: Commonly used as an adverb or adjective meaning correct.

items.sentence_de: In der Nacht ist es hier ruhig.
items.sentence_translation: At night it is quiet here.
items.grammar_tip: Used to describe both places and personality.

items.sentence_de: Ich fahre mit der S-Bahn zur Arbeit.
items.sentence_translation: I go to work by suburban train.
items.grammar_tip: Short for Stadtschnellbahn; feminine like 'die Bahn'.

items.sentence_de: Möchten Sie ein Glas Saft trinken?
items.sentence_translation: Would you like to drink a glass of juice?
items.grammar_tip: Masculine noun; the plural adds an umlaut: 'Säfte'.

items.sentence_de: Was sagen Sie zu diesem Plan?
items.sentence_translation: What do you say to this plan?
items.grammar_tip: A basic weak verb: ich sage, du sagst, er sagt.

items.sentence_de: Ich bestelle einen Salat ohne Tomaten.
items.sentence_translation: I am ordering a salad without tomatoes.
items.grammar_tip: Masculine noun; singular takes -en in accusative.

items.sentence_de: Reichen Sie mir bitte das Salz?
items.sentence_translation: Could you please pass me the salt?
items.grammar_tip: Neuter noun; almost always used in the singular.

items.sentence_de: Ich werde dir heute eine E-Mail schicken.
items.sentence_translation: I will send you an email today.
items.grammar_tip: Similar to 'senden', used for physical or digital mail.

items.sentence_de: Auf dem Schild steht: Bitte warten.
items.sentence_translation: The sign says: Please wait.
items.grammar_tip: 'Das Schild' means sign; 'Der Schild' means shield.

items.sentence_de: Ich möchte ein Brötchen mit Schinken.
items.sentence_translation: I would like a bread roll with ham.
items.grammar_tip: Masculine noun; the plural remains the same.

items.sentence_de: Mir ist heute ein bisschen schlecht.
items.sentence_translation: I feel a bit sick today.
items.grammar_tip: Used with 'mir ist...' to describe feeling unwell.

items.sentence_de: Am Schluss machen wir ein Foto.
items.sentence_translation: At the end, we take a photo.
items.grammar_tip: 'Schluss' is masculine; used in the phrase 'Am Schluss'.

items.sentence_de: Hast du den Schlüssel für die Wohnung?
items.sentence_translation: Do you have the key for the apartment?
items.grammar_tip: Masculine noun; singular and plural are the same.

items.sentence_de: Die Spaghetti schmecken mir sehr gut.
items.sentence_translation: The spaghetti tastes very good to me.
items.grammar_tip: Usually used with a dative object (mir, dir, ihm).

items.sentence_de: Das Auto fährt sehr schnell auf der Autobahn.
items.sentence_translation: The car drives very fast on the highway.
items.grammar_tip: Opposite of 'langsam'.

items.sentence_de: Ich bin schon fertig mit der Arbeit.
items.sentence_translation: I am already finished with the work.
items.grammar_tip: Do not confuse 'schon' (already) with 'schön' (beautiful).

items.sentence_de: Das Wetter heute ist wirklich sehr schön.
items.sentence_translation: The weather today is really very beautiful.
items.grammar_tip: Notice the umlaut 'ö'; it changes the meaning from 'schon'.

items.sentence_de: Zieh bitte deinen linken Schuh an.
items.sentence_translation: Please put on your left shoe.
items.grammar_tip: Masculine; plural 'Schuhe' is much more common.

items.sentence_de: Meine Kinder gehen jeden Tag zur Schule.
items.sentence_translation: My children go to school every day.
items.grammar_tip: Feminine noun; 'zur Schule' implies being a student.

items.sentence_de: Deutsch lernen ist am Anfang oft schwer.
items.sentence_translation: Learning German is often difficult at the beginning.
items.grammar_tip: Means both 'heavy' (weight) and 'difficult' (hard).

items.sentence_de: Meine Schwester wohnt jetzt in London.
items.sentence_translation: My sister is living in London now.
items.grammar_tip: Feminine person noun; plural is 'Schwestern'.

items.sentence_de: Im Sommer gehen wir oft ins Schwimmbad.
items.sentence_translation: In the summer we often go to the swimming pool.
items.grammar_tip: Compound noun: das Schwimmen + das Bad = das Schwimmbad.

items.sentence_de: Wir machen ein Picknick am See.
items.sentence_translation: We are having a picnic by the lake.
items.grammar_tip: 'Der See' is lake; 'Die See' is the sea (ocean).

items.sentence_de: Das Brandenburger Tor ist eine berühmte Sehenswürdigkeit.
items.sentence_translation: The Brandenburg Gate is a famous tourist attraction.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -keit are always feminine.

items.sentence_de: Vielen Dank, es geht mir sehr gut.
items.sentence_translation: Thank you very much, I am doing very well.
items.grammar_tip: Used to intensify adjectives or adverbs.

items.sentence_de: Ich lerne seit drei Monaten Deutsch.
items.sentence_translation: I have been learning German for three months.
items.grammar_tip: 'Seit' always takes the Dative case in German.

items.sentence_de: Er muss sich nach der Arbeit ausruhen.
items.sentence_translation: He must rest (himself) after work.
items.grammar_tip: Reflexive pronoun for 3rd person singular and plural.

items.sentence_de: Das Projekt ist leider nur so lala.
items.sentence_translation: The project is unfortunately only so-so.
items.grammar_tip: 'So lala' is a common expression for 'okay/mediocre'.

items.sentence_de: Das Sofa im Wohnzimmer ist sehr bequem.
items.sentence_translation: The sofa in the living room is very comfortable.
items.grammar_tip: Neuter noun of foreign origin; plural is 'Sofas'.

items.sentence_de: Ich komme sofort, bitte warten Sie kurz.
items.sentence_translation: I'm coming immediately, please wait a moment.
items.grammar_tip: Synonym for 'gleich', but usually even faster.

items.sentence_de: Die Sonne scheint heute den ganzen Tag.
items.sentence_translation: The sun is shining all day today.
items.grammar_tip: Feminine noun; always used with 'die'.

items.sentence_de: Entschuldigung, ich bin heute leider etwas spät.
items.sentence_translation: Sorry, I am unfortunately a bit late today.
items.grammar_tip: Opposite of 'früh' or 'pünktlich'.

items.sentence_de: Können wir das bitte etwas später machen?
items.sentence_translation: Can we please do that a bit later?
items.grammar_tip: Comparative form of 'spät' (late).

items.sentence_de: Darf ich bitte die Speisekarte sehen?
items.sentence_translation: May I please see the menu?
items.grammar_tip: Compound: die Speise (food) + die Karte (card).

items.sentence_de: Die Kinder spielen gerne Fußball im Park.
items.sentence_translation: The children like to play football in the park.
items.grammar_tip: Used for games, sports, and musical instruments.

items.sentence_de: Ich treibe viel Sport in meiner Freizeit.
items.sentence_translation: I do a lot of sport in my free time.
items.grammar_tip: Usually used in singular with the verb 'treiben' or 'machen'.

items.sentence_de: Welche Sprache sprechen Sie zu Hause?
items.sentence_translation: Which language do you speak at home?
items.grammar_tip: Feminine noun; plural ends in -n.

items.sentence_de: Ich suche eine neue Stelle als Verkäufer.
items.sentence_translation: I am looking for a new position as a salesman.
items.grammar_tip: Feminine noun; often a synonym for 'Job' or 'Arbeitsplatz'.

items.sentence_de: Bitte stellen Sie den Computer auf den Tisch.
items.sentence_translation: Please put the computer on the table.
items.grammar_tip: 'Stellen' is used for vertical objects (standing).

items.sentence_de: Meine Wohnung liegt im dritten Stock.
items.sentence_translation: My apartment is on the third floor.
items.grammar_tip: Masculine; 'im Stock' is short for 'in dem Stockwerk'.

items.sentence_de: Gehen Sie bitte geradeaus über diese Straße.
items.sentence_translation: Please go straight across this street.
items.grammar_tip: Feminine noun; names of streets take 'die'.

items.sentence_de: Die Straßenbahn hält direkt vor dem Bahnhof.
items.sentence_translation: The tram stops directly in front of the station.
items.grammar_tip: Compound: die Straße + die Bahn.

items.sentence_de: Er ist Student an der Universität München.
items.sentence_translation: He is a student at the University of Munich.
items.grammar_tip: Specifically refers to a university student.

items.sentence_de: Ich möchte in Deutschland Medizin studieren.
items.sentence_translation: I want to study medicine in Germany.
items.grammar_tip: Used only for university studies, not school homework.

items.sentence_de: Der Kurs dauert genau eine Stunde.
items.sentence_translation: The course lasts exactly one hour.
items.grammar_tip: Refers to a duration of 60 minutes.

items.sentence_de: Ich suche meine Brille, hast du sie gesehen?
items.sentence_translation: I am looking for my glasses, have you seen them?
items.grammar_tip: Regular verb: ich suche, du suchst, er sucht.

items.sentence_de: Wollen wir am Samstagabend zusammen tanzen?
items.sentence_translation: Do we want to dance together on Saturday night?
items.grammar_tip: The stem ends in -z, so 'du' form is 'tanzt'.

items.sentence_de: In meiner Tasche ist viel Platz.
items.sentence_translation: There is a lot of space in my bag.
items.grammar_tip: Feminine; plural is 'Taschen'.

items.sentence_de: Wir nehmen ein Taxi zum Flughafen.
items.sentence_translation: We are taking a taxi to the airport.
items.grammar_tip: Neuter noun; plural is 'Taxis' (or 'Taxen').

items.sentence_de: Trinken Sie lieber Kaffee oder Tee?
items.sentence_translation: Do you prefer drinking coffee or tea?
items.grammar_tip: Masculine noun; usually singular.

items.sentence_de: Das ist der erste Teil vom Film.
items.sentence_translation: That is the first part of the movie.
items.grammar_tip: 'Der Teil' is masculine; plural is 'die Teile'.

items.sentence_de: Wie ist deine Nummer? Ich habe kein Telefon.
items.sentence_translation: What is your number? I don't have a telephone.
items.grammar_tip: Neuter; plural is 'Telefone'.

items.sentence_de: Ich muss heute noch mit meiner Mutter telefonieren.
items.sentence_translation: I still have to talk to my mother on the phone today.
items.grammar_tip: Always used with 'mit' + Dative.

items.sentence_de: Ich habe heute um zehn Uhr einen Termin.
items.sentence_translation: I have an appointment today at ten o'clock.
items.grammar_tip: Masculine; plural is 'Termine'.

items.sentence_de: Der Test heute war nicht so schwer.
items.sentence_translation: The test today was not so difficult.
items.grammar_tip: Masculine; plural 'die Tests'.

items.sentence_de: Das neue Handy ist mir zu teuer.
items.sentence_translation: The new mobile phone is too expensive for me.
items.grammar_tip: Opposite of 'billig'.

items.sentence_de: Lesen Sie bitte den Text auf Seite fünf.
items.sentence_translation: Please read the text on page five.
items.grammar_tip: Masculine noun; plural is 'Texte'.

items.sentence_de: Haben Sie schon ein Ticket für den Zug?
items.sentence_translation: Do you already have a ticket for the train?
items.grammar_tip: Neuter; common synonym for 'Fahrkarte'.

items.sentence_de: Das Essen steht schon auf dem Tisch.
items.sentence_translation: The food is already on the table.
items.grammar_tip: Masculine; plural is 'Tische'.

items.sentence_de: Meine Tochter geht in die erste Klasse.
items.sentence_translation: My daughter goes to the first grade.
items.grammar_tip: Feminine; plural has an umlaut: 'Töchter'.

items.sentence_de: Entschuldigung, wo ist die Toilette bitte?
items.sentence_translation: Excuse me, where is the toilet please?
items.grammar_tip: Feminine nouns ending in -e like 'Toilette' usually take the plural -n.

items.sentence_de: Ich brauche für den Salat eine Tomate.
items.sentence_translation: I need a tomato for the salad.
items.grammar_tip: Tomate is a feminine noun.

items.sentence_de: Gehen Sie bitte die Treppe nach oben.
items.sentence_translation: Please go up the stairs.
items.grammar_tip: German uses 'die Treppe' for both a single step and a whole staircase.

items.sentence_de: Was kann ich für Sie tun?
items.sentence_translation: What can I do for you?
items.grammar_tip: 'Was kann ich für Sie tun?' is a standard formal helpful phrase.

items.sentence_de: Der Turm ist über hundert Jahre alt.
items.sentence_translation: The tower is over one hundred years old.
items.grammar_tip: 'Über' can indicate spatial position or 'more than' with numbers.

items.sentence_de: Wir übernachten heute in einem kleinen Hotel.
items.sentence_translation: We are staying in a small hotel tonight.
items.grammar_tip: This verb combines 'über' and 'Nacht' (night).

items.sentence_de: Ich arbeite von acht bis siebzehn Uhr.
items.sentence_translation: I work from eight to seventeen o'clock.
items.grammar_tip: 'Uhr' is used for the time of day, 'Stunde' for a duration.

items.sentence_de: Wir essen zusammen um sieben Uhr abends.
items.sentence_translation: We eat together at seven in the evening.
items.grammar_tip: Use 'um' for exact clock times.

items.sentence_de: Ich trinke gerne Kaffee und Tee.
items.sentence_translation: I like to drink coffee and tea.
items.grammar_tip: 'Und' connects words or sentences without changing the word order.

items.sentence_de: Die Toiletten sind hier unten im Keller.
items.sentence_translation: The toilets are down here in the basement.
items.grammar_tip: 'Unten' is a static adverb of place.

items.sentence_de: Die Katze schläft unter dem großen Tisch.
items.sentence_translation: The cat is sleeping under the large table.
items.grammar_tip: 'Unter' is a two-way preposition; here it takes dative for location.

items.sentence_de: Der Unterricht beginnt jeden Morgen um acht.
items.sentence_translation: The lesson begins every morning at eight.
items.grammar_tip: 'Unterricht' is usually used in the singular for the activity of teaching.

items.sentence_de: Ich brauche hier bitte noch Ihre Unterschrift.
items.sentence_translation: I still need your signature here, please.
items.grammar_tip: Formed from 'unter' (under) and 'Schrift' (writing).

items.sentence_de: Im Sommer machen wir Urlaub in Spanien.
items.sentence_translation: In summer we are going on holiday in Spain.
items.grammar_tip: 'Urlaub machen' is the standard expression for taking a vacation.

items.sentence_de: Mein Vater arbeitet als Arzt in Berlin.
items.sentence_translation: My father works as a doctor in Berlin.
items.grammar_tip: The plural 'Väter' uses an Umlaut.

items.sentence_de: Rauchen ist in diesem Gebäude leider verboten.
items.sentence_translation: Smoking is unfortunately forbidden in this building.
items.grammar_tip: This is the past participle of 'verbieten' used as an adjective.

items.sentence_de: In meinem neuen Job verdiene ich gut.
items.sentence_translation: In my new job, I earn well.
items.grammar_tip: Regular weak verb: ich verdiene, du verdienst.

items.sentence_de: Sind Sie verheiratet oder leben Sie allein?
items.sentence_translation: Are you married or do you live alone?
items.grammar_tip: A common question for personal status on forms.

items.sentence_de: Ich verkaufe mein altes Auto im Internet.
items.sentence_translation: I am selling my old car on the internet.
items.grammar_tip: The prefix 'ver-' often indicates a change or transfer.

items.sentence_de: Der Verkäufer im Laden ist sehr nett.
items.sentence_translation: The salesperson in the shop is very nice.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -er often have the same form in plural.

items.sentence_de: Herr Schmidt möchte seine Wohnung privat vermieten.
items.sentence_translation: Mr. Schmidt wants to rent out his flat privately.
items.grammar_tip: 'Mieten' is to pay to live there; 'vermieten' is to provide the place.

items.sentence_de: Mein Vermieter wohnt im Haus nebenan.
items.sentence_translation: My landlord lives in the house next door.
items.grammar_tip: The person who rents out the property.

items.sentence_de: Vielleicht kommen wir am Sonntag zu Besuch.
items.sentence_translation: Maybe we will come to visit on Sunday.
items.grammar_tip: Useful for expressing uncertainty.

items.sentence_de: Ich lese gerade ein Buch von Goethe.
items.sentence_translation: I am currently reading a book by Goethe.
items.grammar_tip: 'Von' always requires the dative case.

items.sentence_de: Der Artikel steht immer vor dem Substantiv.
items.sentence_translation: The article always stands before the noun.
items.grammar_tip: 'Vor' can be temporal (before) or local (in front of).

items.sentence_de: Wie ist Ihr Vorname und Ihr Familienname?
items.sentence_translation: What is your first name and your last name?
items.grammar_tip: 'Vor' (before) + 'Name' (name).

items.sentence_de: Wir wandern am Wochenende gerne im Wald.
items.sentence_translation: We like to hike in the forest on weekends.
items.grammar_tip: A very popular German hobby.

items.sentence_de: Ich muss zwanzig Minuten auf den Bus warten.
items.sentence_translation: I have to wait twenty minutes for the bus.
items.grammar_tip: In German, you wait 'auf' someone (accusative).

items.sentence_de: Möchten Sie ein Glas Wasser mit Kohlensäure?
items.sentence_translation: Would you like a glass of water with carbonation?
items.grammar_tip: Standard table water is 'Mineralwasser'.

items.sentence_de: Bitte kreuzen Sie 'weiblich' oder 'männlich' an.
items.sentence_translation: Please mark 'female' or 'male'.
items.grammar_tip: Commonly found on forms for gender.

items.sentence_de: Es ist von hier nicht weit zur Universität.
items.sentence_translation: It is not far to the university from here.
items.grammar_tip: Used for distance.

items.sentence_de: Es gibt viele schöne Länder auf der Welt.
items.sentence_translation: There are many beautiful countries in the world.
items.grammar_tip: 'Auf der Welt' is a fixed expression.

items.sentence_de: Ich spreche leider nur ein wenig Deutsch.
items.sentence_translation: Unfortunately, I only speak a little German.
items.grammar_tip: Used for uncountable quantities.

items.sentence_de: Wie ist das Wetter heute in Berlin?
items.sentence_translation: How is the weather today in Berlin?
items.grammar_tip: Always neuter: das Wetter.

items.sentence_de: Diese Information ist sehr wichtig für uns.
items.sentence_translation: This information is very important for us.
items.grammar_tip: Opposite of 'unwichtig'.

items.sentence_de: Können Sie den Satz bitte noch einmal wiederholen?
items.sentence_translation: Could you please repeat the sentence once more?
items.grammar_tip: Essential verb for language learners.

items.sentence_de: Herzlich willkommen in unserem neuen Haus!
items.sentence_translation: A warm welcome to our new house!
items.grammar_tip: Used as a greeting or an adjective.

items.sentence_de: Heute weht ein sehr kalter Wind draußen.
items.sentence_translation: A very cold wind is blowing outside today.
items.grammar_tip: Der Wind (masculine).

items.sentence_de: Ich wohne seit zwei Jahren in München.
items.sentence_translation: I have been living in Munich for two years.
items.grammar_tip: 'Wohnen' usually refers to a specific address or flat.

items.sentence_de: Meine Wohnung hat drei Zimmer und einen Balkon.
items.sentence_translation: My flat has three rooms and a balcony.
items.grammar_tip: Feminine noun ending in -ung.

items.sentence_de: Das Essen im Restaurant war einfach wunderbar.
items.sentence_translation: The food in the restaurant was simply wonderful.
items.grammar_tip: A high-praise adjective.

items.sentence_de: Wir möchten bitte zahlen, die Rechnung bitte!
items.sentence_translation: We would like to pay, the bill please!
items.grammar_tip: Don't confuse 'zahlen' (to pay) with 'zählen' (to count).

items.sentence_de: Ich habe heute leider keine Zeit für Sport.
items.sentence_translation: Unfortunately, I have no time for sports today.
items.grammar_tip: 'Keine Zeit haben' is a very common phrase.

items.sentence_de: Mein Opa liest jeden Morgen die Zeitung.
items.sentence_translation: My grandpa reads the newspaper every morning.
items.grammar_tip: Ends in -ung, therefore feminine.

items.sentence_de: Das Hotel hat noch ein freies Zimmer.
items.sentence_translation: The hotel still has a vacant room.
items.grammar_tip: Neuter noun; plural is the same as singular.

items.sentence_de: Wir arbeiten heute im Kurs zu zweit.
items.sentence_translation: We are working in pairs in the course today.
items.grammar_tip: 'Zu zweit' means 'in a group of two'.

items.sentence_de: Die Bäckerei ist am Sonntag leider zu.
items.sentence_translation: The bakery is unfortunately closed on Sunday.
items.grammar_tip: 'Zu' is used colloquially for 'geschlossen'.

items.sentence_de: Ich bin mit meiner Arbeit sehr zufrieden.
items.sentence_translation: I am very satisfied with my work.
items.grammar_tip: Used with the preposition 'mit'.

items.sentence_de: Wann kommst du aus dem Urlaub zurück?
items.sentence_translation: When are you coming back from holiday?
items.grammar_tip: Often used with verbs of movement like 'gehen' or 'kommen'.

items.sentence_de: Zurzeit habe ich leider keine Arbeit.
items.sentence_translation: Currently, I unfortunately have no job.
items.grammar_tip: Synonym for 'im Moment'.

items.sentence_de: Wir spielen jeden Freitag zusammen Fußball.
items.sentence_translation: We play football together every Friday.
items.grammar_tip: The opposite of 'allein'.

items.sentence_de: Der Bahnhof liegt zwischen der Post und dem Park.
items.sentence_translation: The station is located between the post office and the park.
items.grammar_tip: Requires dative for locations.

items.sentence_de: Möchtest du ein Würstchen vom Grill essen?
items.sentence_translation: Would you like to eat a sausage from the grill?
items.grammar_tip: The suffix '-chen' always makes a noun neuter.

items.sentence_de: Mein Sohn geht schon in den Kindergarten.
items.sentence_translation: My son is already going to kindergarten.
items.grammar_tip: A compound of 'Kinder' and 'Garten'.

items.sentence_de: Bringen Sie uns bitte eine Flasche Saft.
items.sentence_translation: Please bring us a bottle of juice.
items.grammar_tip: Feminine noun.

items.sentence_de: Ich wünsche Ihnen einen schönen Abend!
items.sentence_translation: I wish you a nice evening!
items.grammar_tip: Masculine noun; used in greetings.

items.sentence_de: Was gibt es heute zum Abendessen?
items.sentence_translation: What is there for dinner today?
items.grammar_tip: A compound of 'Abend' and 'Essen'.

items.sentence_de: In der Oper trägt man oft Abendkleidung.
items.sentence_translation: People often wear evening wear at the opera.
items.grammar_tip: Formal clothes for the evening.

items.sentence_de: Ich sehe abends gerne ein bisschen fern.
items.sentence_translation: I like to watch a bit of TV in the evenings.
items.grammar_tip: Adverbs of time ending in -s denote regularity.

items.sentence_de: Der Zug nach Berlin fährt um neun Uhr ab.
items.sentence_translation: The train to Berlin departs at nine o'clock.
items.grammar_tip: 'Abfahren' is a separable verb (fährt ... ab).

items.sentence_de: Lesen Sie bitte den ersten Abschnitt im Text.
items.sentence_translation: Please read the first section in the text.
items.grammar_tip: Used for parts of a text or document.

items.sentence_de: Wir sollten uns beim Lesen abwechseln.
items.sentence_translation: We should take turns while reading.
items.grammar_tip: Separable verb: ab-wechseln.

items.sentence_de: Bitte lesen Sie den Dialog abwechselnd vor.
items.sentence_translation: Please read the dialogue alternatingly.
items.grammar_tip: Used to describe how an action is shared.

items.sentence_de: Bitte achten Sie auf die richtige Aussprache.
items.sentence_translation: Please pay attention to the correct pronunciation.
items.grammar_tip: Usually used with 'auf' + accusative.

items.sentence_de: Achtung! Der Zug fährt jetzt ein.
items.sentence_translation: Attention! The train is arriving now.
items.grammar_tip: Used to warn or get someone's attention.

items.sentence_de: Meine Schwester ist gerade achtzehn Jahre alt.
items.sentence_translation: My sister is exactly eighteen years old.
items.grammar_tip: Formed by 'acht' + 'zehn'.

items.sentence_de: Das Buch kostet genau achtzig Euro.
items.sentence_translation: The book costs exactly eighty euros.
items.grammar_tip: Numbers ending in -zig represent tens.

items.sentence_de: Das Wort 'schön' ist ein deutsches Adjektiv.
items.sentence_translation: The word 'schön' is a German adjective.
items.grammar_tip: Neuter noun in German.

items.sentence_de: Er sucht einen Job bei der Agentur für Arbeit.
items.sentence_translation: He is looking for a job at the employment office.
items.grammar_tip: The official German government body for employment.

items.sentence_de: Die beiden Brüder sehen sich sehr ähnlich.
items.sentence_translation: The two brothers look very similar to each other.
items.grammar_tip: Used to compare things that are not identical.

items.sentence_de: Mein Akku ist fast leer, ich muss laden.
items.sentence_translation: My battery is almost empty, I need to charge it.
items.grammar_tip: Short for Akkumulator; masculine.

items.sentence_de: Das Verb 'haben' braucht immer den Akkusativ.
items.sentence_translation: The verb 'haben' always needs the accusative.
items.grammar_tip: One of the four German cases.

items.sentence_de: Im Urlaub sind wir immer sehr aktiv.
items.sentence_translation: We are always very active on holiday.
items.grammar_tip: Used for people or activities.

items.sentence_de: Welche Aktivität macht dir am meisten Spaß?
items.sentence_translation: Which activity do you enjoy the most?
items.grammar_tip: Feminine noun ending in -tät.

items.sentence_de: Gibt es heute keine aktuellen Nachrichten?
items.sentence_translation: Are there no current news stories today?
items.grammar_tip: Refers to the present time.

items.sentence_de: Mein Freund kommt aus Algerien.
items.sentence_translation: My friend comes from Algeria.
items.grammar_tip: Countries are usually used without articles in German unless they have a gendered name.

items.sentence_de: Sind alle Teilnehmer im Kurs da?
items.sentence_translation: Are all participants in the course there?
items.grammar_tip: 'Alle' behaves like a plural determiner and indicates the total number of items.

items.sentence_de: Das ist alles für heute.
items.sentence_translation: That is everything for today.
items.grammar_tip: 'Alles' is a neuter singular pronoun meaning 'everything'.

items.sentence_de: Ist das Essen schon alles fertig?
items.sentence_translation: Is the food already all done?
items.grammar_tip: This phrase is used to indicate that a task or preparation is complete.

items.sentence_de: Der Alltag ist oft sehr stressig.
items.sentence_translation: Everyday life is often very stressful.
items.grammar_tip: Alltag is a masculine noun composed of 'all' and 'Tag' (day).

items.sentence_de: Wie viele Buchstaben hat das Alphabet?
items.sentence_translation: How many letters does the alphabet have?
items.grammar_tip: German nouns ending in -et are often neuter.

items.sentence_de: Ich arbeite als Koch in Berlin.
items.sentence_translation: I work as a cook in Berlin.
items.grammar_tip: Use 'als' when talking about professions or roles.

items.sentence_de: Sie sucht eine schöne Altbauwohnung.
items.sentence_translation: She is looking for a beautiful old building flat.
items.grammar_tip: German 'Altbau' refers to buildings built before WWII, known for high ceilings.

items.sentence_de: Die Altstadt hat viele kleine Cafés.
items.sentence_translation: The old town has many small cafes.
items.grammar_tip: 'Stadt' is feminine, so compound words ending in 'stadt' are also feminine.

items.sentence_de: Wir kochen am Wochenende zusammen Spaghetti.
items.sentence_translation: We are cooking spaghetti together on the weekend.
items.grammar_tip: 'am' is a contraction of 'an dem', used for days of the week and times of day.

items.sentence_de: Wir sitzen draußen an Tischen.
items.sentence_translation: We are sitting outside at tables.
items.grammar_tip: 'An' is used for positions close to or beside an object.

items.sentence_de: Haben Sie auch andere Farben?
items.sentence_translation: Do you also have other colors?
items.grammar_tip: 'Andere' is used to refer to additional or different items.

items.sentence_de: Hier ist alles ganz anders.
items.sentence_translation: Everything is completely different here.
items.grammar_tip: 'Anders' is an adverb meaning 'in a different way'.

items.sentence_de: Der Kurs fängt um acht an.
items.sentence_translation: The course starts at eight.
items.grammar_tip: 'Anfangen' is a separable verb; the prefix 'an' goes to the end in main clauses.

items.sentence_de: Machen Sie Angaben zu Ihrer Person.
items.sentence_translation: Provide information about yourself.
items.grammar_tip: 'Angabe' often appears in the plural 'Angaben' in forms and exercises.

items.sentence_de: Die Datei ist im Anhang.
items.sentence_translation: The file is in the attachment.
items.grammar_tip: In emails, 'Anhang' refers to the attached file.

items.sentence_de: Der Zug kommt pünktlich an.
items.sentence_translation: The train arrives on time.
items.grammar_tip: 'Ankommen' is separable and uses 'sein' in the perfect tense.

items.sentence_de: Er nimmt die Einladung an.
items.sentence_translation: He accepts the invitation.
items.grammar_tip: 'Annehmen' is a separable verb with an e-to-i stem change.

items.sentence_de: Kann ich diese Jacke anprobieren?
items.sentence_translation: Can I try this jacket on?
items.grammar_tip: Used specifically for trying on clothing in a shop.

items.sentence_de: Wie lautet die richtige Anredeformel?
items.sentence_translation: What is the correct salutation?
items.grammar_tip: In letters, this refers to phrases like 'Sehr geehrte Damen und Herren'.

items.sentence_de: Wir sehen uns einen Film an.
items.sentence_translation: We are watching a film.
items.grammar_tip: 'Ansehen' is separable and often used reflexively with 'uns' or 'mir'.

items.sentence_de: Die Arbeit ist heute sehr anstrengend.
items.sentence_translation: The work is very exhausting today.
items.grammar_tip: This adjective describes things that require a lot of effort.

items.sentence_de: Bitte lesen Sie die Anweisung genau.
items.sentence_translation: Please read the instruction carefully.
items.grammar_tip: 'Anweisung' is feminine and refers to a directive or order.

items.sentence_de: Ich ziehe mir eine Jacke an.
items.sentence_translation: I am putting on a jacket.
items.grammar_tip: 'Anziehen' is a separable verb used for putting on clothes.

items.sentence_de: Er trägt zur Hochzeit einen Anzug.
items.sentence_translation: He is wearing a suit to the wedding.
items.grammar_tip: Most masculine nouns that take an umlaut in plural are one syllable.

items.sentence_de: Möchten Sie ein Glas Apfelsaft?
items.sentence_translation: Would you like a glass of apple juice?
items.grammar_tip: Compound nouns take the gender of the last word (der Saft).

items.sentence_de: Eine Apfelsaftschorle ist sehr erfrischend.
items.sentence_translation: An apple juice spritzer is very refreshing.
items.grammar_tip: Schorle is feminine. It is a mix of juice and carbonated water.

items.sentence_de: Ich bestelle eine kleine Apfelschorle.
items.sentence_translation: I am ordering a small apple spritzer.
items.grammar_tip: A shorter version of 'Apfelsaftschorle'.

items.sentence_de: Wo ist die nächste Apotheke?
items.sentence_translation: Where is the nearest pharmacy?
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -e are usually feminine.

items.sentence_de: Ich lade eine neue App herunter.
items.sentence_translation: I am downloading a new app.
items.grammar_tip: 'App' is feminine in German (short for Applikation).

items.sentence_de: Im April regnet es oft.
items.sentence_translation: In April it rains often.
items.grammar_tip: Months in German are always masculine.

items.sentence_de: Sie spricht sehr gut Arabisch.
items.sentence_translation: She speaks Arabic very well.
items.grammar_tip: Languages are treated as neuter nouns and used without articles after 'sprechen'.

items.sentence_de: Mein Arbeitsalltag beginnt um neun.
items.sentence_translation: My workday starts at nine.
items.grammar_tip: A compound of 'Arbeit' and 'Alltag'.

items.sentence_de: Mein Arbeitsplatz ist im ersten Stock.
items.sentence_translation: My workplace is on the first floor.
items.grammar_tip: 'Platz' is masculine, so 'Arbeitsplatz' is masculine.

items.sentence_de: Wie lang ist Ihre tägliche Arbeitszeit?
items.sentence_translation: How long are your daily working hours?
items.grammar_tip: 'Zeit' is feminine, making the whole compound feminine.

items.sentence_de: Das Arbeitszimmer ist hell und groß.
items.sentence_translation: The office is bright and large.
items.grammar_tip: 'Zimmer' is neuter; its plural is identical to its singular.

items.sentence_de: Der Architekt plant ein neues Haus.
items.sentence_translation: The architect is planning a new house.
items.grammar_tip: This is a weak masculine noun (N-Deklination) in the plural.

items.sentence_de: Die Architektin zeichnet einen Plan.
items.sentence_translation: The architect (f) is drawing a plan.
items.grammar_tip: Add -in to the masculine profession to make it feminine.

items.sentence_de: Ich interessiere mich für moderne Architektur.
items.sentence_translation: I am interested in modern architecture.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -ur are typically feminine.

items.sentence_de: Das ist ein argentinisch Restaurant.
items.sentence_translation: That is an Argentinian restaurant.
items.grammar_tip: National adjectives are not capitalized unless they are part of a name.

items.sentence_de: Welche Art von Musik magst du?
items.sentence_translation: What type of music do you like?
items.grammar_tip: 'Art' means type, kind, or way.

items.sentence_de: Der Artikel steht vor dem Substantiv.
items.sentence_translation: The article stands before the noun.
items.grammar_tip: Grammar term: 'der', 'die', 'das' are definite articles.

items.sentence_de: Wir müssen die deutschen Artikel lernen.
items.sentence_translation: We must learn the German articles.
items.grammar_tip: Learning the gender (article) with every noun is essential in German.

items.sentence_de: Das Artikelbild passt nicht zum Text.
items.sentence_translation: The article picture doesn't fit the text.
items.grammar_tip: A compound of 'Artikel' and 'Bild' (neuter).

items.sentence_de: Ich muss heute zum Arzt gehen.
items.sentence_translation: I have to go to the doctor today.
items.grammar_tip: The plural 'Ärzte' gets an umlaut.

items.sentence_de: Der Arztbesuch dauert meistens nicht lange.
items.sentence_translation: The doctor's visit usually doesn't take long.
items.grammar_tip: A compound of 'Arzt' and 'Besuch'.

items.sentence_de: Die Ärztin untersucht das kranke Kind.
items.sentence_translation: The doctor (f) examines the sick child.
items.grammar_tip: Notice the umlaut 'Ä' in the feminine form.

items.sentence_de: Ich esse sehr gern asiatisch.
items.sentence_translation: I like eating Asian food very much.
items.grammar_tip: Used here as an adverb describing the cuisine style.

items.sentence_de: Welche Assoziation haben Sie bei 'Sommer'?
items.sentence_translation: What association do you have with 'summer'?
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -ion are always feminine.

items.sentence_de: Die Künstlerin arbeitet in ihrem Atelier.
items.sentence_translation: The artist works in her studio.
items.grammar_tip: A loanword from French, it is neuter in German.

items.sentence_de: Das Restaurant hat eine gemütliche Atmosphäre.
items.sentence_translation: The restaurant has a cozy atmosphere.
items.grammar_tip: Ends in -e, so it is feminine.

items.sentence_de: Der Eiffelturm ist eine berühmte Attraktion.
items.sentence_translation: The Eiffel Tower is a famous attraction.
items.grammar_tip: Refers to a tourist highlight or sight.

items.sentence_de: Das Angebot ist für viele attraktiv.
items.sentence_translation: The offer is attractive to many.
items.grammar_tip: Can describe people or abstract things like offers.

items.sentence_de: Ich komme auf jeden Fall zur Party.
items.sentence_translation: I am coming to the party in any case.
items.grammar_tip: A common idiom meaning 'definitely'.

items.sentence_de: Vielen Dank für den Anruf, auf Wiederhören!
items.sentence_translation: Thanks for the call, goodbye!
items.grammar_tip: Specifically used when ending a telephone conversation.

items.sentence_de: Es war nett, Sie zu treffen, auf Wiedersehen!
items.sentence_translation: It was nice to meet you, goodbye!
items.grammar_tip: The formal way to say goodbye in person.

items.sentence_de: Hören Sie auf die Aufforderung des Lehrers.
items.sentence_translation: Listen to the teacher's request.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -ung are always feminine.

items.sentence_de: Hast du deine Hausaufgaben für heute gemacht?
items.sentence_translation: Did you do your homework for today?
items.grammar_tip: 'Aufgabe' can mean task, exercise, or duty.

items.sentence_de: Kannst du bitte die Wäsche aufhängen?
items.sentence_translation: Can you please hang up the laundry?
items.grammar_tip: A separable verb often used with clothes or laundry.

items.sentence_de: Du musst mit dem Rauchen aufhören.
items.sentence_translation: You must stop smoking.
items.grammar_tip: A separable verb; 'mit etwas aufhören' means to stop doing something.

items.sentence_de: Kannst du bitte das Fenster aufmachen?
items.sentence_translation: Can you please open the window?
items.grammar_tip: A separable verb, synonym of 'öffnen'.

items.sentence_de: In der Schule muss man gut aufpassen.
items.sentence_translation: In school, one must pay good attention.
items.grammar_tip: Separable verb; 'auf jemanden aufpassen' means to look after someone.

items.sentence_de: Ich muss mir die Telefonnummer aufschreiben.
items.sentence_translation: I have to write down the phone number.
items.grammar_tip: Separable verb: 'auf' moves to the end in the present tense.

items.sentence_de: Ich muss jeden Morgen früh aufstehen.
items.sentence_translation: I have to get up early every morning.
items.grammar_tip: Separable verb; refers to getting out of bed or rising from a seat.

items.sentence_de: Wir wollen die Möbel neu aufstellen.
items.sentence_translation: We want to arrange the furniture anew.
items.grammar_tip: Separable verb meaning to set up or position something.

items.sentence_de: Der Aufzug fährt in den fünften Stock.
items.sentence_translation: The elevator goes to the fifth floor.
items.grammar_tip: Synonym for 'Lift'. It is masculine.

items.sentence_de: Im August haben viele Leute Urlaub.
items.sentence_translation: In August, many people have vacation.
items.grammar_tip: Like all months, 'August' is masculine.

items.sentence_de: Kennen Sie diesen deutschen Ausdruck?
items.sentence_translation: Do you know this German expression?
items.grammar_tip: Can mean a linguistic phrase or a computer printout.

items.sentence_de: Wie kann ich das auf Deutsch ausdrücken?
items.sentence_translation: How can I express that in German?
items.grammar_tip: Separable verb meaning to put into words.

items.sentence_de: Bitte füllen Sie dieses Formular aus.
items.sentence_translation: Please fill in this form.
items.grammar_tip: Separable verb used primarily for forms and blanks.

items.sentence_de: Wir gehen heute Abend zusammen aus.
items.sentence_translation: We are going out together this evening.
items.grammar_tip: Separable verb referring to social activities outside the home.

items.sentence_de: Die Auskunft am Bahnhof ist sehr hilfreich.
items.sentence_translation: The information desk at the station is very helpful.
items.grammar_tip: Usually refers to a specific information desk or a piece of info.

items.sentence_de: Ein Aussagesatz endet meistens mit einem Punkt.
items.sentence_translation: A declarative sentence usually ends with a period.
items.grammar_tip: In an 'Aussagesatz', the conjugated verb is in second position.

items.sentence_de: Du siehst heute wirklich sehr gut aus.
items.sentence_translation: You look really very good today.
items.grammar_tip: Separable verb used to describe appearance; 'aus' goes to the end.

items.sentence_de: Wir wohnen etwas außerhalb der Stadt.
items.sentence_translation: We live a bit outside of the city.
items.grammar_tip: Grammatically followed by the genitive case, though 'von' is often used in A1.

items.sentence_de: Diese Äußerung war sehr wichtig für uns.
items.sentence_translation: This remark was very important for us.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -ung are always feminine and usually abstract.

items.sentence_de: Ihre Aussprache ist bereits sehr gut.
items.sentence_translation: Your pronunciation is already very good.
items.grammar_tip: Aussprache refers to the way words are spoken aloud.

items.sentence_de: Wir müssen an der nächsten Station aussteigen.
items.sentence_translation: We have to get off at the next station.
items.grammar_tip: Aussteigen is a separable verb; the 'aus' moves to the end in simple present.

items.sentence_de: Die neue Ausstellung im Museum ist toll.
items.sentence_translation: The new exhibition in the museum is great.
items.grammar_tip: -ung nouns take the plural suffix -en.

items.sentence_de: Ich lerne die neuen Vokabeln auswendig.
items.sentence_translation: I am learning the new vocabulary by heart.
items.grammar_tip: 'Auswendig lernen' means to memorize something perfectly.

items.sentence_de: Du musst dir die Schuhe ausziehen.
items.sentence_translation: You have to take off your shoes.
items.grammar_tip: Ausziehen is the opposite of anziehen (to put on).

items.sentence_de: Der Bäcker verkauft jeden Morgen frisches Brot.
items.sentence_translation: The baker sells fresh bread every morning.
items.grammar_tip: Masculine professions ending in -er often have the same form in plural.

items.sentence_de: Sie trägt im Schwimmbad einen neuen Badeanzug.
items.sentence_translation: She is wearing a new swimsuit at the pool.
items.grammar_tip: Badeanzug is a compound noun: baden (bathe) + Anzug (suit).

items.sentence_de: Er hat seine Badehose zu Hause vergessen.
items.sentence_translation: He forgot his swimming trunks at home.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -e are typically feminine.

items.sentence_de: In diesem Laden gibt es schöne Bademode.
items.sentence_translation: There is beautiful swimwear in this shop.
items.grammar_tip: Mode means fashion; Bademode is specifically fashion for swimming.

items.sentence_de: Wir machen im Sommer einen Badeurlaub.
items.sentence_translation: We are going on a beach holiday in the summer.
items.grammar_tip: Compound nouns take the gender of the last word (der Urlaub).

items.sentence_de: Die Kinder spielen im Garten mit einem Ball.
items.sentence_translation: The children are playing with a ball in the garden.
items.grammar_tip: The plural of Ball involves an umlaut: die Bälle.

items.sentence_de: Mein Bruder spielt jeden Samstag Basketball.
items.sentence_translation: My brother plays basketball every Saturday.
items.grammar_tip: Sports names are usually used without an article.

items.sentence_de: Ich habe heute leider sehr starke Bauchschmerzen.
items.sentence_translation: Unfortunately, I have a very strong stomach ache today.
items.grammar_tip: This is almost always used in the plural form.

items.sentence_de: Vor unserem Haus steht ein alter Baum.
items.sentence_translation: There is an old tree in front of our house.
items.grammar_tip: The plural is die Bäume.

items.sentence_de: Wegen der Baustelle fährt der Bus anders.
items.sentence_translation: The bus is driving differently because of the construction site.
items.grammar_tip: German compound nouns with -stelle refer to a specific place or point.

items.sentence_de: Die Bauzeit für das Haus war kurz.
items.sentence_translation: The construction period for the house was short.
items.grammar_tip: Zeit is feminine; therefore Bauzeit is feminine.

items.sentence_de: Können Sie bitte meine Frage beantworten?
items.sentence_translation: Can you please answer my question?
items.grammar_tip: Beantworten takes a direct object (accusative).

items.sentence_de: Ich möchte bitte einen Becher Kaffee.
items.sentence_translation: I would like a cup of coffee, please.
items.grammar_tip: Becher usually refers to a cup without a handle (like a plastic cup).

items.sentence_de: Wie ist Ihr allgemeines Befinden heute?
items.sentence_translation: How is your general condition today?
items.grammar_tip: This noun comes from the verb 'befinden' (to feel/be located).

items.sentence_de: Seine Begeisterung für Musik ist wirklich groß.
items.sentence_translation: His enthusiasm for music is really great.
items.grammar_tip: The suffix -ung makes nouns feminine.

items.sentence_de: Der Beginn des Films ist um acht.
items.sentence_translation: The beginning of the film is at eight.
items.grammar_tip: Beginn is a synonym for 'Anfang'.

items.sentence_de: Ich habe heute einen Termin beim Arzt.
items.sentence_translation: I have an appointment at the doctor's today.
items.grammar_tip: 'Beim' is a contraction of 'bei dem'.

items.sentence_de: In Wien gehen wir oft ins Beisl.
items.sentence_translation: In Vienna, we often go to the pub.
items.grammar_tip: This is a regional Austrian term for a small restaurant or pub.

items.sentence_de: Wir treffen uns in einer kleinen Beiz.
items.sentence_translation: We are meeting in a small pub.
items.grammar_tip: This is a regional Swiss German term for a pub.

items.sentence_de: Ich bekomme jeden Tag viele E-Mails.
items.sentence_translation: I get many emails every day.
items.grammar_tip: Bekommen means 'to receive', not 'to become' (false friend).

items.sentence_de: Fußball ist ein sehr beliebter Sport.
items.sentence_translation: Football is a very popular sport.
items.grammar_tip: Beliebt describes something many people like.

items.sentence_de: Der neue Stuhl ist wirklich sehr bequem.
items.sentence_translation: The new chair is really very comfortable.
items.grammar_tip: Bequem can describe clothes, furniture, or situations.

items.sentence_de: Wir wandern am Wochenende auf einen Berg.
items.sentence_translation: We are hiking up a mountain this weekend.
items.grammar_tip: The plural is 'die Berge'.

items.sentence_de: Die Bergtour war anstrengend, aber sehr schön.
items.sentence_translation: The mountain tour was exhausting but very beautiful.
items.grammar_tip: Tour is feminine, so Bergtour is feminine.

items.sentence_de: Ich muss für morgen einen Bericht schreiben.
items.sentence_translation: I have to write a report for tomorrow.
items.grammar_tip: Bericht is related to the verb 'berichten'.

items.sentence_de: Die Journalisten berichten über das große Fest.
items.sentence_translation: The journalists are reporting on the big festival.
items.grammar_tip: Berichten is often used with the preposition 'über'.

items.sentence_de: Berlin ist die Hauptstadt von Deutschland.
items.sentence_translation: Berlin is the capital of Germany.
items.grammar_tip: City names in German are usually neuter and used without an article.

items.sentence_de: Es gibt viele verschiedene Berufe im Krankenhaus.
items.sentence_translation: There are many different professions in the hospital.
items.grammar_tip: 'Krankenhaus' is neuter: das Krankenhaus.

items.sentence_de: Koch und Kellner sind Berufe rund ums Essen.
items.sentence_translation: Chef and waiter are professions related to food.
items.grammar_tip: 'Rund ums' is a short form of 'rund um das'.

items.sentence_de: Dieser Schauspieler ist auf der ganzen Welt berühmt.
items.sentence_translation: This actor is famous all over the world.
items.grammar_tip: Berühmt is a stronger version of 'bekannt' (known).

items.sentence_de: Können Sie bitte Ihren Weg zur Arbeit beschreiben?
items.sentence_translation: Can you please describe your way to work?
items.grammar_tip: Beschreiben is a combination of 'be-' and 'schreiben'.

items.sentence_de: Heute ist ein besonderer Tag für mich.
items.sentence_translation: Today is a special day for me.
items.grammar_tip: Besonderer is an inflected form of the adjective 'besonders'.

items.sentence_de: Das Essen in diesem Restaurant ist besonders gut.
items.sentence_translation: The food in this restaurant is especially good.
items.grammar_tip: Besonders is used here as an intensifier.

items.sentence_de: Wir haben um zehn Uhr eine wichtige Besprechung.
items.sentence_translation: We have an important meeting at ten o'clock.
items.grammar_tip: Besprechung is commonly used in business contexts.

items.sentence_de: Ihre Bestellung ist in zwei Tagen fertig.
items.sentence_translation: Your order will be ready in two days.
items.grammar_tip: Bestellung comes from the verb 'bestellen'.

items.sentence_de: Wir werden uns bestimmt bald wiedersehen.
items.sentence_translation: We will certainly see each other again soon.
items.grammar_tip: Bestimmt expresses a high level of certainty.

items.sentence_de: Der bestimmte Artikel für 'Haus' ist 'das'.
items.sentence_translation: The definite article for 'house' is 'das'.
items.grammar_tip: In German, the definite articles are der, die, and das.

items.sentence_de: Wir erwarten am Wochenende Besuch von Freunden.
items.sentence_translation: We are expecting a visit from friends this weekend.
items.grammar_tip: Besuch can mean the act of visiting or the guests themselves.

items.sentence_de: Der Zoo hat jeden Tag viele Besucher.
items.sentence_translation: The zoo has many visitors every day.
items.grammar_tip: The plural is identical to the singular: die Besucher.

items.sentence_de: Eine Besucherin hat ihre Tasche im Museum vergessen.
items.sentence_translation: A female visitor forgot her bag in the museum.
items.grammar_tip: Feminine job/person titles almost always end in -in.

items.sentence_de: In diesem Wort ist die erste Silbe betont.
items.sentence_translation: In this word, the first syllable is stressed.
items.grammar_tip: Used in linguistics to indicate where the emphasis lies in a word.

items.sentence_de: Die Betonung liegt auf dem Buchstaben 'a'.
items.sentence_translation: The stress lies on the letter 'a'.
items.grammar_tip: Refers to word or sentence emphasis.

items.sentence_de: Bitte schreiben Sie die Nummer in den Betreff.
items.sentence_translation: Please write the number in the subject line.
items.grammar_tip: Commonly found in email or letter headers.

items.sentence_de: Sie muss heute die Kinder der Nachbarn betreuen.
items.sentence_translation: She has to look after the neighbors' children today.
items.grammar_tip: Betreuen involves taking care of someone or something.

items.sentence_de: Ich kann meinen Arm nicht mehr richtig bewegen.
items.sentence_translation: I can't move my arm properly anymore.
items.grammar_tip: Refers to physical movement.

items.sentence_de: Viel Bewegung ist sehr gut für die Gesundheit.
items.sentence_translation: Lots of movement is very good for health.
items.grammar_tip: Used often in the context of fitness or physical activity.

items.sentence_de: Ich schicke heute meine Bewerbung an die Firma.
items.sentence_translation: I am sending my application to the company today.
items.grammar_tip: Often used with the verb 'schreiben' or 'schicken'.

items.sentence_de: Die Bewohner des Hauses sind sehr freundlich.
items.sentence_translation: The residents of the house are very friendly.
items.grammar_tip: Refers to people living in a specific building or city.

items.sentence_de: Meine Nachbarin ist eine sehr nette Bewohnerin.
items.sentence_translation: My neighbor is a very nice resident.
items.grammar_tip: The plural is Bewohnerinnen.

items.sentence_de: Heute ist der Himmel leider sehr bewölkt.
items.sentence_translation: Unfortunately, the sky is very cloudy today.
items.grammar_tip: Comes from the noun 'Wolke' (cloud).

items.sentence_de: Ich lerne oft in der Bibliothek für Prüfungen.
items.sentence_translation: I often study in the library for exams.
items.grammar_tip: Bibliothek is a feminine noun of Greek origin.

items.sentence_de: Im Sommer sitzen wir gerne im Biergarten.
items.sentence_translation: In summer we like to sit in the beer garden.
items.grammar_tip: A typical German outdoor eating and drinking area.

items.sentence_de: Sie kauft sich einen neuen Bikini für den Urlaub.
items.sentence_translation: She is buying a new bikini for the holiday.
items.grammar_tip: The plural is formed with -s: Bikinis.

items.sentence_de: Bilden Sie bitte drei Gruppen für das Spiel.
items.sentence_translation: Please form three groups for the game.
items.grammar_tip: Commonly used in classroom instructions.

items.sentence_de: Schreiben Sie einen Text zu dieser Bildgeschichte.
items.sentence_translation: Write a text about this picture story.
items.grammar_tip: Bild (picture) + Geschichte (story).

items.sentence_de: Die Baustelle bleibt noch bis 2024 hier.
items.sentence_translation: The construction site will stay here until 2024.
items.grammar_tip: Used to indicate a time limit.

items.sentence_de: Tschüss, ich muss gehen. Bis bald!
items.sentence_translation: Bye, I have to go. See you soon!
items.grammar_tip: A very common informal goodbye.

items.sentence_de: Wir treffen uns um acht. Bis dann!
items.sentence_translation: We are meeting at eight. See you then!
items.grammar_tip: Used when a specific time to meet has just been set.

items.sentence_de: Ich komme gleich wieder. Bis später!
items.sentence_translation: I'll be right back. See you later!
items.grammar_tip: Used when you expect to see the person later that same day.

items.sentence_de: In dieser Klasse sind bis zu zwanzig Kinder.
items.sentence_translation: There are up to twenty children in this class.
items.grammar_tip: Used to indicate a maximum limit.

items.sentence_de: Der Himmel ist heute wunderschön und blau.
items.sentence_translation: The sky is beautiful and blue today.
items.grammar_tip: German colors are adjectives and are not capitalized unless they are nouns.

items.sentence_de: Wie lange bleiben Sie in dieser Stadt?
items.sentence_translation: How long are you staying in this city?
items.grammar_tip: Bleiben takes the auxiliary verb 'sein' in the perfect tense.

items.sentence_de: Er schreibt jede Woche einen neuen Blog.
items.sentence_translation: He writes a new blog every week.
items.grammar_tip: The plural is Blogs.

items.sentence_de: Diese weiße Bluse passt gut zu deinem Rock.
items.sentence_translation: This white blouse goes well with your skirt.
items.grammar_tip: A blouse is typically worn by women; men wear a 'Hemd'.

items.sentence_de: Der Arzt muss eine Probe von deinem Blut nehmen.
items.sentence_translation: The doctor needs to take a sample of your blood.
items.grammar_tip: Blut is a neuter mass noun and rarely used in plural.

items.sentence_de: Meine Freundin kommt aus Brasilien.
items.sentence_translation: My friend comes from Brazil.
items.grammar_tip: Most country names in German do not use an article.

items.sentence_de: Die Blätter an den Bäumen werden im Herbst braun.
items.sentence_translation: The leaves on the trees turn brown in autumn.
items.grammar_tip: Standard color adjective.

items.sentence_de: Bitte beachten Sie den Briefstandard für offizielle Schreiben.
items.sentence_translation: Please note the standard letter format for official letters.
items.grammar_tip: Refers to the norm for letter writing/sizing.

items.sentence_de: Können Sie mir bitte die Rechnung bringen?
items.sentence_translation: Can you please bring me the bill?
items.grammar_tip: Bringen often takes a dative object (person) and accusative object (thing).

items.sentence_de: Wir gehen über die Brücke in die Stadt.
items.sentence_translation: We are going over the bridge into the city.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -e are often feminine.

items.sentence_de: Ich lese jeden Abend ein interessantes Buch.
items.sentence_translation: I read an interesting book every evening.
items.grammar_tip: The plural of 'Buch' is 'Bücher'.

items.sentence_de: Im Buchladen kaufe ich ein neues Wörterbuch.
items.sentence_translation: In the bookstore I am buying a new dictionary.
items.grammar_tip: Compound nouns take the gender of the last word.

items.sentence_de: Die Musiker stehen heute auf der Bühne.
items.sentence_translation: The musicians are standing on the stage today.
items.grammar_tip: 'Auf der Bühne' uses the dative case for location.

items.sentence_de: Sprichst du auch ein bisschen Bulgarisch?
items.sentence_translation: Do you also speak a little Bulgarian?
items.grammar_tip: Languages are treated as neuter nouns and usually used without an article.

items.sentence_de: Die alte Burg liegt oben auf dem Berg.
items.sentence_translation: The old castle is located up on the mountain.
items.grammar_tip: A 'Burg' is a fortress, while a 'Schloss' is a palace.

items.sentence_de: Ich arbeite von Montag bis Freitag im Büro.
items.sentence_translation: I work from Monday to Friday in the office.
items.grammar_tip: 'Im' is a contraction of 'in dem'.

items.sentence_de: Möchtest du ein Butterbrot für die Pause?
items.sentence_translation: Would you like a sandwich for the break?
items.grammar_tip: Literally 'butter bread', it refers to a simple open-faced or closed sandwich.

items.sentence_de: Wir machen im Sommer einen Campingurlaub.
items.sentence_translation: We are going on a camping holiday in the summer.
items.grammar_tip: 'Urlaub' is always masculine.

items.sentence_de: Das Brötchen kostet nur fünfzig Cent.
items.sentence_translation: The bread roll costs only fifty cents.
items.grammar_tip: Units of currency usually stay singular after numbers.

items.sentence_de: Ich brauche für die Pizza noch einen Champignon.
items.sentence_translation: I still need a mushroom for the pizza.
items.grammar_tip: This is a loanword from French, but follows German grammar.

items.sentence_de: Meine Chefin ist heute sehr zufrieden.
items.sentence_translation: My boss is very satisfied today.
items.grammar_tip: The suffix -in denotes a female professional.

items.sentence_de: Am Wochenende möchte ich einfach nur chillen.
items.sentence_translation: On the weekend I just want to chill.
items.grammar_tip: This is a modern loanword from English.

items.sentence_de: Wir essen beim Fernsehen gerne Chips.
items.sentence_translation: We like to eat crisps while watching TV.
items.grammar_tip: Usually used in the plural form.

items.sentence_de: Er singt jeden Dienstag im Chor.
items.sentence_translation: He sings in the choir every Tuesday.
items.grammar_tip: 'Chor' starts with a 'K' sound.

items.sentence_de: Ich gehe jetzt nach Hause, ciao!
items.sentence_translation: I'm going home now, bye!
items.grammar_tip: Informal goodbye used frequently in Germany.

items.sentence_de: Die Fahrt dauert circa zwanzig Minuten.
items.sentence_translation: The journey takes approximately twenty minutes.
items.grammar_tip: Often abbreviated as 'ca.'.

items.sentence_de: Wir gehen am Samstag in einen Club.
items.sentence_translation: We are going to a club on Saturday.
items.grammar_tip: Refers to a disco or a social association.

items.sentence_de: Ich lerne Spanisch im Club Español.
items.sentence_translation: I learn Spanish at the Club Español.
items.grammar_tip: Proper names of clubs usually don't change.

items.sentence_de: In dieser Straße gibt es Kneipen & Co.
items.sentence_translation: In this street there are bars and so on.
items.grammar_tip: '& Co' is used like 'and others' or 'and the like'.

items.sentence_de: Mein Sohn liest am liebsten einen Comic.
items.sentence_translation: My son prefers reading a comic book.
items.grammar_tip: Plural is formed with -s.

items.sentence_de: Meine Augen sind müde von der Computerarbeit.
items.sentence_translation: My eyes are tired from the computer work.
items.grammar_tip: Feminine because 'Arbeit' is feminine.

items.sentence_de: Er sucht einen Job bei einer Computerfirma.
items.sentence_translation: He is looking for a job at a computer company.
items.grammar_tip: 'Firma' changes to 'Firmen' in plural.

items.sentence_de: Ich habe heute ein großes Computerproblem.
items.sentence_translation: I have a big computer problem today.
items.grammar_tip: 'Problem' is always neuter.

items.sentence_de: Dein neues Fahrrad sieht echt cool aus.
items.sentence_translation: Your new bike looks really cool.
items.grammar_tip: Used mostly in informal spoken German.

items.sentence_de: Wann wirst du morgen wieder da sein?
items.sentence_translation: When will you be there again tomorrow?
items.grammar_tip: 'Da' means 'there' or 'present'.

items.sentence_de: Die Post ist gleich da vorne rechts.
items.sentence_translation: The post office is right over there on the right.
items.grammar_tip: Used to point out something nearby.

items.sentence_de: Die Damenmode befindet sich im ersten Stock.
items.sentence_translation: Women's fashion is located on the first floor.
items.grammar_tip: 'Mode' is always feminine.

items.sentence_de: Zuerst essen wir, danach gehen wir spazieren.
items.sentence_translation: First we eat, after that we go for a walk.
items.grammar_tip: A temporal adverb indicating subsequent action.

items.sentence_de: Hier ist Ihr Kaffee. - Oh, danke schön!
items.sentence_translation: Here is your coffee. - Oh, thank you!
items.grammar_tip: A more polite version of 'danke'.

items.sentence_de: Der Tisch ist leer, nichts liegt darauf.
items.sentence_translation: The table is empty, nothing is lying upon it.
items.grammar_tip: A pronominal adverb used to refer to a surface.

items.sentence_de: Bitte speichern Sie die Datei auf dem Desktop.
items.sentence_translation: Please save the file on the desktop.
items.grammar_tip: Refers to a digital file.

items.sentence_de: Wir müssen die Daten im System aktualisieren.
items.sentence_translation: We need to update the data/files in the system.
items.grammar_tip: Often used as a plural-only noun for 'data'.

items.sentence_de: Nach der Präposition 'mit' folgt der Dativ.
items.sentence_translation: The dative follows the preposition 'mit'.
items.grammar_tip: One of the four cases in German grammar.

items.sentence_de: Welches Datum haben wir heute eigentlich?
items.sentence_translation: What date do we actually have today?
items.grammar_tip: Note the irregular plural 'Daten'.

items.sentence_de: Ich nehme ein Schnitzel und dazu Pommes.
items.sentence_translation: I'll have a cutlet and fries with that.
items.grammar_tip: Used when adding an item to a meal or order.

items.sentence_de: Die Kinder sollen auch zur Familie dazugehören.
items.sentence_translation: The children should also belong to the family.
items.grammar_tip: A separable verb: 'gehören... dazu'.

items.sentence_de: Die Lampe hängt oben an der Decke.
items.sentence_translation: The lamp is hanging from the ceiling.
items.grammar_tip: Can also mean 'blanket'.

items.sentence_de: Wo ist der Deckel für diesen Topf?
items.sentence_translation: Where is the lid for this pot?
items.grammar_tip: The plural is the same as the singular.

items.sentence_de: Ist das dein Auto da vor dem Haus?
items.sentence_translation: Is that your car there in front of the house?
items.grammar_tip: Informal possessive pronoun for 'du'.

items.sentence_de: Die Schiffe fahren auf dem breiten Fluss.
items.sentence_translation: The ships sail on the wide river.
items.grammar_tip: Dative masculine/neuter singular article.

items.sentence_de: 'Dieser' ist ein Beispiel für einen Demonstrativartikel.
items.sentence_translation: 'This' is an example of a demonstrative article.
items.grammar_tip: Used to point out specific things.

items.sentence_de: Ich nehme den Bus zum Bahnhof.
items.sentence_translation: I take the bus to the station.
items.grammar_tip: Accusative masculine singular article.

items.sentence_de: Ich muss kurz über deine Frage denken.
items.sentence_translation: I have to think about your question for a moment.
items.grammar_tip: The past participle is 'gedacht'.

items.sentence_de: Zum Frühstück esse ich gern einen Joghurt.
items.sentence_translation: I like to eat a yogurt for breakfast.
items.grammar_tip: Both 'der' and 'das' are acceptable articles.

items.sentence_de: Möchtest du einen Keks zu deinem Tee?
items.sentence_translation: Would you like a cookie with your tea?
items.grammar_tip: Commonly used in masculine form.

items.sentence_de: Ich kaufe mir am Bahnhof ein Sandwich.
items.sentence_translation: I'm buying myself a sandwich at the station.
items.grammar_tip: Plural is usually 'Sandwiches'.

items.sentence_de: Eine Bekannte von mir wohnt in Berlin.
items.sentence_translation: An acquaintance of mine lives in Berlin.
items.grammar_tip: Functions like an adjective: 'der Bekannte' / 'die Bekannte'.

items.sentence_de: Der Deutsche dort spricht sehr gut Englisch.
items.sentence_translation: The German man there speaks English very well.
items.grammar_tip: Adjectival noun: 'ein Deutscher' but 'der Deutsche'.

items.sentence_de: Sie ist die Erste in der Schlange.
items.sentence_translation: She is the first in the line.
items.grammar_tip: Ordinal numbers act like adjectives.

items.sentence_de: Der Preis für eine erwachsene Person ist höher.
items.sentence_translation: The price for an adult person is higher.
items.grammar_tip: Refers to a grown-up.

items.sentence_de: Viele Jugendliche gehen am Wochenende ins Kino.
items.sentence_translation: Many teenagers go to the cinema at the weekend.
items.grammar_tip: Refers to people between 12 and 18.

items.sentence_de: Der Kranke muss heute im Bett bleiben.
items.sentence_translation: The sick person must stay in bed today.
items.grammar_tip: Noun derived from the adjective 'krank'.

items.sentence_de: Der Krankenwagen bringt den Verletzten ins Krankenhaus.
items.sentence_translation: The ambulance is taking the injured person to the hospital.
items.grammar_tip: Accusative masculine singular: 'den Verletzten'.

items.sentence_de: Ich besuche meine Verwandten oft an Weihnachten.
items.sentence_translation: I often visit my relatives at Christmas.
items.grammar_tip: General term for family members.

items.sentence_de: Das Design des neuen Autos ist toll.
items.sentence_translation: The design of the new car is great.
items.grammar_tip: Loanword from English, neuter gender.

items.sentence_de: Der Designer entwirft ein neues Logo.
items.sentence_translation: The designer is designing a new logo.
items.grammar_tip: The plural is identical to the singular.

items.sentence_de: Sie arbeitet als Designerin in einer Agentur.
items.sentence_translation: She works as a designer in an agency.
items.grammar_tip: Female form of Designer.

items.sentence_de: Als Designfan mag ich diese moderne Lampe.
items.sentence_translation: As a design fan, I like this modern lamp.
items.grammar_tip: Someone who is very interested in design.

items.sentence_de: Möchten Sie nach dem Essen ein Dessert?
items.sentence_translation: Would you like a dessert after the meal?
items.grammar_tip: Synonym for 'Nachtisch'.

items.sentence_de: Mein Freund ist deutsch und kommt aus Berlin.
items.sentence_translation: My friend is German and comes from Berlin.
items.grammar_tip: The adjective is written in lowercase.

items.sentence_de: In der Schule lerne ich fleißig Deutsch.
items.sentence_translation: I am studying German diligently at school.
items.grammar_tip: Language names are capitalized nouns.

items.sentence_de: Ich habe mein Deutschbuch zu Hause vergessen.
items.sentence_translation: I forgot my German book at home.
items.grammar_tip: Compound: Deutsch + Buch.

items.sentence_de: Die Deutsche wohnt erst seit gestern hier.
items.sentence_translation: The German woman has only lived here since yesterday.
items.grammar_tip: Refers to a German woman.

items.sentence_de: Deutschland liegt in der Mitte von Europa.
items.sentence_translation: Germany is located in the middle of Europe.
items.grammar_tip: Countries usually don't have articles unless plural or specific.

items.sentence_de: Österreich ist ein deutschsprachig Land in Europa.
items.sentence_translation: Austria is a German-speaking country in Europe.
items.grammar_tip: Compound adjective: deutsch + sprachig.

items.sentence_de: Im Dezember schneit es oft in Deutschland.
items.sentence_translation: In December it often snows in Germany.
items.grammar_tip: All months in German are masculine.

items.sentence_de: Hören Sie den Dialog und antworten Sie.
items.sentence_translation: Listen to the dialogue and answer.
items.grammar_tip: Common task in language learning.

items.sentence_de: Ich trinke eine kalte Cola zum Mittagessen.
items.sentence_translation: I'm drinking a cold cola with lunch.
items.grammar_tip: Often used as feminine 'die Cola'.

items.sentence_de: Die Tram fährt alle zehn Minuten zum Zentrum.
items.sentence_translation: The tram runs every ten minutes to the center.
items.grammar_tip: Short for 'Straßenbahn'.

items.sentence_de: Am Dienstag habe ich keinen Termin frei.
items.sentence_translation: On Tuesday I have no free appointments.
items.grammar_tip: All days of the week are masculine.

items.sentence_de: Diese Tasche hier gehört meiner netten Kollegin.
items.sentence_translation: This bag here belongs to my nice colleague.
items.grammar_tip: Demonstrative pronoun; form changes with gender/case.

items.sentence_de: Was ist das für ein komisches Ding?
items.sentence_translation: What kind of strange thing is that?
items.grammar_tip: Generic term for objects.

items.sentence_de: Das Hotel liegt direkt neben dem großen Bahnhof.
items.sentence_translation: The hotel is located right next to the large station.
items.grammar_tip: Used here as an adverb of place.

items.sentence_de: Der Mann möchte das große Orchester dirigieren.
items.sentence_translation: The man wants to conduct the large orchestra.
items.grammar_tip: Refers specifically to leading a musical group.

items.sentence_de: Wir diskutieren oft über Politik.
items.sentence_translation: We often discuss politics.
items.grammar_tip: This is a regular weak verb ending in -ieren.

items.sentence_de: Kommst du nicht? Doch, ich komme!
items.sentence_translation: Aren't you coming? Yes (on the contrary), I am coming!
items.grammar_tip: 'Doch' is used to answer a negative question with 'yes'.

items.sentence_de: Der Doktor untersucht den Patienten heute.
items.sentence_translation: The doctor is examining the patient today.
items.grammar_tip: Masculine professions in German usually take the 'der' article.

items.sentence_de: Die Doktorin arbeitet im großen Krankenhaus.
items.sentence_translation: The doctor works in the big hospital.
items.grammar_tip: Add -in to the masculine form to make a profession feminine.

items.sentence_de: Ich esse einen Döner zum Mittagessen.
items.sentence_translation: I am eating a kebab for lunch.
items.grammar_tip: The plural of 'Döner' is also 'Döner'.

items.sentence_de: Am Donnerstag habe ich einen Termin.
items.sentence_translation: On Thursday I have an appointment.
items.grammar_tip: All days of the week are masculine and take 'der'.

items.sentence_de: Das Wetter heute ist wirklich doof.
items.sentence_translation: The weather today is really stupid/bad.
items.grammar_tip: 'Doof' is a common colloquial word for 'silly' or 'lame'.

items.sentence_de: Ich brauche ein Zimmer mit Doppelbett.
items.sentence_translation: I need a room with a double bed.
items.grammar_tip: Often used when talking about quantities or sizes.

items.sentence_de: Meine Eltern leben in einem Dorf.
items.sentence_translation: My parents live in a village.
items.grammar_tip: Neuter nouns like 'das Dorf' add -er for the plural (Dörfer).

items.sentence_de: Dort steht mein altes Fahrrad.
items.sentence_translation: There stands my old bicycle.
items.grammar_tip: 'Dort' indicates a location further away than 'hier'.

items.sentence_de: Eine Dose Tomaten kostet einen Euro.
items.sentence_translation: A can of tomatoes costs one euro.
items.grammar_tip: Feminine nouns ending in -e usually add -n for the plural.

items.sentence_de: Das Kino zeigt heute ein Double Feature.
items.sentence_translation: The cinema is showing a double feature today.
items.grammar_tip: Many English film terms are used as neuter nouns in German.

items.sentence_de: Wann werde ich endlich im Kurs drankommen?
items.sentence_translation: When will I finally have my turn in the course?
items.grammar_tip: This is a separable verb (dran + kommen).

items.sentence_de: Ich trinke dreimal am Tag Wasser.
items.sentence_translation: I drink water three times a day.
items.grammar_tip: Combine a number with '-mal' to express frequency.

items.sentence_de: Meine Schwester ist jetzt dreißig Jahre alt.
items.sentence_translation: My sister is now thirty years old.
items.grammar_tip: Remember: dreißig is the only tens number using 'ß'.

items.sentence_de: Das Kind ist heute dreizehn geworden.
items.sentence_translation: The child turned thirteen today.
items.grammar_tip: German numbers 13-19 end in '-zehn'.

items.sentence_de: Wir arbeiten heute zu dritt zusammen.
items.sentence_translation: We are working in threes today.
items.grammar_tip: 'Zu dritt' means 'as a group of three people'.

items.sentence_de: Im Winter wird es sehr früh dunkel.
items.sentence_translation: In winter it gets dark very early.
items.grammar_tip: 'Dunkel' is the opposite of 'hell' (light/bright).

items.sentence_de: Haben Sie eine direkte Durchwahl für mich?
items.sentence_translation: Do you have a direct extension for me?
items.grammar_tip: This refers to a telephone extension number.

items.sentence_de: Hier darf man nicht im Park rauchen.
items.sentence_translation: One is not allowed to smoke here in the park.
items.grammar_tip: This is a modal verb expressing permission.

items.sentence_de: Ich dusche jeden Morgen nach dem Sport.
items.sentence_translation: I shower every morning after sports.
items.grammar_tip: A regular weak verb.

items.sentence_de: Ich brauche neues Duschgel für den Urlaub.
items.sentence_translation: I need new shower gel for the vacation.
items.grammar_tip: Compound noun: das Duschen + das Gel = das Duschgel.

items.sentence_de: Wie ist deine aktuelle E-Mail-Adresse bitte?
items.sentence_translation: What is your current email address please?
items.grammar_tip: Usually abbreviated as E-Mail. It is always feminine.

items.sentence_de: Ich wünsche dir einen ebenso schönen Tag.
items.sentence_translation: I wish you an equally nice day.
items.grammar_tip: 'Ebenso' is a synonym for 'ebenfalls' or 'genauso'.

items.sentence_de: Das war ein echt langer Tag heute.
items.sentence_translation: That was a really long day today.
items.grammar_tip: Used for emphasis, similar to 'wirklich'.

items.sentence_de: Es ist mir egal, was wir essen.
items.sentence_translation: I don't care what we eat.
items.grammar_tip: 'Das ist mir egal' is the standard way to say 'I don't care'.

items.sentence_de: Seine Ehefrau kommt aus der Schweiz.
items.sentence_translation: His wife comes from Switzerland.
items.grammar_tip: 'Frau' is often used alone, but 'Ehefrau' is more formal.

items.sentence_de: Mein Ehemann arbeitet als Lehrer in Berlin.
items.sentence_translation: My husband works as a teacher in Berlin.
items.grammar_tip: The plural of 'Mann' is 'Männer'.

items.sentence_de: Ich möchte mein eigenes Haus bauen.
items.sentence_translation: I want to build my own house.
items.grammar_tip: The adjective 'eigen-' takes endings based on the noun it describes.

items.sentence_de: Was machen wir eigentlich heute Abend?
items.sentence_translation: What are we actually doing this evening?
items.grammar_tip: A common filler word used to focus on the real point.

items.sentence_de: Ein Anruf bei meiner Mutter dauert lange.
items.sentence_translation: A phone call to my mother takes a long time.
items.grammar_tip: 'Anruf' is derived from the verb 'anrufen'.

items.sentence_de: Ich spreche nur ein bisschen Deutsch.
items.sentence_translation: I only speak a little German.
items.grammar_tip: Always used together to mean 'a small amount'.

items.sentence_de: Ich kaufe ein paar Äpfel im Supermarkt.
items.sentence_translation: I am buying a few apples at the supermarket.
items.grammar_tip: When 'paar' is lowercase, it means 'some/a few'.

items.sentence_de: Hier ist ein Apfel für dich.
items.sentence_translation: Here is an apple for you.
items.grammar_tip: This is the indefinite article for masculine and neuter nouns.

items.sentence_de: Ich habe eine große Überraschung für dich.
items.sentence_translation: I have a big surprise for you.
items.grammar_tip: The suffix -ung always makes a noun feminine (die).

items.sentence_de: Mir fällt gerade kein Name ein.
items.sentence_translation: I can't think of a name right now.
items.grammar_tip: This verb is separable and takes the dative (mir).

items.sentence_de: Bitte geben Sie Ihr Passwort ein.
items.sentence_translation: Please enter your password.
items.grammar_tip: Separable verb: ein + geben. Used for data entry.

items.sentence_de: Das Ticket kostet genau einhundert Euro.
items.sentence_translation: The ticket costs exactly one hundred euros.
items.grammar_tip: You can say 'hundert' or 'einhundert'.

items.sentence_de: Der Einkauf dauert heute besonders lange.
items.sentence_translation: The shopping is taking especially long today.
items.grammar_tip: Refers to the act or the items bought.

items.sentence_de: Wir gehen am Samstag zusammen einkaufen.
items.sentence_translation: We are going shopping together on Saturday.
items.grammar_tip: 'Einkaufen' is for groceries/necessities; 'bummeln' is for browsing.

items.sentence_de: Einkaufen im Supermarkt macht mir Spaß.
items.sentence_translation: Shopping at the supermarket is fun for me.
items.grammar_tip: Verbs can be turned into neuter nouns by capitalizing them.

items.sentence_de: Der Einkaufswagen ist schon fast voll.
items.sentence_translation: The shopping cart is already almost full.
items.grammar_tip: A compound of Einkauf + Wagen.

items.sentence_de: Ich habe den Einkaufszettel zu Hause vergessen.
items.sentence_translation: I forgot the grocery list at home.
items.grammar_tip: Plural is same as singular: die Einkaufszettel.

items.sentence_de: Ich möchte dich zu meiner Party einladen.
items.sentence_translation: I would like to invite you to my party.
items.grammar_tip: A separable verb: ich lade ... ein.

items.sentence_de: Hast du meine Einladungs-Mail schon bekommen?
items.sentence_translation: Have you received my invitation email yet?
items.grammar_tip: Feminine because 'die Mail' is feminine.

items.sentence_de: Ich muss noch meine Koffer einpacken.
items.sentence_translation: I still have to pack my suitcases.
items.grammar_tip: Opposite of 'auspacken' (to unpack).

items.sentence_de: Der Lehrer möchte die Tests einsammeln.
items.sentence_translation: The teacher wants to collect the tests.
items.grammar_tip: Separable verb: ein + sammeln.

items.sentence_de: Ich kann abends oft nicht einschlafen.
items.sentence_translation: I often cannot fall asleep in the evenings.
items.grammar_tip: The past tense uses 'sein' because it's a change of state.

items.sentence_de: Alle Passagiere müssen jetzt in den Bus einsteigen.
items.sentence_translation: All passengers must board the bus now.
items.grammar_tip: Used for entering a vehicle. Separable.

items.sentence_de: Das Fahrrad kostet genau eintausend Euro.
items.sentence_translation: The bicycle costs exactly one thousand euros.
items.grammar_tip: 'Tausend' is also acceptable without 'ein-'.

items.sentence_de: Es gibt einen neuen Eintrag im Kalender.
items.sentence_translation: There is a new entry in the calendar.
