items.grammar_tip: Used for notes in a book, calendar, or blog.

items.sentence_de: Kommst du zu meiner Einweihungsfeier am Samstag?
items.sentence_translation: Are you coming to my housewarming party on Saturday?
items.grammar_tip: Compound: Einweihung + Feier.

items.sentence_de: Ich möchte bitte zwei Kugeln Eis.
items.sentence_translation: I would like two scoops of ice cream, please.
items.grammar_tip: 'Eis' can mean ice or ice cream.

items.sentence_de: Sie trägt heute ein sehr elegantes Kleid.
items.sentence_translation: She is wearing a very elegant dress today.
items.grammar_tip: Often used to describe formal clothing.

items.sentence_de: Der Elektriker repariert die Lampe im Flur.
items.sentence_translation: The electrician is repairing the lamp in the hallway.
items.grammar_tip: The plural form is the same as the singular.

items.sentence_de: Meine Schwester ist eine sehr gute Elektrikerin.
items.sentence_translation: My sister is a very good electrician.
items.grammar_tip: Feminine version of 'Elektriker'.

items.sentence_de: Welches Elektrogerät brauchen wir in der Küche?
items.sentence_translation: Which electronic device do we need in the kitchen?
items.grammar_tip: A general term for gadgets like mixers or toasters.

items.sentence_de: Ich kaufe ein Stück Emmentaler zum Frühstück.
items.sentence_translation: I am buying a piece of Emmentaler for breakfast.
items.grammar_tip: A specific type of Swiss cheese.

items.sentence_de: Wer ist die Empfängerin von diesem Paket?
items.sentence_translation: Who is the recipient of this package?
items.grammar_tip: From the verb 'empfangen' (to receive).

items.sentence_de: Können Sie mir einen guten Wein empfehlen?
items.sentence_translation: Can you recommend a good wine to me?
items.grammar_tip: Irregular verb: er empfiehlt.

items.sentence_de: Ich habe die schwere Prüfung endlich bestanden.
items.sentence_translation: I finally passed the difficult exam.
items.grammar_tip: Expresses relief that something has happened.

items.sentence_de: Achten Sie auf die richtige Endung beim Verb.
items.sentence_translation: Pay attention to the correct ending on the verb.
items.grammar_tip: Refers to grammatical suffixes.

items.sentence_de: Die Hose ist mir leider zu eng.
items.sentence_translation: Unfortunately, the pants are too tight for me.
items.grammar_tip: Opposite of 'weit' (wide/loose).

items.sentence_de: In der Schule lernen wir alle Englisch.
items.sentence_translation: At school, we all learn English.
items.grammar_tip: Languages in German are usually neuter (das Englisch).

items.sentence_de: Morgen schreiben wir einen wichtigen Englisch-Test.
items.sentence_translation: Tomorrow we are writing an important English test.
items.grammar_tip: Compound noun: Language + Test.

items.sentence_de: Wir entdecken viele neue Cafés in Berlin.
items.sentence_translation: We are discovering many new cafes in Berlin.
items.grammar_tip: The prefix 'ent-' is inseparable.

items.sentence_de: Das war eine sehr schwere Entscheidung heute.
items.sentence_translation: That was a very difficult decision today.
items.grammar_tip: Takes the verb 'treffen' (to make a decision).

items.sentence_de: Die Wohnung liegt unten im Erdgeschoss.
items.sentence_translation: The apartment is located downstairs on the ground floor.
items.grammar_tip: In Germany, the first floor is above the 'Erdgeschoss'.

items.sentence_de: Das Konzert war ein tolles Ereignis.
items.sentence_translation: The concert was a great event.
items.grammar_tip: Neuter noun ending in -nis, plural is -nisse.

items.sentence_de: Das Internet ist eine sehr wichtige Erfindung.
items.sentence_translation: The internet is a very important invention.
items.grammar_tip: Noun from the verb 'erfinden'.

items.sentence_de: Bitte ergänzen Sie die fehlenden Wörter hier.
items.sentence_translation: Please fill in the missing words here.
items.grammar_tip: Common instruction in German exercises.

items.sentence_de: Ich bin leider krank und stark erkältet.
items.sentence_translation: Unfortunately, I am sick and have a bad cold.
items.grammar_tip: Used with the verb 'sein' (ich bin erkältet).

items.sentence_de: Hast du die Erlaubnis vom Chef bekommen?
items.sentence_translation: Did you get the permission from the boss?
items.grammar_tip: Derived from 'erlauben' (to allow).

items.sentence_de: Parken ist hier vor dem Haus erlaubt.
items.sentence_translation: Parking is allowed here in front of the house.
items.grammar_tip: Opposite of 'verboten' (forbidden).

items.sentence_de: Man kann die Bedeutung aus dem Text erschließen.
items.sentence_translation: One can deduce the meaning from the text.
items.grammar_tip: Inseparable verb with 'er-'.

items.sentence_de: Es ist erst acht Uhr am Morgen.
items.sentence_translation: It is only eight o'clock in the morning.
items.grammar_tip: In time contexts, 'erst' means it is earlier than expected.

items.sentence_de: Der erste Tag im Urlaub war toll.
items.sentence_translation: The first day on holiday was great.
items.grammar_tip: Ordinal numbers take adjective endings based on the noun's gender.

items.sentence_de: Der Erzieher spielt mit den Kindern draußen.
items.sentence_translation: The kindergarten teacher is playing with the children outside.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns for male professions in German often end in -er.

items.sentence_de: Die Erzieherin arbeitet in einem großen Kindergarten.
items.sentence_translation: The kindergarten teacher works in a large kindergarten.
items.grammar_tip: Add -in to the masculine profession to make it feminine.

items.sentence_de: Er isst jeden Tag einen Apfel.
items.sentence_translation: He eats an apple every day.
items.grammar_tip: 'Essen' is an irregular verb: the 'e' changes to 'i' for 'du' and 'er/sie/es'.

items.sentence_de: Ich brauche Öl und Essig für den Salat.
items.sentence_translation: I need oil and vinegar for the salad.
items.grammar_tip: 'Essig' is masculine: der Essig.

items.sentence_de: Möchten Sie noch etwas zum Essen bestellen?
items.sentence_translation: Would you like to order anything else to eat?
items.grammar_tip: 'Etwas' is used for an unspecified amount or thing.

items.sentence_de: Ist das euer Haus in Berlin?
items.sentence_translation: Is that your house in Berlin?
items.grammar_tip: 'Euer' is the possessive pronoun for plural 'ihr' (you all).

items.sentence_de: Das Buch kostet genau fünfzehn Euro.
items.sentence_translation: The book costs exactly fifteen euros.
items.grammar_tip: The word 'Euro' usually stays singular after numbers.

items.sentence_de: Das Event findet am Samstagabend statt.
items.sentence_translation: The event is taking place on Saturday evening.
items.grammar_tip: Modern German often uses English loanwords for cultural happenings.

items.sentence_de: Gibt es heute gute Events in Hamburg?
items.sentence_translation: Are there any good events in Hamburg today?
items.grammar_tip: The preposition 'in' describes a location.

items.sentence_de: Das Experiment in der Schule war interessant.
items.sentence_translation: The experiment at school was interesting.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -ment are usually neuter.

items.sentence_de: Dieser Service kostet eine Extra-Gebühr.
items.sentence_translation: This service costs an extra fee.
items.grammar_tip: Used as a prefix to indicate something additional.

items.sentence_de: Das alte Fachwerkhaus steht im Stadtzentrum.
items.sentence_translation: The old half-timbered house is in the city center.
items.grammar_tip: This is a compound noun: Fachwerk + Haus.

items.sentence_de: Er fährt jeden Morgen mit dem Zug.
items.sentence_translation: He travels by train every morning.
items.grammar_tip: 'Fahren' is for transport; it changes 'a' to 'ä' for 'du' and 'er/sie/es'.

items.sentence_de: Ich fahre mit dem Fahrrad zur Arbeit.
items.sentence_translation: I go to work by bicycle.
items.grammar_tip: Remember: 'mit dem Fahrrad' (dative case).

items.sentence_de: Wir machen am Sonntag eine lange Fahrradtour.
items.sentence_translation: We are doing a long bike ride on Sunday.
items.grammar_tip: 'Tour' is feminine, so the whole compound is feminine.

items.sentence_de: Ich koordiniere meine Familie und Termine gut.
items.sentence_translation: I coordinate my family and appointments well.
items.grammar_tip: Plural of Termin is Termine.

items.sentence_de: Das ist ein schönes Familienfoto von uns.
items.sentence_translation: That is a beautiful family photograph of us.
items.grammar_tip: German connects nouns often with an 'n' or 's' (Fugenelement).

items.sentence_de: Kinder haben oft sehr viel Fantasie.
items.sentence_translation: Children often have a lot of imagination.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -ie are usually feminine.

items.sentence_de: Heute bin ich müde und ein bisschen faul.
items.sentence_translation: Today I am tired and a bit lazy.
items.grammar_tip: The opposite of 'faul' is 'fleißig'.

items.sentence_de: Der Februar ist oft der kälteste Monat.
items.sentence_translation: February is often the coldest month.
items.grammar_tip: All months in German are masculine (der).

items.sentence_de: Bitte ergänzen Sie die fehlenden Wörter.
items.sentence_translation: Please fill in the missing words.
items.grammar_tip: This is a present participle used as an adjective.

items.sentence_de: Die Feier zum Geburtstag war sehr lustig.
items.sentence_translation: The birthday celebration was very fun.
items.grammar_tip: 'Feier' is feminine: die Feier.

items.sentence_de: Ich habe um 17 Uhr endlich Feierabend.
items.sentence_translation: I finally finish work at 5 p.m.
items.grammar_tip: 'Feierabend machen' means to finish work for the day.

items.sentence_de: Das Wort 'Sonne' ist im Deutschen feminin.
items.sentence_translation: The word 'Sonne' is feminine in German.
items.grammar_tip: In grammar, nouns have a gender (Genus).

items.sentence_de: Bitte mach das Fenster im Wohnzimmer zu.
items.sentence_translation: Please close the window in the living room.
items.grammar_tip: 'Das Fenster' is neuter.

items.sentence_de: Abends möchte ich nur ein bisschen fernsehen.
items.sentence_translation: In the evening I just want to watch some TV.
items.grammar_tip: This is a separable verb: Ich sehe fern.

items.sentence_de: Unser neuer Fernseher hat ein großes Bild.
items.sentence_translation: Our new television has a large screen.
items.grammar_tip: The device is 'der Fernseher'; the activity is 'fernsehen'.

items.sentence_de: Er arbeitet bei einer großen Fernsehproduktion.
items.sentence_translation: He works for a large TV production.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -ion are always feminine.

items.sentence_de: Wir feiern jedes Jahr ein großes Fest.
items.sentence_translation: We celebrate a big festival every year.
items.grammar_tip: 'Das Fest' is a generic word for celebration/party.

items.sentence_de: Das Musik-Festival findet im Sommer statt.
items.sentence_translation: The music festival takes place in summer.
items.grammar_tip: The plural is 'Festivals'.

items.sentence_de: Die Festspiele in Salzburg sind weltberühmt.
items.sentence_translation: The festival productions in Salzburg are world-famous.
items.grammar_tip: Often used in the plural 'Festspiele' for arts festivals.

items.sentence_de: Dieses Fleisch hat leider sehr viel Fett.
items.sentence_translation: This meat unfortunately has a lot of fat.
items.grammar_tip: 'Das Fett' is neuter.

items.sentence_de: Als Filmfan gehe ich oft ins Kino.
items.sentence_translation: As a film fan, I often go to the cinema.
items.grammar_tip: Compound noun: Film + Fan.

items.sentence_de: Die Filmproduktion sucht neue Schauspieler für Berlin.
items.sentence_translation: The film production is looking for new actors for Berlin.
items.grammar_tip: Ends in -ion, so it is feminine.

items.sentence_de: Wie finden Sie den neuen Film?
items.sentence_translation: How do you find (what do you think of) the new film?
items.grammar_tip: 'Finden' can mean 'to locate' or 'to have an opinion'.

items.sentence_de: Ich habe mir in den Finger geschnitten.
items.sentence_translation: I cut my finger.
items.grammar_tip: The plural is identical to the singular: 'die Finger'.

items.sentence_de: Meine Firma hat das Büro in München.
items.sentence_translation: My company has its office in Munich.
items.grammar_tip: The plural 'Firmen' is very common in business.

items.sentence_de: Das Fischgericht schmeckt in diesem Restaurant hervorragend.
items.sentence_translation: The fish dish tastes excellent in this restaurant.
items.grammar_tip: Neuter noun: 'das Gericht'.

items.sentence_de: Ich mache Sport, um fit zu bleiben.
items.sentence_translation: I do sports to stay fit.
items.grammar_tip: 'Fit' is used exactly like in English.

items.sentence_de: Welche Fitness-App nutzt du für das Training?
items.sentence_translation: Which fitness app do you use for training?
items.grammar_tip: App is short for Applikation and is feminine.

items.sentence_de: Ich gehe dreimal pro Woche ins Fitnessstudio.
items.sentence_translation: I go to the gym three times a week.
items.grammar_tip: Contraction: 'ins' = in + das.

items.sentence_de: Dieses Fitnessgerät ist sehr einfach zu bedienen.
items.sentence_translation: This piece of fitness equipment is very easy to use.
items.grammar_tip: 'Gerät' is neuter.

items.sentence_de: Die Marke eröffnet einen neuen Flagship-Store.
items.sentence_translation: The brand is opening a new flagship store.
items.grammar_tip: English loanword, usually masculine.

items.sentence_de: Die Schüler in dieser Klasse sind sehr fleißig.
items.sentence_translation: The students in this class are very hardworking.
items.grammar_tip: The opposite of 'faul'.

items.sentence_de: Wir fliegen nächsten Monat nach Spanien.
items.sentence_translation: We are flying to Spain next month.
items.grammar_tip: The perfect tense uses 'sein': 'ist geflogen'.

items.sentence_de: Der Flug nach London dauert zwei Stunden.
items.sentence_translation: The flight to London takes two hours.
items.grammar_tip: Masculine: der Flug.

items.sentence_de: Die Schuhe stehen im Flur neben der Tür.
items.sentence_translation: The shoes are in the hallway next to the door.
items.grammar_tip: 'Im Flur' = in + dem (dative).

items.sentence_de: Die Elbe ist ein sehr langer Fluss.
items.sentence_translation: The Elbe is a very long river.
items.grammar_tip: Masculine: der Fluss.

items.sentence_de: Der Tisch hat eine runde Form.
items.sentence_translation: The table has a round shape.
items.grammar_tip: 'Die Form' is feminine.

items.sentence_de: In einem Brief ist die Anrede formell.
items.sentence_translation: In a letter, the greeting is formal.
items.grammar_tip: Opposite of 'informell'.

items.sentence_de: Können Sie den Satz bitte anders formulieren?
items.sentence_translation: Can you please phrase the sentence differently?
items.grammar_tip: Verbs ending in -ieren don't use 'ge-' in the past participle.

items.sentence_de: Ich habe einen interessanten Forumsbeitrag gelesen.
items.sentence_translation: I read an interesting forum post.
items.grammar_tip: Masculine: der Beitrag.

items.sentence_de: Der Fotograf macht Fotos für die Zeitung.
items.sentence_translation: The photographer takes photos for the newspaper.
items.grammar_tip: Masculine noun for a profession.

items.sentence_de: Im Urlaub möchte ich viel fotografieren.
items.sentence_translation: On vacation I want to take a lot of photos.
items.grammar_tip: Common verb for hobbies.

items.sentence_de: Die Fotografin arbeitet in ihrem eigenen Studio.
items.sentence_translation: The photographer works in her own studio.
items.grammar_tip: Feminine form of Fotograf.

items.sentence_de: Er kauft neues Fotozubehör für seine Kamera.
items.sentence_translation: He is buying new photographic accessories for his camera.
items.grammar_tip: 'Zubehör' is a collective noun and usually neuter.

items.sentence_de: 'Wer' ist ein wichtiges Fragewort im Deutschen.
items.sentence_translation: 'Who' is an important interrogative word in German.
items.grammar_tip: Words like wer, wie, was, wo are Fragewörter.

items.sentence_de: In der Schweiz zahlt man mit Franken.
items.sentence_translation: In Switzerland one pays with francs.
items.grammar_tip: Official currency of Switzerland and Liechtenstein.

items.sentence_de: Paris ist die Hauptstadt von Frankreich.
items.sentence_translation: Paris is the capital of France.
items.grammar_tip: Most countries in German don't have an article.

items.sentence_de: Ich lerne seit zwei Jahren Französisch.
items.sentence_translation: I have been learning French for two years.
items.grammar_tip: Languages are usually neuter but used without articles.

items.sentence_de: Morgen muss ich nicht arbeiten, ich habe frei.
items.sentence_translation: I don't have to work tomorrow, I have the day off.
items.grammar_tip: 'Freihaben' refers to time away from work or school.

items.sentence_de: Am Freitag gehen wir oft ins Kino.
items.sentence_translation: On Friday we often go to the cinema.
items.grammar_tip: All days of the week are masculine (der).

items.sentence_de: Was ist deine liebste Freizeitaktivität?
items.sentence_translation: What is your favorite leisure activity?
items.grammar_tip: Compound: Freizeit + Aktivität.

items.sentence_de: Am Wochenende trage ich am liebsten Freizeitkleidung.
items.sentence_translation: On the weekend I like wearing leisure clothes most.
items.grammar_tip: 'Kleidung' is a singular collective noun in German.

items.sentence_de: Ich freue mich auf die Party am Samstag.
items.sentence_translation: I am looking forward to the party on Saturday.
items.grammar_tip: Reflexive verb: sich freuen.

items.sentence_de: Meine Freundin kommt heute zu Besuch.
items.sentence_translation: My (female) friend/girlfriend is coming to visit today.
items.grammar_tip: Can mean a female friend or a romantic girlfriend.

items.sentence_de: Die Verkäuferin im Laden ist sehr freundlich.
items.sentence_translation: The shop assistant in the store is very friendly.
items.grammar_tip: Derived from 'Freund'.

items.sentence_de: Mit freundlichen Grüßen, Ihr Max Müller.
items.sentence_translation: Sincerely, your Max Müller.
items.grammar_tip: Standard formal closing for German letters/emails.

items.sentence_de: Ich kaufe auf dem Markt frisches Gemüse.
items.sentence_translation: I buy fresh vegetables at the market.
items.grammar_tip: Commonly used for food items.

items.sentence_de: Der Friseur schneidet mir die Haare.
items.sentence_translation: The hairdresser is cutting my hair.
items.grammar_tip: Masculine: der Friseur.

items.sentence_de: Ich habe einen Termin bei meiner Friseurin.
items.sentence_translation: I have an appointment with my hairdresser.
items.grammar_tip: Feminine: die Friseurin.

items.sentence_de: Ich bin froh, dass du hier bist.
items.sentence_translation: I am glad that you are here.
items.grammar_tip: Synonym for 'glücklich' in many contexts.

items.sentence_de: Ich muss morgen sehr früh aufstehen.
items.sentence_translation: I have to get up very early tomorrow.
items.grammar_tip: Opposite of 'spät'.

items.sentence_de: Im Frühling blühen viele schöne Blumen.
items.sentence_translation: In spring, many beautiful flowers bloom.
items.grammar_tip: German seasons are all masculine (der).

items.sentence_de: Wann gibt es Frühstück, Mittagessen und Abendessen?
items.sentence_translation: When is there breakfast, lunch, and dinner?
items.grammar_tip: These three main meal words in German are all neuter (das).

items.sentence_de: Wir führen heute ein wichtiges Gespräch.
items.sentence_translation: We are having an important conversation today.
items.grammar_tip: The phrase 'ein Gespräch führen' is a common light verb construction.

items.sentence_de: Mein Sohn ist heute fünfzehn Jahre alt.
items.sentence_translation: My son is fifteen years old today.
items.grammar_tip: Numbers like fifteen end in '-zehn', while tens end in '-zig'.

items.sentence_de: Das Ticket kostet genau fünfzig Euro.
items.sentence_translation: The ticket costs exactly fifty Euros.
items.grammar_tip: Remember that '-zig' denotes tens (20, 30, 40, etc.).

items.sentence_de: Mein linker Fuß tut heute weh.
items.sentence_translation: My left foot hurts today.
items.grammar_tip: The plural of 'Fuß' is 'Füße' with an umlaut.

items.sentence_de: Er spielt am Wochenende gern Fußball.
items.sentence_translation: He likes to play football at the weekend.
items.grammar_tip: The verb 'spielen' is used for sports without a preposition.

items.sentence_de: Das Fußballspiel fängt um acht Uhr an.
items.sentence_translation: The football game starts at eight o'clock.
items.grammar_tip: This is a compound noun: der Fußball + das Spiel = das Fußballspiel.

items.sentence_de: Ich brauche bitte eine Gabel zum Essen.
items.sentence_translation: I need a fork to eat, please.
items.grammar_tip: Cutlery items: der Löffel (m), das Messer (n), die Gabel (f).

items.sentence_de: Dieses kleine Gadget ist sehr praktisch.
items.sentence_translation: This small gadget is very practical.
items.grammar_tip: Borrowed English words are often neuter (das) in German.

items.sentence_de: Wie geht es dir? - Ganz gut.
items.sentence_translation: How are you? - Pretty good.
items.grammar_tip: 'Ganz' is often used before adjectives to mean 'quite' or 'fairly'.

items.sentence_de: Das ist gar nicht so teuer.
items.sentence_translation: That is not at all that expensive.
items.grammar_tip: 'Gar nicht' is a common phrase meaning 'not at all'.

items.sentence_de: Der Gast möchte ein Zimmer reservieren.
items.sentence_translation: The guest would like to reserve a room.
items.grammar_tip: The plural 'Gäste' takes an umlaut and an 'e'.

items.sentence_de: Bitte schreiben Sie etwas in unser Gästebuch.
items.sentence_translation: Please write something in our guestbook.
items.grammar_tip: Compound noun: der Gast + das Buch = das Gästebuch.

items.sentence_de: Sie gibt dem Kellner ein Trinkgeld.
items.sentence_translation: She gives the waiter a tip.
items.grammar_tip: The verb 'geben' is irregular: ich gebe, du gibst, er gibt.

items.sentence_de: Ich gebe morgen Unterricht an der Universität.
items.sentence_translation: I am giving lessons at the university tomorrow.
items.grammar_tip: 'Unterricht geben' means to teach a class.

items.sentence_de: Es gibt hier viele schöne Cafés.
items.sentence_translation: There are many beautiful cafes here.
items.grammar_tip: 'Es gibt' always takes the accusative case.

items.sentence_de: Das erste Gebot ist sehr wichtig.
items.sentence_translation: The first commandment is very important.
items.grammar_tip: In modern contexts, this word is also used for a 'bid' in an auction.

items.sentence_de: Schreiben Sie bitte Ihr Geburtsdatum hier.
items.sentence_translation: Please write your date of birth here.
items.grammar_tip: Compound nouns ending in -datum are neuter.

items.sentence_de: Sehr geehrte Damen und Herren, wie geht's?
items.sentence_translation: Dear Sir or Madam, how are things?
items.grammar_tip: 'Sehr geehrte' is the formal opening for letters/emails.

items.sentence_de: Laufen auf der Autobahn ist sehr gefährlich.
items.sentence_translation: Walking on the highway is very dangerous.
items.grammar_tip: Adjectives ending in '-lich' are very common in German.

items.sentence_de: Das Kleid gefällt mir sehr gut.
items.sentence_translation: I like the dress very much (lit: The dress pleases me).
items.grammar_tip: The subject of 'gefallen' is the thing you like; the person is in the dative.

items.sentence_de: Wir müssen uns gegenseitig immer helfen.
items.sentence_translation: We must always help each other.
items.grammar_tip: 'Gegenseitig' describes an interaction between two or more parties.

items.sentence_de: Die Bank liegt direkt gegenüber vom Park.
items.sentence_translation: The bank is located directly across from the park.
items.grammar_tip: 'Gegenüber' is a dative preposition and often follows the noun.

items.translation: Shall we go to the cinema?
items.sentence_de: Gehen wir heute Abend ins Kino?
items.sentence_translation: Are we going to the cinema tonight?
items.grammar_tip: To suggest an activity, use the verb 'gehen' in a question form.

items.sentence_de: Wie geht es dir heute Morgen?
items.sentence_translation: How are you doing this morning?
items.grammar_tip: 'Wie geht es...' is a fixed expression for asking how someone is.

items.sentence_de: Hörst du gern Musik? - Es geht.
items.sentence_translation: Do you like listening to music? - It's okay.
items.grammar_tip: 'Es geht' (so) is a common way to say something is mediocre or 'so-so'.

items.sentence_de: Meine Schwester spielt jeden Tag Geige.
items.sentence_translation: My sister plays the violin every day.
items.grammar_tip: Most musical instruments ending in -e are feminine.

items.sentence_de: Der Geigenunterricht findet am Dienstag statt.
items.sentence_translation: The violin lesson takes place on Tuesday.
items.grammar_tip: Note that Unterricht (lessons/instruction) is masculine.

items.sentence_de: Die Sonne ist heute hell und gelb.
items.sentence_translation: The sun is bright and yellow today.
items.grammar_tip: Basic colors are usually used as indeclinable adjectives after the verb.

items.sentence_de: Unser Wohnzimmer ist sehr warm und gemütlich.
items.sentence_translation: Our living room is very warm and cozy.
items.grammar_tip: 'Gemütlich' is a classic German word for 'cozy'.

items.sentence_de: Ja, genau das habe ich auch gedacht.
items.sentence_translation: Yes, that is exactly what I thought too.
items.grammar_tip: 'Genau' is frequently used to express agreement.

items.sentence_de: Wir genießen das schöne Wetter im Park.
items.sentence_translation: We are enjoying the beautiful weather in the park.
items.grammar_tip: The past participle is 'genossen'.

items.sentence_de: Ich habe leider nicht genug Geld dabei.
items.sentence_translation: Unfortunately, I don't have enough money with me.
items.grammar_tip: 'Genug' usually comes after the adjective but before the noun.

items.sentence_de: Gehen Sie immer geradeaus bis zur Ampel.
items.sentence_translation: Go straight ahead until the traffic light.
items.grammar_tip: 'Geradeaus' is essential for giving directions.

items.sentence_de: Welches Gerät brauchen wir für die Küche?
items.sentence_translation: Which device do we need for the kitchen?
items.grammar_tip: Generic word for an appliance or technical device.

items.sentence_de: Dieses italienische Gericht schmeckt wirklich wunderbar.
items.sentence_translation: This Italian dish tastes really wonderful.
items.grammar_tip: 'Gericht' can mean a meal or a court of law.

items.sentence_de: Ich esse sehr gern Pizza mit Käse.
items.sentence_translation: I like to eat pizza with cheese very much.
items.grammar_tip: In German, you don't 'like to do' something; you 'do it gladly' (gern).

items.sentence_de: Kannst du mir helfen? - Ja, gerne!
items.sentence_translation: Can you help me? - Yes, with pleasure!
items.grammar_tip: 'Gern' and 'gerne' are interchangeable; 'gerne' is often used in replies.

items.sentence_de: Opa erzählt uns oft eine lustige Geschichte.
items.sentence_translation: Grandpa often tells us a funny story.
items.grammar_tip: 'Geschichte' means both 'story' and 'history'.

items.sentence_de: Wer wäscht heute das Geschirr in der Küche?
items.sentence_translation: Who is washing the dishes in the kitchen today?
items.grammar_tip: 'Geschirr' is a collective noun and usually singular.

items.sentence_de: Wasch dir bitte das Gesicht mit Wasser.
items.sentence_translation: Please wash your face with water.
items.grammar_tip: Plural is 'Gesichter'.

items.sentence_de: Das Wetter ist ein beliebtes Gesprächsthema.
items.sentence_translation: The weather is a popular topic of conversation.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -ma often come from Greek and take -men in plural.

items.sentence_de: Obst und Gemüse sind sehr gesund.
items.sentence_translation: Fruit and vegetables are very healthy.
items.grammar_tip: Opposite of 'krank' (sick).

items.sentence_de: Wir möchten bitte getrennt zahlen.
items.sentence_translation: We would like to pay separately, please.
items.grammar_tip: Commonly used when paying at a restaurant.

items.sentence_de: Möchten Sie ein Glas Wasser trinken?
items.sentence_translation: Would you like to drink a glass of water?
items.grammar_tip: Plural is 'Gläser' (with umlaut).

items.sentence_de: Schönes Wochenende! - Danke, gleichfalls!
items.sentence_translation: Have a nice weekend! - Thanks, likewise!
items.grammar_tip: A polite way to return a wish like 'Guten Appetit' or 'Schönen Tag'.

items.sentence_de: Heute sind es nur fünf Grad Celsius.
items.sentence_translation: Today it is only five degrees Celsius.
items.grammar_tip: The unit 'Grad' remains singular after numbers.

items.sentence_de: Ich hätte gern zweihundert Gramm Käse.
items.sentence_translation: I would like two hundred grams of cheese.
items.grammar_tip: Like 'Grad', 'Gramm' usually stays singular after a number.

items.sentence_de: Die deutsche Grammatik ist manchmal etwas schwierig.
items.sentence_translation: German grammar is sometimes a bit difficult.
items.grammar_tip: Most nouns ending in -ik are feminine.

items.sentence_de: Der Himmel ist heute sehr grau.
items.sentence_translation: The sky is very gray today.
items.grammar_tip: Basic color adjective.

items.sentence_de: Wir machen diesen Sommer Urlaub in Griechenland.
items.sentence_translation: We are going on vacation in Greece this summer.
items.grammar_tip: Most country names in German are neuter and used without an article.

items.sentence_de: Kommst du am Samstag zu unserer Grillparty?
items.sentence_translation: Are you coming to our barbecue on Saturday?
items.grammar_tip: Plural is 'Grillpartys' (English-style plural for words ending in y).

items.sentence_de: Grüezi! Wie geht es Ihnen heute?
items.sentence_translation: Hello! How are you today?
items.grammar_tip: This is a traditional greeting used in Switzerland.

items.sentence_de: Das Gras im Garten ist sehr grün.
items.sentence_translation: The grass in the garden is very green.
items.grammar_tip: Basic color adjective.

items.sentence_de: Das ist der Grund für meine Verspätung.
items.sentence_translation: That is the reason for my delay.
items.grammar_tip: The plural is 'Gründe'.

items.sentence_de: Herzliche Grüße aus dem Urlaub in Spanien!
items.sentence_translation: Warm greetings from the vacation in Spain!
items.grammar_tip: The 'ß' changes to 'ss' only in Switzerland; elsewhere it remains 'ß'.

items.sentence_de: Grüß Gott! Kann ich Ihnen helfen?
items.sentence_translation: Hello! Can I help you?
items.grammar_tip: Common greeting in Southern Germany and Austria.

items.sentence_de: Bitte grüßen Sie Ihre Frau von mir.
items.sentence_translation: Please greet your wife for me.
items.grammar_tip: The verb 'grüßen' is regular.

items.sentence_de: Welche Grußformel benutzt man in einem Brief?
items.sentence_translation: Which salutation does one use in a letter?
items.grammar_tip: Examples include 'Mit freundlichen Grüßen'.

items.sentence_de: Ich möchte einen Salat mit einer Gurke.
items.sentence_translation: I would like a salad with a cucumber.
items.grammar_tip: Feminine noun ending in -e.

items.sentence_de: Du bist krank? Dann gute Besserung!
items.sentence_translation: You are sick? Then get well soon!
items.grammar_tip: Standard phrase used when someone is ill.

items.sentence_de: Schlaf gut und gute Nacht, mein Kind.
items.sentence_translation: Sleep well and good night, my child.
items.grammar_tip: Note that it is 'gute Nacht' (feminine) but 'guten Tag' (masculine).

items.sentence_de: Guten Abend, meine Damen und Herren!
items.sentence_translation: Good evening, ladies and gentlemen!
items.grammar_tip: Used after approximately 6 PM.

items.sentence_de: Das Essen ist fertig. Guten Appetit!
items.sentence_translation: The food is ready. Enjoy your meal!
items.grammar_tip: Said before starting a meal.

items.sentence_de: Guten Morgen! Wie haben Sie geschlafen?
items.sentence_translation: Good morning! How did you sleep?
items.grammar_tip: Used early in the day, usually until 10 or 11 AM.

items.sentence_de: Guten Tag, ich suche Herrn Schmidt.
items.sentence_translation: Good day, I am looking for Mr. Schmidt.
items.grammar_tip: The standard formal greeting during the day.

items.sentence_de: Guten Tag! Und auf Wiedersehen bis morgen!
items.sentence_translation: Good day! And goodbye until tomorrow!
items.grammar_tip: 'Auf Wiedersehen' is the standard formal way to say goodbye.

items.sentence_de: Ich habe heute viele Termine im Büro.
items.sentence_translation: I have many appointments in the office today.
items.grammar_tip: 'Haben' is one of the most important auxiliary and main verbs.

items.sentence_de: Ich habe heute sehr lange Deutsch gelernt.
items.sentence_translation: I studied German for a very long time today.
items.grammar_tip: 'Haben' is used as an auxiliary verb to form the Perfekt tense.

items.sentence_de: Das Schiff fährt langsam aus dem Hafen.
items.sentence_translation: The ship is slowly sailing out of the harbor.
items.grammar_tip: Plural is 'Häfen'.

items.sentence_de: Ich frühstücke meistens um halb acht Uhr.
items.sentence_translation: I usually eat breakfast at half past seven.
items.grammar_tip: In German time, 'halb acht' means 7:30 (half way to eight).

items.sentence_de: Ich warte schon eine halbe Stunde hier.
items.sentence_translation: I have been waiting here for half an hour.
items.grammar_tip: 'Stunde' is feminine (die).

items.sentence_de: Er läuft im Herbst einen ganzen Halbmarathon.
items.sentence_translation: He is running a whole half-marathon in the fall.
items.grammar_tip: A marathon is 42.195 km; a 'Halbmarathon' is half that.

items.sentence_de: Hallo! Wie geht es dir? - Tschüs!
items.sentence_translation: Hello! How are you? - Bye!
items.grammar_tip: Informal ways to say hello and goodbye.

items.sentence_de: Mein Hals tut heute sehr weh.
items.sentence_translation: My neck hurts very much today.
items.grammar_tip: The plural is 'Hälse' and it uses the masculine article 'der'.

items.sentence_de: Ich habe seit gestern schlimme Halsschmerzen.
items.sentence_translation: I have had a bad sore throat since yesterday.
items.grammar_tip: This is a plural noun often used with 'haben'.

items.sentence_de: Mein kleiner Hamster schläft den ganzen Tag.
items.sentence_translation: My little hamster sleeps all day.
items.grammar_tip: The plural is the same as the singular: 'die Hamster'.

items.sentence_de: Was hast du in deiner rechten Hand?
items.sentence_translation: What do you have in your right hand?
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -and often have an umlaut in the plural: 'Hände'.

items.sentence_de: Der Händler verkauft Obst auf dem Markt.
items.sentence_translation: The merchant sells fruit at the market.
items.grammar_tip: Occupations ending in -er are typically masculine.

items.sentence_de: Die Händlerin ist heute nicht am Stand.
items.sentence_translation: The female merchant is not at the stall today.
items.grammar_tip: Add -in to the masculine form to create the feminine occupation.

items.sentence_de: Ich habe einen Handschuh im Bus verloren.
items.sentence_translation: I lost a glove on the bus.
items.grammar_tip: This is a compound word: 'Hand' + 'Schuh' (shoe).

items.sentence_de: Sie sucht ihren Schlüssel in der Handtasche.
items.sentence_translation: She is looking for her key in the handbag.
items.grammar_tip: Compound words take the gender of the last word (die Tasche).

items.sentence_de: Das Handtuch liegt im Bad auf dem Boden.
items.sentence_translation: The towel is lying on the floor in the bathroom.
items.grammar_tip: Plural: 'Handtücher'. Remember: Hand + Tuch (cloth).

items.sentence_de: Der Handwerker repariert morgen die kaputte Tür.
items.sentence_translation: The craftsman will repair the broken door tomorrow.
items.grammar_tip: The plural stays 'Handwerker'.

items.sentence_de: Die Handwerkerin streicht die Wände im Wohnzimmer.
items.sentence_translation: The craftswoman is painting the walls in the living room.
items.grammar_tip: Feminine nouns ending in -in take -innen in plural.

items.sentence_de: Mein Handy-Akku ist leider schon wieder leer.
items.sentence_translation: My phone battery is unfortunately empty again.
items.grammar_tip: 'Akku' is short for 'Akkumulator' and is masculine.

items.sentence_de: Wie ist deine neue Handynummer für WhatsApp?
items.sentence_translation: What is your new mobile number for WhatsApp?
items.grammar_tip: Usually asked with 'Wie ist...?' rather than 'Was ist...?'.

items.sentence_de: Ich finde diese gelbe Lampe wirklich hässlich.
items.sentence_translation: I find this yellow lamp really ugly.
items.grammar_tip: The opposite of 'hässlich' is 'schön'.

items.sentence_de: Berlin ist die größte Hauptstadt von Deutschland.
items.sentence_translation: Berlin is the largest capital city of Germany.
items.grammar_tip: Compound: 'Haupt' (main) + 'Stadt' (city).

items.sentence_de: Wir wohnen in einem kleinen Haus am Wald.
items.sentence_translation: We live in a small house by the forest.
items.grammar_tip: Plural: 'Häuser'.

items.sentence_de: Wer macht bei euch zu Hause den Haushalt?
items.sentence_translation: Who does the housework in your home?
items.grammar_tip: 'Den Haushalt machen' means 'to do the housework'.

items.sentence_de: Wo finde ich die Haushaltswaren in diesem Geschäft?
items.sentence_translation: Where do I find the homewares in this shop?
items.grammar_tip: Common department name in department stores.

items.sentence_de: Der Hausmeister hat den Schlüssel für den Keller.
items.sentence_translation: The caretaker has the key for the cellar.
items.grammar_tip: The plural is the same as the singular.

items.sentence_de: Fragen Sie die Hausmeisterin nach dem Paket.
items.sentence_translation: Ask the female caretaker about the package.
items.grammar_tip: Feminine job title.

items.sentence_de: Tee mit Honig ist ein gutes Hausmittel.
items.sentence_translation: Tea with honey is a good home remedy.
items.grammar_tip: Literal: 'House means/agent'.

items.sentence_de: Meine Hausnummer ist die zwölf im Erdgeschoss.
items.sentence_translation: My house number is twelve on the ground floor.
items.grammar_tip: Always 'die' because 'Nummer' is feminine.

items.sentence_de: Schreiben Sie die Sätze bitte in Ihr Heft.
items.sentence_translation: Please write the sentences in your exercise book.
items.grammar_tip: Plural: 'Hefte'.

items.sentence_de: Im Sommer ist es in der Stadt sehr heiß.
items.sentence_translation: In summer, it is very hot in the city.
items.grammar_tip: Don't confuse 'heiß' (temperature) with 'scharf' (spicy).

items.sentence_de: Wie heißen Sie mit Ihrem Nachnamen bitte?
items.sentence_translation: What is your last name, please?
items.grammar_tip: Used for names. 'Ich heiße...' means 'My name is...'.

items.sentence_de: Können Sie mir bitte bei den Hausaufgaben helfen?
items.sentence_translation: Can you please help me with the homework?
items.grammar_tip: The verb 'helfen' always takes the dative case (mir, dir, ihm...).

items.sentence_de: Beim Fahrradfahren sollte man immer einen Helm tragen.
items.sentence_translation: One should always wear a helmet when cycling.
items.grammar_tip: Masculine article: 'der Helm'.

items.sentence_de: Er trägt ein weißes Hemd für die Arbeit.
items.sentence_translation: He is wearing a white shirt for work.
items.grammar_tip: 'Hemd' usually refers to a men's button-up shirt.

items.sentence_de: Das ist schon eine lange Zeit her.
items.sentence_translation: That was a long time ago.
items.grammar_tip: Often used with 'ist' to indicate time passed.

items.sentence_de: Im Herbst werden die Blätter an den Bäumen bunt.
items.sentence_translation: In autumn, the leaves on the trees become colorful.
items.grammar_tip: All seasons in German are masculine ('der').

items.sentence_de: Guten Tag, Herr Müller, wie geht es Ihnen?
items.sentence_translation: Good day, Mr. Müller, how are you?
items.grammar_tip: Used as a formal title for men.

items.sentence_de: Die Herrenmode befindet sich im zweiten Stock.
items.sentence_translation: The men's fashion is located on the second floor.
items.grammar_tip: Compound: 'Herren' + 'Mode'.

items.sentence_de: Herzliche Grüße aus dem Urlaub in Spanien!
items.sentence_translation: Warm greetings from the holiday in Spain!
items.grammar_tip: Often used in letters and card greetings.

items.sentence_de: Hey, wie war dein Wochenende in Berlin?
items.sentence_translation: Hey, how was your weekend in Berlin?
items.grammar_tip: Informal greeting or attention-getter.

items.sentence_de: Hi, hast du heute Abend Zeit für Kino?
items.sentence_translation: Hi, do you have time for the cinema tonight?
items.grammar_tip: Short, informal greeting borrowed from English.

items.sentence_de: Norden ist eine wichtige Himmelsrichtung auf der Karte.
items.sentence_translation: North is an important cardinal direction on the map.
items.grammar_tip: There are four: Nord, Süd, Ost, West.

items.sentence_de: Ich bin müde und möchte mich kurz hinlegen.
items.sentence_translation: I am tired and want to lie down for a moment.
items.grammar_tip: Reflexive verb: 'sich hinlegen'.

items.sentence_de: Das Auto parkt direkt hinter dem großen Haus.
items.sentence_translation: The car is parked directly behind the big house.
items.grammar_tip: A two-way preposition (Wechselpräposition) using Dative or Accusative.

items.sentence_de: Die Hitze im August ist dieses Jahr extrem.
items.sentence_translation: The heat in August is extreme this year.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -e are very often feminine.

items.sentence_de: Ich muss zuerst meinen Computer im Büro hochfahren.
items.sentence_translation: I first have to start up my computer in the office.
items.grammar_tip: Separable verb: 'Ich fahre den Computer hoch'.

items.sentence_de: Sie wohnt im zehnten Stock in einem Hochhaus.
items.sentence_translation: She lives on the tenth floor in a skyscraper.
items.grammar_tip: Literally 'high house'. Plural: 'Hochhäuser'.

items.sentence_de: Die Kinder spielen heute Nachmittag im Hof.
items.sentence_translation: The children are playing in the courtyard this afternoon.
items.grammar_tip: Plural: 'Höfe'.

items.sentence_de: Hoffentlich regnet es morgen bei unserem Ausflug nicht.
items.sentence_translation: Hopefully it doesn't rain tomorrow during our trip.
items.grammar_tip: Expresses a wish or hope.

items.sentence_de: Es ist wichtig, zu anderen Menschen höflich zu sein.
items.sentence_translation: It is important to be polite to other people.
items.grammar_tip: The opposite of 'unhöflich'.

items.sentence_de: Höflichkeit macht das Leben viel einfacher für alle.
items.sentence_translation: Politeness makes life much easier for everyone.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -heit are always feminine.

items.sentence_de: Der Tisch ist aus massivem Holz gebaut.
items.sentence_translation: The table is built from solid wood.
items.grammar_tip: Usually used in the singular when referring to material.

items.sentence_de: Informationen finden Sie auf unserer neuen Homepage.
items.sentence_translation: You can find information on our new homepage.
items.grammar_tip: Borrowed from English; gender is feminine.

items.sentence_de: Ich esse zum Frühstück gerne Brot mit Honig.
items.sentence_translation: I like to eat bread with honey for breakfast.
items.grammar_tip: 'Honig' is masculine: 'der Honig'.

items.sentence_de: Diese blaue Hose passt mir leider nicht.
items.sentence_translation: Unfortunately, these blue trousers don't fit me.
items.grammar_tip: In German, 'Hose' is singular (one pair of pants).

items.sentence_de: Der Hotelchef begrüßt die Gäste an der Rezeption.
items.sentence_translation: The hotel boss greets the guests at the reception.
items.grammar_tip: Compound of 'Hotel' + 'Chef'.

items.sentence_de: Die Hotelchefin organisiert die Feier im Saal.
items.sentence_translation: The female hotel boss organizes the celebration in the hall.
items.grammar_tip: Feminine version of 'Hotelchef'.

items.sentence_de: Eine warme Hühnersuppe hilft gut gegen Erkältung.
items.sentence_translation: A warm chicken soup helps well against a cold.
items.grammar_tip: Compound: 'Hühner' (chickens) + 'Suppe' (soup).

items.sentence_de: Ich habe noch nichts gegessen und bin hungrig.
items.sentence_translation: I haven't eaten anything yet and am hungry.
items.grammar_tip: Opposite of 'satt' (full/satisfied).

items.sentence_de: Hurra, wir haben endlich Urlaub und fahren weg!
items.sentence_translation: Hooray, we finally have vacation and are going away!
items.grammar_tip: Exclamation of joy.

items.sentence_de: Sie muss wegen der kalten Luft viel husten.
items.sentence_translation: She has to cough a lot because of the cold air.
items.grammar_tip: The noun is 'der Husten'.

items.sentence_de: Der Arzt verschreibt mir einen süßen Hustensaft.
items.sentence_translation: The doctor prescribes me a sweet cough syrup.
items.grammar_tip: Compound: 'Husten' + 'Saft' (juice).

items.sentence_de: Er trägt bei der Hochzeit einen schwarzen Hut.
items.sentence_translation: He is wearing a black hat at the wedding.
items.grammar_tip: Plural form has an umlaut: 'Hüte'.

items.sentence_de: Mein Schrank ist leer, ich brauche neue Kleidung!
items.sentence_translation: My wardrobe is empty, I need new clothes!
items.grammar_tip: 'Kleidung' is a collective noun and usually singular.

items.sentence_de: Das Wetter heute ist ideal für ein Picknick.
items.sentence_translation: The weather today is ideal for a picnic.
items.grammar_tip: Used to describe something perfect for a purpose.

items.sentence_de: Ich habe eine gute Idee für unser Projekt.
items.sentence_translation: I have a good idea for our project.
items.grammar_tip: Plural: 'Ideen'. Gender: feminine.

items.sentence_de: Wie geht es Ihnen heute Morgen, Frau Schmidt?
items.sentence_translation: How are you this morning, Mrs. Schmidt?
items.grammar_tip: Always capitalized when used as the formal 'you'.

items.sentence_de: Wo ist Ihre Tasche, Frau Müller?
items.sentence_translation: Where is your bag, Mrs. Müller?
items.grammar_tip: The possessive pronoun for formal 'Sie'.

items.sentence_de: Ich trainiere dreimal pro Woche im Fitness-Studio.
items.sentence_translation: I work out three times a week at the gym.
items.grammar_tip: 'im' is a contraction of 'in' + 'dem'.

items.sentence_de: Man kann im Kaufhaus fast alles kaufen.
items.sentence_translation: You can buy almost everything in the department store.
items.grammar_tip: 'Kaufhaus' is neuter: 'das Kaufhaus'.

items.sentence_de: Wir essen heute Abend im Restaurant zu Mittag.
items.sentence_translation: We are eating lunch at the restaurant this evening.
items.grammar_tip: Contraction: in + dem Restaurant.

items.sentence_de: Es regnet schon wieder. Immer dieses Wetter!
items.sentence_translation: It's raining again. Always this weather!
items.grammar_tip: A common colloquial expression of frustration.

items.sentence_de: Der Imperativ wird für Befehle oder Bitten genutzt.
items.sentence_translation: The imperative is used for commands or requests.
items.grammar_tip: Grammar term for command forms like 'Geh!' or 'Kommen Sie!'.

items.sentence_de: Er ist ein Individualist und arbeitet lieber allein.
items.sentence_translation: He is an individualist and prefers to work alone.
items.grammar_tip: Refers to someone who acts independently.

items.sentence_de: Als Individualistin geht sie ihren eigenen Weg.
items.sentence_translation: As an individualist, she goes her own way.
items.grammar_tip: Feminine version of 'Individualist'.

items.sentence_de: Wir suchen eine individuelle Lösung für Ihr Problem.
items.sentence_translation: We are looking for an individual solution to your problem.
items.grammar_tip: Means unique or tailored to a person.

items.sentence_de: Sprechen Sie Indonesisch oder nur Englisch und Deutsch?
items.sentence_translation: Do you speak Indonesian or only English and German?
items.grammar_tip: Languages in German are usually neuter but used without an article.

items.sentence_de: 'Gehen' ist der Infinitiv von 'ich gehe'.
items.sentence_translation: 'Gehen' is the infinitive of 'I go'.
items.grammar_tip: The basic dictionary form of a verb.

items.sentence_de: Mein Bruder arbeitet als Informatiker bei Siemens.
items.sentence_translation: My brother works as a computer scientist at Siemens.
items.grammar_tip: The plural is identical to the singular.

items.sentence_de: Sie ist eine sehr erfolgreiche Informatikerin in Berlin.
items.sentence_translation: She is a very successful computer scientist in Berlin.
items.grammar_tip: Feminine form of the profession.

items.sentence_de: In der Familie sprechen wir meistens sehr informell.
items.sentence_translation: In the family, we usually speak very informally.
items.grammar_tip: The opposite of 'formell'. Used with 'du'.

items.sentence_de: Der Infotext ist sehr lang und schwer.
items.sentence_translation: The informational text is very long and difficult.
items.grammar_tip: German compound nouns like 'Infotext' take the gender of the last word (der Text).

items.sentence_de: Mein Bruder arbeitet als Ingenieur bei BMW.
items.sentence_translation: My brother works as an engineer at BMW.
items.grammar_tip: Professional titles for men usually have no suffix, while women's titles end in -in.

items.sentence_de: Sie ist eine sehr erfolgreiche Ingenieurin.
items.sentence_translation: She is a very successful engineer.
items.grammar_tip: Most female professions in German end with the suffix '-in'.

items.sentence_de: Ich muss heute gegen den Schnupfen inhalieren.
items.sentence_translation: I have to inhale today against the cold.
items.grammar_tip: Verbs ending in '-ieren' do not take 'ge-' in the past participle (Partizip II).

items.sentence_de: Das ist ein inoffiziell Treffen der Gruppe.
items.sentence_translation: That is an unofficial meeting of the group.
items.grammar_tip: The prefix 'in-' often negates the meaning of an adjective.

items.sentence_de: Wir machen Urlaub auf einer kleinen Insel.
items.sentence_translation: We are going on vacation on a small island.
items.grammar_tip: Use 'auf' when talking about being on an island.

items.sentence_de: Das macht insgesamt zwanzig Euro bitte.
items.sentence_translation: That makes twenty euros all together please.
items.grammar_tip: 'Insgesamt' is often used when summing up prices or quantities.

items.sentence_de: Das Buch ist wirklich sehr interessant.
items.sentence_translation: The book is really very interesting.
items.grammar_tip: The opposite of 'interessant' is 'langweilig' (boring).

items.sentence_de: Die Nachrichten interessieren mich heute nicht.
items.sentence_translation: The news doesn't interest me today.
items.grammar_tip: The reflexive form is 'sich interessieren für' (+ Accusative).

items.sentence_de: Welches Wort ist hier der Interrogativartikel?
items.sentence_translation: Which word is the interrogative article here?
items.grammar_tip: Words like 'welcher' or 'was für ein' are interrogative articles.

items.sentence_de: Das Interview mit dem Musiker war kurz.
items.sentence_translation: The interview with the musician was short.
items.grammar_tip: Note that 'Interview' is neuter (das).

items.sentence_de: Ich fahre im Sommer nach Italien.
items.sentence_translation: I am going to Italy in the summer.
items.grammar_tip: Most country names in German do not use an article (e.g., nach Italien).

items.sentence_de: Ich lerne Italienisch in der Schule.
items.sentence_translation: I am learning Italian at school.
items.grammar_tip: Languages are usually neuter nouns and capitalized in German.

items.sentence_de: Das ist eine einfache Ja-/Nein-Frage.
items.sentence_translation: That is a simple yes/no question.
items.grammar_tip: A 'Ja-/Nein-Frage' starts with the verb in German.

items.sentence_de: Ein Jahr hat zwölf Monate.
items.sentence_translation: One year has twelve months.
items.grammar_tip: 'Jahr' is a neuter noun (das Jahr).

items.sentence_de: Alle Mitarbeiter kommen zum Jahrestreffen.
items.sentence_translation: All employees are coming to the annual meeting.
items.grammar_tip: 'Jahres-' acts as a prefix meaning 'annual' or 'yearly'.

items.sentence_de: Meine liebste Jahreszeit ist der Sommer.
items.sentence_translation: My favorite season is summer.
items.grammar_tip: There are four 'Jahreszeiten': Frühling, Sommer, Herbst, Winter.

items.sentence_de: Wir lernen über Jahreszeiten in D-A-CH.
items.sentence_translation: We are learning about seasons in DACH countries.
items.grammar_tip: D-A-CH stands for Deutschland (D), Austria (A), and Switzerland (CH).

items.sentence_de: Im Januar ist es meistens sehr kalt.
items.sentence_translation: In January it is usually very cold.
items.grammar_tip: All months in German are masculine (der).

items.sentence_de: Meine Freundin kommt aus Japan.
items.sentence_translation: My friend comes from Japan.
items.grammar_tip: Like Italy, Japan is used without an article.

items.sentence_de: Kannst du Japanisch sprechen?
items.sentence_translation: Can you speak Japanese?
items.grammar_tip: The suffix '-isch' is common for languages and nationalities.

items.sentence_de: Die blaue Jeans passt mir gut.
items.sentence_translation: The blue jeans fit me well.
items.grammar_tip: 'Jeans' is used in the singular or plural in German, often treated as a feminine singular noun.

items.sentence_de: Ich gehe jede Woche zum Sport.
items.sentence_translation: I go to sports every week.
items.grammar_tip: 'Jede' changes endings based on the gender of the noun (jede Woche, jeder Tag).

items.sentence_de: Kann mir bitte jemand helfen?
items.sentence_translation: Can someone please help me?
items.grammar_tip: 'Jemand' refers to an unspecified person.

items.sentence_de: Ich suche eine Stelle im Job-Portal.
items.sentence_translation: I am looking for a position in the job portal.
items.grammar_tip: Many modern German terms related to the internet use English loans.

items.sentence_de: Es gibt viele Jobs rund ums Jahr.
items.sentence_translation: There are many jobs all year round.
items.grammar_tip: 'Rund ums Jahr' means 'throughout the whole year'.

items.sentence_de: Wir joggen jeden Morgen im Park.
items.sentence_translation: We jog every morning in the park.
items.grammar_tip: 'Joggen' is a loanword from English and follows regular conjugation.

items.sentence_de: Der Journalist schreibt einen neuen Artikel.
items.sentence_translation: The journalist is writing a new article.
items.grammar_tip: Masculine professions ending in '-ist' often take 'en' in other cases (n-declension).

items.sentence_de: Meine Tante ist eine bekannte Journalistin.
items.sentence_translation: My aunt is a well-known journalist.
items.grammar_tip: Remember: feminine professions almost always end in '-in'.

items.sentence_de: Wir übernachten in einer günstigen Jugendherberge.
items.sentence_translation: We are staying overnight in a cheap youth hostel.
items.grammar_tip: 'Jugendherberge' is a compound of 'Jugend' (youth) and 'Herberge' (hostel).

items.sentence_de: Im Juli haben wir Sommerferien.
items.sentence_translation: In July we have summer holidays.
items.grammar_tip: All months are masculine: der Januar, der Februar... der Juli.

items.sentence_de: Der Juni ist ein schöner Sommermonat.
items.sentence_translation: June is a beautiful summer month.
items.grammar_tip: Be careful with the pronunciation difference between 'Juni' and 'Juli'.

items.sentence_de: Er arbeitet als Jurist in Berlin.
items.sentence_translation: He works as a lawyer in Berlin.
items.grammar_tip: 'Jurist' is another word for 'Rechtsanwalt'.

items.sentence_de: Sie ist eine sehr gute Juristin.
items.sentence_translation: She is a very good lawyer.
items.grammar_tip: Professional names for women take 'die' and the '-in' ending.

items.sentence_de: Nach dem Sport bin ich völlig k.o.
items.sentence_translation: After sports, I am completely knocked out/tired.
items.grammar_tip: 'k.o.' is colloquial for being extremely exhausted.

items.sentence_de: Wir treffen uns im Wiener Kaffeehaus.
items.sentence_translation: We are meeting in the Viennese coffee house.
items.grammar_tip: 'Kaffeehaus' is a traditional term, especially in Austria.

items.sentence_de: Die Kaffeemaschine in der Küche ist kaputt.
items.sentence_translation: The coffee machine in the kitchen is broken.
items.grammar_tip: 'Die Maschine' is feminine, so 'Kaffeemaschine' is also feminine.

items.sentence_de: Ich schreibe den Termin in meinen Kalender.
items.sentence_translation: I write the appointment in my calendar.
items.grammar_tip: 'Der Kalender' is masculine.

items.sentence_de: Im Winter ist es draußen sehr kalt.
items.sentence_translation: In winter it is very cold outside.
items.grammar_tip: 'Mir ist kalt' means 'I feel cold'.

items.sentence_de: Ich mache Fotos mit meiner neuen Kamera.
items.sentence_translation: I am taking photos with my new camera.
items.grammar_tip: The plural of 'Kamera' is 'Kameras'.

items.sentence_de: Guten Tag, kann ich einen Termin haben?
items.sentence_translation: Good day, can I have an appointment?
items.grammar_tip: Use this phrase at the doctor or hair salon.

items.sentence_de: Guten Tag, kann ich Ihnen helfen?
items.sentence_translation: Good day, can I help you?
items.grammar_tip: This is a polite way to offer assistance using 'Ihnen' (formal you).

items.sentence_de: Das Essen in der Kantine ist günstig.
items.sentence_translation: The food in the canteen is cheap.
items.grammar_tip: A 'Kantine' is typically found in a workplace or school.

items.sentence_de: Wir lesen heute das dritte Kapitel.
items.sentence_translation: We are reading the third chapter today.
items.grammar_tip: 'Kapitel' is a neuter noun (das).

items.sentence_de: Mein Sohn macht zwei Mal pro Woche Karate.
items.sentence_translation: My son does karate twice a week.
items.grammar_tip: Use 'Karate machen' rather than 'spielen'.

items.sentence_de: Sie möchte eine Karriere als Ärztin machen.
items.sentence_translation: She wants to make a career as a doctor.
items.grammar_tip: 'Karriere machen' means to advance in one's profession.

items.sentence_de: Die Kinder fahren gerne auf dem Karussell.
items.sentence_translation: The children like to ride on the merry-go-round.
items.grammar_tip: Note the double 'r' and double 's' in 'Karussell'.

items.sentence_de: Ich esse zum Frühstück Brot mit Käse.
items.sentence_translation: I eat bread with cheese for breakfast.
items.grammar_tip: 'Der Käse' is masculine.

items.sentence_de: Brauchen Sie den Kassenzettel für die Tasche?
items.sentence_translation: Do you need the receipt for the bag?
items.grammar_tip: A 'Kassenzettel' is specifically the slip of paper from a cash register.

items.sentence_de: Wir kaufen die Kleidung im Kaufhaus.
items.sentence_translation: We buy the clothes in the department store.
items.grammar_tip: 'Kaufhaus' is a large store selling many different types of goods.

items.sentence_de: Ich kann dich am Telefon kaum hören.
items.sentence_translation: I can barely hear you on the phone.
items.grammar_tip: 'Kaum' indicates a very small amount or degree.

items.sentence_de: Du hast das Spiel verloren? Kein Glück?!
items.sentence_translation: You lost the game? No luck?!
items.grammar_tip: 'Glück' is neuter, but 'kein' here matches its gender in the nominative.

items.sentence_de: Ich habe heute leider kein Geld dabei.
items.sentence_translation: Unfortunately, I have no money with me today.
items.grammar_tip: 'Kein' is used to negate nouns with an indefinite or zero article.

items.sentence_de: Der Kellner bringt uns die Speisekarte.
items.sentence_translation: The waiter is bringing us the menu.
items.grammar_tip: The plural of 'Kellner' is the same as the singular.

items.sentence_de: Die Kellnerin in diesem Café ist freundlich.
items.sentence_translation: The waitress in this café is friendly.
items.grammar_tip: Waitress is 'Kellnerin' in German.

items.sentence_de: Ich kenne diesen Mann schon sehr lange.
items.sentence_translation: I have known this man for a very long time.
items.grammar_tip: 'Kennen' is used for people or places you are familiar with.

items.sentence_de: Ich möchte bitte ein Kilo Äpfel kaufen.
items.sentence_translation: I would like to buy a kilo of apples, please.
items.grammar_tip: 'Kilo' is short for 'Kilogramm' and is neuter.

items.sentence_de: Ein Kilogramm Mehl kostet einen Euro.
items.sentence_translation: One kilogram of flour costs one euro.
items.grammar_tip: Abbreviation for 'Kilogramm' is 'kg'.

items.sentence_de: Der Supermarkt ist einen Kilometer von hier.
items.sentence_translation: The supermarket is one kilometer from here.
items.grammar_tip: 'Kilometer' is masculine (der Kilometer).

items.sentence_de: Die Kinder spielen in ihrem Kinderzimmer.
items.sentence_translation: The children are playing in their nursery.
items.grammar_tip: 'Zimmer' is neuter, so compound words with '-zimmer' are also neuter.

items.sentence_de: Die Kirche steht mitten auf dem Marktplatz.
items.sentence_translation: The church stands in the middle of the marketplace.
items.grammar_tip: 'Kirche' is a feminine noun.

items.sentence_de: In der Kiste liegen viele alte Bücher.
items.sentence_translation: There are many old books in the box.
items.grammar_tip: 'Kiste' is often used for large boxes or crates.

items.sentence_de: Ich muss meine Klamotten in den Schrank räumen.
items.sentence_translation: I have to put my clothes in the closet.
items.grammar_tip: 'Klamotten' is a colloquial term for 'Kleidung'.

items.sentence_de: Sie trägt heute ein schönes rotes Kleid.
items.sentence_translation: She is wearing a beautiful red dress today.
items.grammar_tip: 'Das Kleid' refers specifically to a woman's dress.

items.sentence_de: Ich arbeite samstags in einem Kleidergeschäft.
items.sentence_translation: I work in a clothing store on Saturdays.
items.grammar_tip: 'Geschäft' is another word for 'Laden' (shop).

items.sentence_de: Der Kleiderkauf hat viel Spaß gemacht.
items.sentence_translation: The clothes shopping was a lot of fun.
items.grammar_tip: 'Kauf' comes from 'kaufen' (to buy).

items.sentence_de: Die Kinder klettern gerne auf den Baum.
items.sentence_translation: The children like to climb the tree.
items.grammar_tip: 'Klettern' is used for climbing trees, mountains, or walls.

items.sentence_de: Das Lied klingt sehr schön und traurig.
items.sentence_translation: The song sounds very beautiful and sad.
items.grammar_tip: Use 'klingen' to describe how something sounds.

items.sentence_de: Bitte klopfen Sie, bevor Sie reinkommen.
items.sentence_translation: Please knock before you come in.
items.grammar_tip: 'Klopfen' is a regular verb.

items.sentence_de: Wir trinken ein Bier in der Kneipe.
items.sentence_translation: We are drinking a beer in the pub.
items.grammar_tip: A 'Kneipe' is a casual place to drink, similar to a pub.

items.sentence_de: In Berlin gibt es viele Kneipen & Co.
items.sentence_translation: In Berlin there are many pubs and such.
items.grammar_tip: '& Co' is used like 'and company' or 'and similar things'.

items.sentence_de: Mein Knie tut nach dem Fußball weh.
items.sentence_translation: My knee hurts after football.
items.grammar_tip: 'Das Knie' (singular) is pronounced with a long 'i'.

items.sentence_de: Der Koch arbeitet in einem großen Restaurant.
items.sentence_translation: The cook works in a large restaurant.
items.grammar_tip: The plural 'Köche' involves an Umlaut change.

items.sentence_de: Meine Mutter ist eine fantastische Köchin.
items.sentence_translation: My mother is a fantastic cook.
items.grammar_tip: The female form 'Köchin' also adds an Umlaut compared to 'Koch'.

items.sentence_de: Ich hasse Kofferpacken vor dem Urlaub.
items.sentence_translation: I hate packing suitcases before vacation.
items.grammar_tip: Verbal nouns like 'Kofferpacken' are always neuter in German.

items.sentence_de: Meine Kollegin arbeitet heute im Büro.
items.sentence_translation: My female colleague is working in the office today.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -in are almost always feminine and refer to female persons.

items.sentence_de: Woher kommen Sie genau aus Deutschland?
items.sentence_translation: Where exactly do you come from in Germany?
items.grammar_tip: The verb 'kommen' is often used with 'aus' to indicate origin.

items.sentence_de: Er schreibt einen kurzen Kommentar dazu.
items.sentence_translation: He is writing a short commentary on it.
items.grammar_tip: The plural of Kommentar is Kommentare.

items.sentence_de: Kommt ihr heute Abend zur Party?
items.sentence_translation: Are you (plural) coming to the party tonight?
items.grammar_tip: 'Ihr' is the plural informal form of 'you' in German.

items.sentence_de: Das Wort ist ein langes Kompositum.
items.sentence_translation: The word is a long compound.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -um often have plurals ending in -a.

items.sentence_de: Ich kann schon sehr gut Deutsch.
items.sentence_translation: I can already speak German very well.
items.grammar_tip: 'Können' is a modal verb; the vowel changes from 'ö' to 'a' in singular forms.

items.sentence_de: Dieser Buchstabe ist ein harter Konsonant.
items.sentence_translation: This letter is a hard consonant.
items.grammar_tip: This is a masculine noun following the weak declension (n-declension).

items.sentence_de: Wir haben leider keinen Kontakt mehr.
items.sentence_translation: Unfortunately, we are no longer in contact.
items.grammar_tip: Remember: 'keinen Kontakt' is used in the accusative case here.

items.sentence_de: Man muss das Wort im Kontext verstehen.
items.sentence_translation: One must understand the word in context.
items.grammar_tip: German often uses 'im' (in dem) before Kontext.

items.sentence_de: Ich möchte ein neues Konto eröffnen.
items.sentence_translation: I would like to open a new account.
items.grammar_tip: The plural 'Konten' is more common than 'Kontos'.

items.sentence_de: Wie lautet Ihre aktuelle Kontonummer bitte?
items.sentence_translation: What is your current account number, please?
items.grammar_tip: The word is a compound of 'Konto' and 'Nummer'.

items.sentence_de: Die Fahrkarten wurden in einer Kontrolle geprüft.
items.sentence_translation: The tickets were checked in an inspection.
items.grammar_tip: The noun 'Kontrolle' corresponds to the verb 'kontrollieren'.

items.sentence_de: Der Lehrer muss die Hausaufgaben kontrollieren.
items.sentence_translation: The teacher has to check the homework.
items.grammar_tip: Verbs ending in -ieren do not use 'ge-' in the past participle (kontrolliert).

items.sentence_de: Wir gehen am Samstag ins Konzert.
items.sentence_translation: We are going to the concert on Saturday.
items.grammar_tip: 'Ins' is a contraction of 'in das'.

items.sentence_de: Der Konzertbeginn ist um acht Uhr.
items.sentence_translation: The concert starts at eight o'clock.
items.grammar_tip: This is a compound noun: Konzert + Beginn.

items.sentence_de: Das Konzerthaus liegt direkt am Marktplatz.
items.sentence_translation: The concert hall is located directly on the market square.
items.grammar_tip: In compounds, the last noun determines the gender (das Haus -> das Konzerthaus).

items.sentence_de: Ich habe noch eine Konzertkarte übrig.
items.sentence_translation: I have one concert ticket left.
items.grammar_tip: 'Karte' is feminine, so it is 'eine' in the accusative.

items.sentence_de: Ich kann nicht kommen, ich habe Kopfschmerzen.
items.sentence_translation: I can't come, I have a headache.
items.grammar_tip: This word is almost always used in the plural in German.

items.sentence_de: Regelmäßiger Sport ist gut für den Körper.
items.sentence_translation: Regular sport is good for the body.
items.grammar_tip: The plural form is identical to the singular form.

items.sentence_de: Der Fuß ist ein wichtiger Körperteil.
items.sentence_translation: The foot is an important body part.
items.grammar_tip: Teil is masculine, therefore Körperteil is also masculine.

items.sentence_de: Bitte korrigieren Sie die Fehler im Text.
items.sentence_translation: Please correct the mistakes in the text.
items.grammar_tip: Like other -ieren verbs, it does not take 'ge-' in the perfect tense.

items.sentence_de: In dieser Abteilung gibt es viel Kosmetik.
items.sentence_translation: In this department there are many cosmetics.
items.grammar_tip: Abstract nouns like 'Kosmetik' are often used without a plural in general contexts.

items.sentence_de: Mein Opa liegt seit gestern im Krankenhaus.
items.sentence_translation: My grandpa has been in the hospital since yesterday.
items.grammar_tip: Literally 'sick house'.

items.sentence_de: Er arbeitet als Krankenpfleger in Berlin.
items.sentence_translation: He works as a nurse in Berlin.
items.grammar_tip: Job titles for males often end in -er.

items.sentence_de: Die Krankenpflegerin bringt mir das Essen.
items.sentence_translation: The nurse brings me the food.
items.grammar_tip: Job titles for females add -in to the male form.

items.sentence_de: Gegen diese Krankheit gibt es eine Medizin.
items.sentence_translation: There is a medicine for this illness.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -heit are always feminine.

items.sentence_de: Er trägt heute eine blaue Krawatte.
items.sentence_translation: He is wearing a blue tie today.
items.grammar_tip: 'Tragen' (to wear) takes the accusative case.

items.sentence_de: Meine Schwester ist eine sehr kreative Person.
items.sentence_translation: My sister is a very creative person.
items.grammar_tip: Adjectives take endings when they come before a noun.

items.sentence_de: Kann ich hier mit Kreditkarte bezahlen?
items.sentence_translation: Can I pay by credit card here?
items.grammar_tip: Commonly used with the preposition 'mit'.

items.sentence_de: Die Vögel kreisen hoch oben am Himmel.
items.sentence_translation: The birds are circling high up in the sky.
items.grammar_tip: This verb describes circular motion.

items.sentence_de: Berlin bietet sehr viel Kunst und Kultur.
items.sentence_translation: Berlin offers a lot of art and culture.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -ur are typically feminine.

items.sentence_de: Wir besuchen die Lange Kultur-Nacht im Museum.
items.sentence_translation: We are visiting the Long Night of Culture at the museum.
items.grammar_tip: A compound of 'Kultur' and 'Nacht'.

items.sentence_de: Das internationale Kulturfestival beginnt nächste Woche.
items.sentence_translation: The international culture festival starts next week.
items.grammar_tip: Compound noun: das Festival is neutral.

items.sentence_de: Mein Chef ist heute auf einem Kundenbesuch.
items.sentence_translation: My boss is on a customer visit today.
items.grammar_tip: Kunden is the plural/genitive form of Kunde (customer).

items.sentence_de: Eine nette Kundin hat das Kleid gekauft.
items.sentence_translation: A nice female customer bought the dress.
items.grammar_tip: Female version of 'der Kunde'.

items.sentence_de: Sie interessiert sich sehr für moderne Kunst.
items.sentence_translation: She is very interested in modern art.
items.grammar_tip: The plural 'Künste' refers to 'the arts'.

items.sentence_de: Die neue Ausstellung in der Kunsthalle ist toll.
items.sentence_translation: The new exhibition in the art gallery is great.
items.grammar_tip: In the dative case (after 'in'), 'die' changes to 'der'.

items.sentence_de: Der Künstler malt ein Bild in seinem Atelier.
items.sentence_translation: The artist is painting a picture in his studio.
items.grammar_tip: The plural is the same as the singular.

items.sentence_de: Sie ist eine bekannte Künstlerin aus Wien.
items.sentence_translation: She is a well-known female artist from Vienna.
items.grammar_tip: Remember to add -in for the female form.

items.sentence_de: Das Kursplakat hängt an der großen Wand.
items.sentence_translation: The course poster is hanging on the big wall.
items.grammar_tip: Plakat is a neutral noun.

items.sentence_de: Unser Kursraum ist im zweiten Stock links.
items.sentence_translation: Our classroom is on the second floor on the left.
items.grammar_tip: Raum is masculine; Kurs + Raum.

items.sentence_de: Die Kursstatistik zeigt viele Teilnehmer aus Spanien.
items.sentence_translation: The course statistics show many participants from Spain.
items.grammar_tip: Statistik is feminine.

items.sentence_de: 'Uni' ist die Kurzform für Universität.
items.sentence_translation: 'Uni' is the short form for university.
items.grammar_tip: Opposite of 'Langform'.

items.sentence_de: Dieses Label produziert sehr teure Kleidung.
items.sentence_translation: This brand produces very expensive clothing.
items.grammar_tip: The word is borrowed from English but takes a German article.

items.sentence_de: Sie macht Experimente im chemischen Labor.
items.sentence_translation: She does experiments in the chemistry lab.
items.grammar_tip: The plural can be 'Labore' or 'Laboratorien'.

items.sentence_de: Der Laborant prüft die Proben sehr genau.
items.sentence_translation: The lab assistant checks the samples very carefully.
items.grammar_tip: Follows the n-declension: den Laboranten (accusative).

items.sentence_de: Die Laborantin arbeitet heute bis spät abends.
items.sentence_translation: The lab assistant works until late in the evening today.
items.grammar_tip: Feminine job title ending in -in.

items.sentence_de: Die Wohnung hat eine sehr ruhige Lage.
items.sentence_translation: The apartment has a very quiet location.
items.grammar_tip: Refers to the geographical position of a property.

items.sentence_de: Die Lampe auf dem Tisch ist kaputt.
items.sentence_translation: The lamp on the table is broken.
items.grammar_tip: Most nouns ending in -e are feminine.

items.sentence_de: Deutschland ist ein Land in Europa.
items.sentence_translation: Germany is a country in Europe.
items.grammar_tip: The plural 'Länder' uses an umlaut.

items.sentence_de: In der Schule lernen wir Länder und Sprachen.
items.sentence_translation: In school, we learn about countries and languages.
items.grammar_tip: Both nouns are in their plural forms here.

items.sentence_de: Die Landschaft in den Alpen ist wunderschön.
items.sentence_translation: The landscape in the Alps is beautiful.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -schaft are always feminine.

items.sentence_de: Im Sommer sind die Tage viel länger.
items.sentence_translation: In summer, the days are much longer.
items.grammar_tip: The comparative form of 'lang' (long).

items.sentence_de: Der Film gestern war leider sehr langweilig.
items.sentence_translation: The movie yesterday was unfortunately very boring.
items.grammar_tip: The opposite of 'interessant' or 'spannend'.

items.sentence_de: Wir laufen jeden Morgen eine kleine Runde.
items.sentence_translation: We run a small lap every morning.
items.grammar_tip: In the 3rd person singular, it changes to 'läuft'.

items.sentence_de: Wie läuft es heute bei deiner Arbeit?
items.sentence_translation: How is it going today at your work?
items.grammar_tip: An idiomatic way to ask how a situation is progressing.

items.sentence_de: Lauras Praktikum in der Firma beginnt morgen.
items.sentence_translation: Laura's internship at the company starts tomorrow.
items.grammar_tip: Add 's' to names to show possession (no apostrophe in German).

items.sentence_de: Der Marktplatz in der Stadt ist sehr lebendig.
items.sentence_translation: The market square in the city is very lively.
items.grammar_tip: Can mean 'alive' or 'lively/vibrant'.

items.sentence_de: Der Kuchen schmeckt wirklich sehr lecker.
items.sentence_translation: The cake tastes really very delicious.
items.grammar_tip: Commonly used with the verb 'schmecken'.

items.sentence_de: Die Flasche Wasser ist schon ganz leer.
items.sentence_translation: The bottle of water is already completely empty.
items.grammar_tip: The opposite of 'voll' (full).

items.sentence_de: Unsere Lehrerin erklärt die Grammatik sehr gut.
items.sentence_translation: Our teacher explains the grammar very well.
items.grammar_tip: The male form is 'Lehrer'.

items.sentence_de: Es tut mir leid, ich habe keine Zeit.
items.sentence_translation: I am sorry, I don't have time.
items.grammar_tip: A separable verb often used as a set phrase for apologizing.

items.sentence_de: Ich schreibe Vokabeln auf eine Lernkarte.
items.sentence_translation: I write vocabulary on a learning card.
items.grammar_tip: A compound: Lernen + Karte.

items.sentence_de: Dieser Lernwortschatz ist wichtig für die Prüfung.
items.sentence_translation: This learning vocabulary is important for the exam.
items.grammar_tip: Wortschatz (vocabulary) is masculine.

items.sentence_de: Ich lese am Abend gerne ein Buch.
items.sentence_translation: I like to read a book in the evening.
items.grammar_tip: Irregular verb: ich lese, du liest, er liest.

items.sentence_de: Das war die letzte Woche meines Urlaubs.
items.sentence_translation: That was the last week of my vacation.
items.grammar_tip: Adjective endings change based on the noun's gender and case.

items.sentence_de: Liebe Grüße an deine ganze Familie!
items.sentence_translation: Kind regards to your whole family!
items.grammar_tip: Standard closing for informal letters or emails.

items.sentence_de: Meine Lieblingsfarbe ist Blau, und deine?
items.sentence_translation: My favorite color is blue, and yours?
items.grammar_tip: 'Lieblings-' can be prefixed to many nouns to mean 'favorite'.

items.sentence_de: Der Park ist mein absoluter Lieblingsort.
items.sentence_translation: The park is my absolute favorite place.
items.grammar_tip: Ort is masculine, so 'mein' stays the same in nominative.

items.sentence_de: Die Küche ist mein liebstes Lieblingszimmer.
items.sentence_translation: The kitchen is my favorite room of all.
items.grammar_tip: The plural form is the same as the singular.

items.sentence_de: München liegt im Süden von Deutschland.
items.sentence_translation: Munich is located in the south of Germany.
items.grammar_tip: Used for the geographical location of cities and countries.

items.sentence_de: Das Mädchen trägt heute ein lila Kleid.
items.sentence_translation: The girl is wearing a purple dress today.
items.grammar_tip: Some color adjectives like 'lila' or 'rosa' often don't take endings.

items.sentence_de: Ich trinke im Sommer gerne kalte Limonade.
items.sentence_translation: I like to drink cold lemonade in summer.
items.grammar_tip: Usually shortened to 'Limo' in spoken German.

items.sentence_de: Gehen Sie links, rechts und dann geradeaus.
items.sentence_translation: Go left, right, and then straight ahead.
items.grammar_tip: Basic directions used when asking or giving the way.

items.sentence_de: Ich schreibe eine Liste für den Supermarkt.
items.sentence_translation: I am writing a list for the supermarket.
items.grammar_tip: Used with the preposition 'auf' (on) or 'für' (for).

items.sentence_de: Ich kaufe einen Liter Milch.
items.sentence_translation: I am buying one litre of milk.
items.grammar_tip: Liter remains in singular form after numbers.

items.sentence_de: Ich brauche einen Löffel für die Suppe.
items.sentence_translation: I need a spoon for the soup.
items.grammar_tip: Löffel is one of the many German nouns that do not change in plural.

items.sentence_de: Sie wohnen in einem modernen Loft.
items.sentence_translation: They live in a modern loft.
items.grammar_tip: Borrowed from English, this noun takes 'das' as its article.

items.sentence_de: Was ist heute in der Stadt los?
items.sentence_translation: What is going on in the city today?
items.grammar_tip: 'Was ist los?' is a very common way to ask 'What's happening?'.
