items.sentence_de: Wir müssen jetzt mit dem Auto losfahren.
items.sentence_translation: We have to drive off now.
items.grammar_tip: Losfahren is a separable verb used for vehicles.

items.sentence_de: Wann soll die Party heute losgehen?
items.sentence_translation: When is the party supposed to start today?
items.grammar_tip: Literally 'to go loose', it often means 'to start' or 'to begin'.

items.sentence_de: Hast du Lust auf ein Eis?
items.sentence_translation: Do you feel like having an ice cream?
items.grammar_tip: Always used with 'haben' (Ich habe Lust).

items.sentence_de: Mahlzeit! Das Essen schmeckt sehr gut.
items.sentence_translation: Enjoy your meal! The food tastes very good.
items.grammar_tip: Used as a greeting around lunchtime in workplaces.

items.sentence_de: Im Mai blühen viele Blumen.
items.sentence_translation: In May, many flowers bloom.
items.grammar_tip: All months in German are masculine (der).

items.sentence_de: Ich schreibe dir heute eine Mail.
items.sentence_translation: I will write you an email today.
items.grammar_tip: Short for E-Mail; it is feminine.

items.sentence_de: Komm mich mal in Berlin besuchen!
items.sentence_translation: Come visit me in Berlin sometime!
items.grammar_tip: Used here as a modal particle to make the request sound friendlier.

items.sentence_de: Ich war schon drei Mal dort.
items.sentence_translation: I have been there three times already.
items.grammar_tip: Use 'Mal' for frequency and 'Zeit' for duration.

items.sentence_de: Die Kinder malen ein schönes Bild.
items.sentence_translation: The children are painting a beautiful picture.
items.grammar_tip: Malen refers to artistic painting; use 'streichen' for walls.

items.sentence_de: Ich gehe manchmal am Abend spazieren.
items.sentence_translation: I sometimes go for a walk in the evening.
items.grammar_tip: Manchmal indicates a frequency between 'selten' and 'oft'.

items.sentence_de: Der Mann dort ist mein Onkel.
items.sentence_translation: The man over there is my uncle.
items.grammar_tip: Mann means both 'man' and 'husband'.

items.sentence_de: Zieh bitte deinen warmen Mantel an.
items.sentence_translation: Please put on your warm coat.
items.grammar_tip: Note the stem vowel change in the plural: Mantel -> Mäntel.

items.sentence_de: Er läuft dieses Jahr einen Marathon.
items.sentence_translation: He is running a marathon this year.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -on often take -s in the plural.

items.sentence_de: Bitte markieren Sie die richtigen Antworten.
items.sentence_translation: Please highlight the correct answers.
items.grammar_tip: Verbs ending in -ieren never take 'ge-' in the past participle.

items.sentence_de: Wir kaufen Obst auf dem Markt.
items.sentence_translation: We buy fruit at the market.
items.grammar_tip: In German, you go 'auf den Markt' (to the market).

items.sentence_de: Ich esse Brot mit Butter und Marmelade.
items.sentence_translation: I eat bread with butter and jam.
items.grammar_tip: Most German words for fruit spreads are feminine.

items.sentence_de: Der Frühling beginnt meistens im März.
items.sentence_translation: Spring usually begins in March.
items.grammar_tip: Month names are masculine.

items.sentence_de: Das Wort 'Hund' ist grammatikalisch maskulin.
items.sentence_translation: The word 'dog' is grammatically masculine.
items.grammar_tip: Used to describe grammatical gender (der).

items.sentence_de: Wir brauchen das genaue Maß vom Tisch.
items.sentence_translation: We need the exact measurement of the table.
items.grammar_tip: The letter 'ß' is used after long vowels.

items.sentence_de: Morgen schreiben wir einen schweren Mathe-Test.
items.sentence_translation: Tomorrow we are writing a difficult math test.
items.grammar_tip: Compound nouns take the article of the last word (der Test).

items.sentence_de: Die Katze sucht die kleine Maus.
items.sentence_translation: The cat is looking for the little mouse.
items.grammar_tip: Maus can refer to the animal or the computer peripheral.

items.sentence_de: Das Paket darf maximal zwei Kilo wiegen.
items.sentence_translation: The package may weigh two kilos at most.
items.grammar_tip: Often used with measurements and limits.

items.sentence_de: Der Mechaniker repariert mein altes Auto.
items.sentence_translation: The mechanic is repairing my old car.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -er often don't change in plural.

items.sentence_de: Die Mechanikerin arbeitet in der Werkstatt.
items.sentence_translation: The mechanic is working in the workshop.
items.grammar_tip: Add -in to the male profession to make it female.

items.sentence_de: Wir nutzen täglich viele verschiedene Medien.
items.sentence_translation: We use many different media daily.
items.grammar_tip: This is the plural form; the singular is 'das Medium'.

items.sentence_de: Er muss ein Medikament gegen Schmerzen nehmen.
items.sentence_translation: He has to take a medicine for pain.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -ment are usually neuter.

items.sentence_de: Ich habe mehrere Freunde in dieser Stadt.
items.sentence_translation: I have several friends in this city.
items.grammar_tip: 'Mehrere' is used only in the plural.

items.sentence_de: Mein Beruf macht mir viel Spaß.
items.sentence_translation: My profession gives me a lot of joy.
items.grammar_tip: Always capitalize 'Beruf' as it is a noun.

items.sentence_de: Das ist mein Bruder aus Berlin.
items.sentence_translation: That is my brother from Berlin.
items.grammar_tip: Possessive pronouns match the gender of the possessed noun.

items.sentence_de: Meine Hobbys sind Lesen und Schwimmen.
items.sentence_translation: My hobbies are reading and swimming.
items.grammar_tip: The German plural of Hobby is 'Hobbys' (with a 'y').

items.sentence_de: Was meinen Sie genau mit diesem Wort?
items.sentence_translation: What exactly do you mean by this word?
items.grammar_tip: Meinen expresses an opinion or intent.

items.sentence_de: Die meisten Menschen leben in der Stadt.
items.sentence_translation: Most people live in the city.
items.grammar_tip: Usually used with the definite article 'die'.

items.sentence_de: Ich trinke meistens Tee zum Frühstück.
items.sentence_translation: I mostly drink tea for breakfast.
items.grammar_tip: Meistens is an adverb of frequency meaning 'usually'.

items.sentence_de: Bitte melden Sie sich am Empfang.
items.sentence_translation: Please report to the reception.
items.grammar_tip: 'Sich melden' is a reflexive verb.

items.sentence_de: Wir essen heute Mittag in der Mensa.
items.sentence_translation: We are eating in the canteen at noon today.
items.grammar_tip: Refers specifically to a university dining hall.

items.sentence_de: Ich kann mir die Nummer nicht merken.
items.sentence_translation: I cannot remember the number.
items.grammar_tip: 'Sich etwas merken' is reflexive in the dative.

items.sentence_de: Das Messer ist leider nicht sehr scharf.
items.sentence_translation: The knife is unfortunately not very sharp.
items.grammar_tip: One of the common neuter kitchen utensils.

items.sentence_de: Der Baum ist zehn Meter hoch.
items.sentence_translation: The tree is ten metres high.
items.grammar_tip: Like Liter, Meter stays singular after a number.

items.sentence_de: Diese Methode ist sehr einfach und schnell.
items.sentence_translation: This method is very simple and fast.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -e are often feminine.

items.sentence_de: Ich kaufe die Würstchen in der Metzgerei.
items.sentence_translation: I buy the sausages at the butcher's.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -ei are always feminine.

items.sentence_de: Er kommt aus Mexiko und spricht Spanisch.
items.sentence_translation: He comes from Mexico and speaks Spanish.
items.grammar_tip: Countries without articles (like Mexico) use 'aus'.

items.sentence_de: Auf der Welt leben mehrere Milliarden Menschen.
items.sentence_translation: Several billion people live in the world.
items.grammar_tip: In German, 'Milliarde' is 10 to the power of 9.

items.sentence_de: Die Stadt hat über eine Million Einwohner.
items.sentence_translation: The city has over a million inhabitants.
items.grammar_tip: Numbers like Million and Milliarde are treated as nouns.

items.sentence_de: Ich schlafe mindestens acht Stunden pro Nacht.
items.sentence_translation: I sleep at least eight hours per night.
items.grammar_tip: Used to express a minimum amount.

items.sentence_de: Wir erstellen eine Mindmap für das Projekt.
items.sentence_translation: We are creating a mind map for the project.
items.grammar_tip: Borrowed from English, it is feminine.

items.sentence_de: Fünf minus zwei ist gleich drei.
items.sentence_translation: Five minus two equals three.
items.grammar_tip: Used for subtraction and negative temperatures.

items.sentence_de: Warten Sie bitte eine Minute auf mich.
items.sentence_translation: Please wait one minute for me.
items.grammar_tip: Plural form simply adds -n.

items.sentence_de: Du musst den Saft mit Wasser mischen.
items.sentence_translation: You have to mix the juice with water.
items.grammar_tip: Often used with the preposition 'mit'.

items.sentence_de: Er zeigte sein Missfallen über das Wetter.
items.sentence_translation: He showed his disapproval about the weather.
items.grammar_tip: This noun is based on the verb 'fallen' but with 'miss-'.

items.sentence_de: So ein Mist! Ich habe meinen Schlüssel vergessen.
items.sentence_translation: Such a bother! I forgot my key.
items.grammar_tip: Common mild expression of frustration.

items.sentence_de: Bei diesem Mistwetter bleibe ich lieber zu Hause.
items.sentence_translation: In this rotten weather, I'd rather stay at home.
items.grammar_tip: A compound of 'Mist' and 'Wetter'.

items.translation: Who do I have to speak with?
items.sentence_de: Mit wem muss ich über das Problem sprechen?
items.sentence_translation: Who do I have to speak with about the problem?
items.grammar_tip: 'Mit' always triggers the dative case (wem).

items.sentence_de: Mein Mitarbeiter hilft mir bei der Arbeit.
items.sentence_translation: My colleague helps me with the work.
items.grammar_tip: Can mean employee or co-worker.

items.sentence_de: Die neue Mitarbeiterin ist sehr freundlich.
items.sentence_translation: The new colleague is very friendly.
items.grammar_tip: The feminine form of Mitarbeiter.

items.sentence_de: Soll ich einen Kuchen zur Party mitbringen?
items.sentence_translation: Should I bring a cake to the party?
items.grammar_tip: A separable verb: 'Ich bringe etwas mit'.

items.sentence_de: Ich bin seit einem Jahr Mitglied im Verein.
items.sentence_translation: I have been a member of the club for a year.
items.grammar_tip: Commonly used for sports clubs or associations.

items.sentence_de: Willst du heute Abend ins Kino mitkommen?
items.sentence_translation: Do you want to come along to the cinema tonight?
items.grammar_tip: Separable verb: 'Kommst du mit?'.

items.sentence_de: Die Schüler sollen im Buch leise mitlesen.
items.sentence_translation: The students should read along quietly in the book.
items.grammar_tip: Separable verb using 'mit' and 'lesen'.

items.sentence_de: Kannst du mich im Auto zum Bahnhof mitnehmen?
items.sentence_translation: Can you take me along in the car to the station?
items.grammar_tip: Separable verb; the stem 'nehmen' is irregular.

items.sentence_de: Alle Kinder sollen das Lied laut mitsprechen.
items.sentence_translation: All children should speak the song along loudly.
items.grammar_tip: Often used in language learning contexts.

items.sentence_de: Am Mittag essen wir in der Kantine.
items.sentence_translation: At noon we eat in the canteen.
items.grammar_tip: Literally 'mid-day'.

items.sentence_de: Was gibt es heute zum Mittagessen?
items.sentence_translation: What is for lunch today?
items.grammar_tip: It is a neuter noun (das Essen).

items.sentence_de: Ich mache mittags immer eine kurze Pause.
items.sentence_translation: I always take a short break at noon.
items.grammar_tip: Adverbs of time ending in -s indicate repetition.

items.sentence_de: Wir gehen in der Mittagspause im Park spazieren.
items.sentence_translation: We go for a walk in the park during the lunch break.
items.grammar_tip: A compound of 'Mittag' and 'Pause'.

items.sentence_de: Am Mittwoch habe ich einen Termin beim Arzt.
items.sentence_translation: On Wednesday I have an appointment with the doctor.
items.grammar_tip: The only day of the week that doesn't end in '-tag'.

items.sentence_de: Das Modalverb 'können' steht oft auf Position zwei.
items.sentence_translation: The modal verb 'können' is often at position two.
items.grammar_tip: Modal verbs change the meaning of the main verb.

items.sentence_de: Sie interessiert sich sehr für moderne Mode.
items.sentence_translation: She is very interested in modern fashion.
items.grammar_tip: Usually singular in German.

items.sentence_de: Der Modedesigner entwirft ein neues Kleid.
items.sentence_translation: The fashion designer is designing a new dress.
items.grammar_tip: Compound: Mode + Designer.

items.sentence_de: Die Modedesignerin zeigt ihre Kollektion in Paris.
items.sentence_translation: The fashion designer is showing her collection in Paris.
items.grammar_tip: Feminine form of Modedesigner.

items.sentence_de: Als Modefan kauft er viele neue Kleider.
items.sentence_translation: As a fashion fan, he buys many new clothes.
items.grammar_tip: A casual term for someone who loves fashion.

items.sentence_de: Dieses Modell gibt es auch in blauer Farbe.
items.sentence_translation: This model is also available in blue.
items.grammar_tip: Can refer to a product version or a person.

items.sentence_de: Sie studiert Design an einer Modeschule.
items.sentence_translation: She is studying design at a fashion school.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -schule are feminine (die).

items.sentence_de: Ich mag Pizza und Eis sehr.
items.sentence_translation: I like pizza and ice cream very much.
items.grammar_tip: The verb mögen is irregular: ich mag, du magst, er/sie/es mag.

items.sentence_de: Es gibt eine Möglichkeit für dich.
items.sentence_translation: There is a possibility for you.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -keit are always feminine.

items.sentence_de: Moin, wie geht es dir heute?
items.sentence_translation: Morning, how are you today?
items.grammar_tip: Moin is a common greeting in Northern Germany, used at any time of day.

items.sentence_de: Der Monat Januar ist sehr kalt.
items.sentence_translation: The month of January is very cold.
items.grammar_tip: Months and the word Monat are masculine (der).

items.sentence_de: Am Montag gehe ich zur Arbeit.
items.sentence_translation: On Monday I go to work.
items.grammar_tip: Days of the week are always masculine. Use 'am' for 'on'.

items.sentence_de: Ich trinke morgens immer einen Kaffee.
items.sentence_translation: I always drink a coffee in the morning.
items.grammar_tip: Temporal adverbs like 'morgens' are not capitalized.

items.sentence_de: Sein Motorrad ist sehr schnell und neu.
items.sentence_translation: His motorcycle is very fast and new.
items.grammar_tip: Compound nouns take the gender of the last part: das Rad -> das Motorrad.

items.sentence_de: Das Museum ist am Montag leider geschlossen.
items.sentence_translation: The museum is unfortunately closed on Monday.
items.grammar_tip: Words of Latin origin ending in -um are often neuter.

items.sentence_de: Wir gehen heute zur langen Museumsnacht.
items.sentence_translation: We are going to the long museum night today.
items.grammar_tip: Nacht is feminine, so Museumsnacht is feminine.

items.sentence_de: Ich höre gerne laute Musik im Auto.
items.sentence_translation: I like listening to loud music in the car.
items.grammar_tip: The word Musik is usually used in the singular.

items.sentence_de: Die Musikgruppe spielt live im Park.
items.sentence_translation: The music group is playing live in the park.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -e often have the plural -n.

items.sentence_de: Er arbeitet bei einer großen Musikproduktion.
items.sentence_translation: He works at a large music production.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -tion are always feminine.

items.sentence_de: Mein Sohn geht in die Musikschule.
items.sentence_translation: My son goes to the music school.
items.grammar_tip: Compound nouns: Musik + Schule = die Musikschule.

items.sentence_de: Zum Frühstück esse ich meistens Müsli.
items.sentence_translation: For breakfast I usually eat muesli.
items.grammar_tip: Müsli is a neuter noun in German.

items.sentence_de: Ich muss heute lange im Büro arbeiten.
items.sentence_translation: I have to work late in the office today.
items.grammar_tip: Müssen expresses necessity or obligation.

items.sentence_de: Meine Muttersprache ist Deutsch und Englisch.
items.sentence_translation: My mother tongue is German and English.
items.grammar_tip: Sprache is feminine, therefore Muttersprache is feminine.

items.sentence_de: Es ist kalt, nimm deine Mütze mit.
items.sentence_translation: It is cold, take your hat with you.
items.grammar_tip: Mütze refers to a soft cap/beanie, while Hut is a formal hat.

items.sentence_de: Ich gehe jetzt müde nach Hause.
items.sentence_translation: I am going home now tired.
items.grammar_tip: 'Nach Hause' indicates movement towards home; 'zu Hause' indicates being there.

items.sentence_de: Mein Nachbar ist sehr freundlich und hilft.
items.sentence_translation: My neighbor is very friendly and helps.
items.grammar_tip: Nachbar belongs to the N-Declension group.

items.sentence_de: Meine Nachbarin wohnt schon lange hier.
items.sentence_translation: My neighbor (f) has lived here for a long time.
items.grammar_tip: Add -in to the masculine form to make it feminine.

items.sentence_de: Ich muss beim Lehrer kurz nachfragen.
items.sentence_translation: I have to ask the teacher briefly.
items.grammar_tip: This is a separable verb: Er fragt nach.

items.sentence_de: Was machst du heute am Nachmittag?
items.sentence_translation: What are you doing today in the afternoon?
items.grammar_tip: Nach + Mittag (After + Noon). It is masculine.

items.sentence_de: Ich gehe nachmittags oft im Park spazieren.
items.sentence_translation: I often go for a walk in the park in the afternoons.
items.grammar_tip: The suffix -s makes it an adverb meaning 'every afternoon'.

items.sentence_de: Wie ist Ihr Nachname, Herr Schmidt?
items.sentence_translation: What is your last name, Mr. Schmidt?
items.grammar_tip: Nachname is masculine: der Nachname.

items.sentence_de: Ich habe eine Nachricht für dich erhalten.
items.sentence_translation: I received a message for you.
items.grammar_tip: Nachricht is feminine: die Nachricht.

items.sentence_de: Ich sehe jeden Abend die Nachrichten.
items.sentence_translation: I watch the news every evening.
items.grammar_tip: In the plural, Nachrichten usually refers to the news broadcast.

items.sentence_de: Bitte sprechen Sie den Satz nach.
items.sentence_translation: Please repeat the sentence.
items.grammar_tip: Separable verb: 'Sprechen Sie mir nach'.

items.sentence_de: Die nächste Haltestelle ist der Bahnhof.
items.sentence_translation: The next stop is the train station.
items.grammar_tip: Adjective endings change based on the following noun's gender.

items.sentence_de: In der Nacht schlafen alle Leute.
items.sentence_translation: Everyone sleeps during the night.
items.grammar_tip: Gute Nacht! (Feminine noun).

items.sentence_de: Das ist ein großer Nachteil für uns.
items.sentence_translation: That is a big disadvantage for us.
items.grammar_tip: Opposite of Vorteil (advantage).

items.sentence_de: Es ist nachts sehr ruhig in der Stadt.
items.sentence_translation: It is very quiet in the city at night.
items.grammar_tip: Adverb used to describe regular occurrences at night.

items.sentence_de: In der Nähe gibt es einen Supermarkt.
items.sentence_translation: There is a supermarket nearby.
items.grammar_tip: Use 'in der Nähe' to say 'nearby'.

items.sentence_de: Die Telefonnummer beginnt mit einer null.
items.sentence_translation: The phone number starts with a zero.
items.grammar_tip: Numbers are usually treated as feminine when used as nouns (die Null).

items.sentence_de: Meine Nase ist rot vom kalten Wetter.
items.sentence_translation: My nose is red from the cold weather.
items.grammar_tip: Nase is feminine (die Nase).

items.sentence_de: Wir wandern gerne in der Natur.
items.sentence_translation: We like hiking in nature.
items.grammar_tip: Natur is a feminine noun.

items.sentence_de: Kannst du mir helfen? – Ja, natürlich!
items.sentence_translation: Can you help me? – Yes, of course!
items.grammar_tip: Used as an adverb to signal agreement.

items.sentence_de: Die Post ist direkt neben der Bank.
items.sentence_translation: The post office is right next to the bank.
items.grammar_tip: Two-way preposition (Wechselpräposition) using dative for location.

items.sentence_de: 'Kein' ist ein Negationsartikel im Deutschen.
items.sentence_translation: 'Kein' is a negative article in German.
items.grammar_tip: The main negative article in German is 'kein'.

items.sentence_de: Das Ergebnis des Tests war leider negativ.
items.sentence_translation: The result of the test was unfortunately negative.
items.grammar_tip: Opposite of positiv.

items.sentence_de: Ich brauche eine Nelke für das Rezept.
items.sentence_translation: I need a clove for the recipe.
items.grammar_tip: Nelke can mean the spice (clove) or the flower (carnation).

items.sentence_de: Kannst du mir ein Beispiel nennen?
items.sentence_translation: Can you name an example for me?
items.grammar_tip: Nennen is used to name or mention something.

items.sentence_de: Meine kleinen Geschwister nerven mich manchmal.
items.sentence_translation: My little siblings annoy me sometimes.
items.grammar_tip: Informal verb used for someone being irritating.

items.sentence_de: Unsere neue Lehrerin ist sehr nett.
items.sentence_translation: Our new teacher is very nice.
items.grammar_tip: Used to describe personality.

items.sentence_de: Im Tunnel habe ich leider kein Netz.
items.sentence_translation: In the tunnel I unfortunately have no reception.
items.grammar_tip: Netz can mean 'net' or mobile network signal.

items.sentence_de: Er ist seit heute neu im Club.
items.sentence_translation: He is new to the club as of today.
items.grammar_tip: 'Neu' is an adjective meaning new.

items.sentence_de: Wir ziehen bald in eine neue Wohnung.
items.sentence_translation: We are moving into a new apartment soon.
items.grammar_tip: Wohnung is feminine; adjectives take -e in nominative with die.

items.sentence_de: Das Kind ist heute neunzehn Jahre alt.
items.sentence_translation: The child is nineteen years old today.
items.grammar_tip: Formed by neun + zehn.

items.sentence_de: Das Buch kostet neunzig Euro.
items.sentence_translation: The book costs ninety euros.
items.grammar_tip: The suffix -zig is equivalent to -ty in English.

items.sentence_de: Dieses Wort ist im Deutschen neutral.
items.sentence_translation: This word is neuter in German.
items.grammar_tip: Used often in grammar for the 'das' gender.

items.sentence_de: Das Wort 'Kind' ist ein Neutrum.
items.sentence_translation: The word 'child' is a neuter.
items.grammar_tip: Refers to the third gender in German.

items.sentence_de: Ich habe Hunger, aber das Brot ist nicht mehr da.
items.sentence_translation: I am hungry, but the bread is no longer there.
items.grammar_tip: Indicates a finished state.

items.sentence_de: Er spielt nicht nur Klavier, sondern auch Gitarre.
items.sentence_translation: He doesn't only play the piano, but also the guitar.
items.grammar_tip: Often used with 'sondern auch' (but also).

items.sentence_de: Können Sie das bitte noch einmal sagen?
items.sentence_translation: Can you please say that once more?
items.grammar_tip: Commonly used when you didn't understand something.

items.sentence_de: Wie war Ihr Name bitte noch mal?
items.sentence_translation: What was your name again, please?
items.grammar_tip: Short/informal version of 'noch einmal'.

items.sentence_de: Nomen werden im Deutschen immer großgeschrieben.
items.sentence_translation: Nouns are always capitalized in German.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns are the names of things, people, or places.

items.sentence_de: Das Subjekt steht im Satz im Nominativ.
items.sentence_translation: The subject in the sentence is in the nominative.
items.grammar_tip: The basic case for the subject.

items.sentence_de: Hamburg liegt im Norden von Deutschland.
items.sentence_translation: Hamburg is located in the north of Germany.
items.grammar_tip: Compass directions are masculine (der Norden).

items.sentence_de: Normalerweise stehe ich um sieben Uhr auf.
items.sentence_translation: Normally I get up at seven o'clock.
items.grammar_tip: Standard frequency adverb.

items.sentence_de: Rufen Sie bitte schnell einen Notarzt!
items.sentence_translation: Please call an emergency doctor quickly!
items.grammar_tip: Used for urgent medical help.

items.sentence_de: Die Notärztin ist in fünf Minuten hier.
items.sentence_translation: The emergency doctor (f) will be here in five minutes.
items.grammar_tip: Feminine version of Notarzt.

items.sentence_de: Bitte notieren Sie sich die Telefonnummer.
items.sentence_translation: Please note down the phone number.
items.grammar_tip: A regular -ieren verb (no 'ge-' in past participle).

items.sentence_de: Ich schreibe eine kurze Notiz für dich.
items.sentence_translation: I'm writing a short note for you.
items.grammar_tip: Die Notiz is feminine.

items.sentence_de: Im November regnet es oft in Berlin.
items.sentence_translation: In November it often rains in Berlin.
items.grammar_tip: Months are always masculine.

items.sentence_de: Ich esse am liebsten eine Nudel mit Soße.
items.sentence_translation: I like eating a noodle with sauce best.
items.grammar_tip: Commonly used in plural: Nudeln (pasta).

items.sentence_de: Bitte nummerieren Sie die Sätze von eins bis fünf.
items.sentence_translation: Please number the sentences from one to five.
items.grammar_tip: Refers to putting numbers in order.

items.sentence_de: Wir haben nur noch zwei Eier im Kühlschrank.
items.sentence_translation: We only have two eggs left in the fridge.
items.grammar_tip: Used to emphasize a small remaining amount.

items.sentence_de: Möchtest du einen Tee oder einen Kaffee?
items.sentence_translation: Would you like a tea or a coffee?
items.grammar_tip: Conjunction used to present alternatives.

items.sentence_de: Das Fenster ist im Zimmer noch offen.
items.sentence_translation: The window in the room is still open.
items.grammar_tip: Used for doors, windows, and shops.

items.sentence_de: Das ist eine offizielle Einladung zur Party.
items.sentence_translation: This is an official invitation to the party.
items.grammar_tip: Often used for documents or formal events.

items.sentence_de: Ich bin am Wochenende meistens offline.
items.sentence_translation: I am mostly offline on the weekend.
items.grammar_tip: Borrowed from English.

items.sentence_de: Wie sind die Öffnungszeiten vom Supermarkt?
items.sentence_translation: What are the opening hours of the supermarket?
items.grammar_tip: Always used in the plural.

items.sentence_de: Mein linkes Ohr tut ein bisschen weh.
items.sentence_translation: My left ear hurts a little bit.
items.grammar_tip: The plural is 'die Ohren'.

items.sentence_de: Alles klar, das ist für mich okay.
items.sentence_translation: Everything clear, that is okay with me.
items.grammar_tip: Universal expression of agreement.

items.sentence_de: Der Oktober bringt oft bunte Blätter.
items.sentence_translation: October often brings colorful leaves.
items.grammar_tip: All months are masculine.

items.sentence_de: Ich brauche ein bisschen Öl zum Kochen.
items.sentence_translation: I need a little bit of oil for cooking.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns for liquids like 'Öl' or 'Milch' are often used without a plural in general contexts.

items.sentence_de: Ich esse gerne eine Olive zum Salat.
items.sentence_translation: I like to eat an olive with my salad.
items.grammar_tip: Feminine nouns ending in -e usually add -n in the plural.

items.sentence_de: Mein Onkel wohnt in einer anderen Stadt.
items.sentence_translation: My uncle lives in another city.
items.grammar_tip: The plural of 'Onkel' is the same as the singular, only the article changes.

items.sentence_de: Ich kaufe meine Kleidung oft online ein.
items.sentence_translation: I often buy my clothes online.
items.grammar_tip: 'Online' is an adverb/adjective borrowed from English and does not change its form.

items.sentence_de: Wir gehen heute Abend ins Open-Air-Kino.
items.sentence_translation: We are going to the open-air cinema tonight.
items.grammar_tip: Compound words ending in '-Kino' always take the neuter article 'das'.

items.sentence_de: Besuchen Sie oft die Oper in Berlin?
items.sentence_translation: Do you often visit the opera in Berlin?
items.grammar_tip: 'Oper' is feminine; nouns ending in -er are often masculine, but this is an exception.

items.sentence_de: Das neue Hemd von Markus ist orange.
items.sentence_translation: Markus's new shirt is orange.
items.grammar_tip: Color names like 'orange' or 'lila' often remain indeclinable in spoken German.

items.sentence_de: Möchten Sie zum Frühstück einen Orangensaft trinken?
items.sentence_translation: Would you like to drink an orange juice for breakfast?
items.grammar_tip: Compound nouns take the gender of the last word (der Saft -> der Orangensaft).

items.sentence_de: Mein Bruder spielt Geige in einem Orchester.
items.sentence_translation: My brother plays violin in an orchestra.
items.grammar_tip: The plural of 'Orchester' is identical to the singular form.

items.sentence_de: Heute lernen wir im Deutschkurs die Ordinalzahl.
items.sentence_translation: Today we are learning the ordinal number in the German course.
items.grammar_tip: Ordinal numbers (1st, 2nd) are used for dates in German.

items.sentence_de: Bitte ordnen Sie die Wörter nach dem Alphabet.
items.sentence_translation: Please arrange the words according to the alphabet.
items.grammar_tip: The verb stem ends in -n, so the 'du' and 'er/sie/es' forms add an 'e' for easier pronunciation (du ordnest).

items.sentence_de: In einer fremden Stadt muss man sich orientieren.
items.sentence_translation: In a strange city, one must orient oneself.
items.grammar_tip: This is a reflexive verb; it always needs a reflexive pronoun like 'mich', 'dich', or 'sich'.

items.sentence_de: Deine Idee für das Geschenk ist wirklich originell.
items.sentence_translation: Your idea for the gift is really original.
items.grammar_tip: 'Originell' is an adjective used to describe something creative or unique.

items.sentence_de: Die Präposition 'in' ist eine wichtige Ortsangabe.
items.sentence_translation: The preposition 'in' is an important indication of location.
items.grammar_tip: 'Ort' (place) + 'Angabe' (information) = location/place indication.

items.sentence_de: Verben der Ortsveränderung nutzen meistens das Hilfsverb 'sein'.
items.sentence_translation: Verbs of change of location mostly use the auxiliary verb 'sein'.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -ung are always feminine.

items.sentence_de: Die Sonne geht morgens im Osten auf.
items.sentence_translation: The sun rises in the East in the morning.
items.grammar_tip: Compass directions (Norden, Süden, Osten, Westen) are always masculine.

items.sentence_de: Ich mache diesen Sommer Urlaub in Österreich.
items.sentence_translation: I am going on vacation in Austria this summer.
items.grammar_tip: Most countries like 'Österreich' do not use an article unless they are feminine or plural.

items.sentence_de: Ich kaufe mir ein neues Paar Schuhe.
items.sentence_translation: I am buying myself a new pair of shoes.
items.grammar_tip: 'Ein paar' (lowercase) means 'a few', while 'ein Paar' (uppercase) means 'a pair'.

items.sentence_de: Ich muss heute Abend noch meinen Koffer packen.
items.sentence_translation: I still have to pack my suitcase tonight.
items.grammar_tip: 'Packen' is a regular weak verb in the present tense.

items.sentence_de: Ich kaufe eine Packung Nudeln im Supermarkt.
items.sentence_translation: I am buying a packet of pasta at the supermarket.
items.grammar_tip: Commonly used for food packaging like pasta, rice, or cigarettes.

items.sentence_de: Die Post bringt mir heute ein großes Paket.
items.sentence_translation: The post is bringing me a big package today.
items.grammar_tip: 'Das Paket' refers to a parcel, while 'die Packung' is usually for smaller store packaging.

items.sentence_de: Wir spielen gerne Pantomime auf der Party.
items.sentence_translation: We like to play pantomime at the party.
items.grammar_tip: The word can refer to the performance or the actor.

items.sentence_de: Das Parfüm riecht sehr gut und blumig.
items.sentence_translation: The perfume smells very good and flowery.
items.grammar_tip: French loanwords in German often take the neuter article 'das'.

items.sentence_de: In der Parfümerie kann man teure Düfte kaufen.
items.sentence_translation: In the perfumery, one can buy expensive scents.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -ie are usually feminine and stressed on the last syllable.

items.sentence_de: Wir spazieren am Sonntag oft im Park.
items.sentence_translation: We often walk in the park on Sunday.
items.grammar_tip: 'Im' is a contraction of 'in dem' (Dative case for location).

items.sentence_de: Das Partizip II benutzt man für das Perfekt.
items.sentence_translation: The participle II is used for the perfect tense.
items.grammar_tip: Grammatical terms ending in -ip often take the 'das' article.

items.sentence_de: Mein Partner arbeitet bei einer großen Firma.
items.sentence_translation: My partner works at a large company.
items.grammar_tip: Masculine profession/role nouns ending in -er usually have the same plural form.

items.sentence_de: Meine Partnerin kommt aus der Schweiz.
items.sentence_translation: My partner comes from Switzerland.
items.grammar_tip: Add -in to the masculine form to make it feminine; the plural then ends in -innen.

items.sentence_de: Ich brauche meinen Pass für die Reise.
items.sentence_translation: I need my passport for the trip.
items.grammar_tip: Don't confuse 'Pass' (passport) with 'Spaß' (fun).

items.sentence_de: Welches Bild passt zu welchem Text?
items.sentence_translation: Which picture matches which text?
items.grammar_tip: 'Passen' is followed by the preposition 'zu' + Dative when meaning 'to match'.

items.sentence_de: Ich suche ein passend Kleidung für die Hochzeit.
items.sentence_translation: I am looking for matching clothing for the wedding.
items.grammar_tip: This is the present participle of 'passen', used as an adjective.

items.sentence_de: Was ist gestern auf der Straße passiert?
items.sentence_translation: What happened on the street yesterday?
items.grammar_tip: Verbs ending in -ieren do not use the 'ge-' prefix in the Partizip II (passiert).

items.sentence_de: Ich habe mein Passwort leider vergessen.
items.sentence_translation: Unfortunately, I have forgotten my password.
items.grammar_tip: Compound noun: 'Pass' + 'Wort'. Neuter because 'Wort' is neuter.

items.sentence_de: Der Patient wartet schon seit einer Stunde.
items.sentence_translation: The patient has been waiting for an hour already.
items.grammar_tip: This is an N-declension noun; it adds -en in all cases except nominative singular.

items.sentence_de: Die Patientin spricht gerade mit dem Arzt.
items.sentence_translation: The patient is speaking with the doctor right now.
items.grammar_tip: Feminine version of 'Patient'.

items.sentence_de: Oh nein, mein Handy ist kaputt. So ein Pech!
items.sentence_translation: Oh no, my phone is broken. Such bad luck!
items.grammar_tip: 'Viel Glück!' is the opposite of 'Pech haben'.

items.sentence_de: Wir übernachten in einer kleinen Pension am See.
items.sentence_translation: We are staying in a small guesthouse by the lake.
items.grammar_tip: A 'Pension' is usually cheaper and smaller than a 'Hotel'.

items.sentence_de: Dein Deutsch ist schon fast perfekt!
items.sentence_translation: Your German is already almost perfect!
items.grammar_tip: Used just like the English word 'perfect'.

items.sentence_de: Im A1 Kurs lernen wir das Perfekt.
items.sentence_translation: In the A1 course we learn the perfect tense.
items.grammar_tip: The most common past tense used in spoken German.

items.sentence_de: Wie viele Personen kommen zu der Party?
items.sentence_translation: How many persons are coming to the party?
items.grammar_tip: 'Person' is always feminine, regardless of the gender of the human it refers to.

items.sentence_de: 'Ich' und 'du' sind wichtige Personalpronomen.
items.sentence_translation: 'I' and 'you' are important personal pronouns.
items.grammar_tip: Compound: 'Personal' + 'Pronomen'.

items.sentence_de: Ich möchte das gerne persönlich mit dir besprechen.
items.sentence_translation: I would like to discuss that with you personally.
items.grammar_tip: Derived from 'Person'. Used to mean 'in person' or 'private'.

items.sentence_de: Salz und Pfeffer stehen auf dem Tisch.
items.sentence_translation: Salt and pepper are on the table.
items.grammar_tip: Like 'Salz', it is typically used in the singular.

items.sentence_de: Diese grüne Pflanze braucht viel Wasser.
items.sentence_translation: This green plant needs a lot of water.
items.grammar_tip: Feminine nouns ending in -e are very common in German.

items.sentence_de: Hast du ein Pflaster für meinen Finger?
items.sentence_translation: Do you have a band-aid for my finger?
items.grammar_tip: Neuter noun; plural is the same as singular.

items.sentence_de: Der Physiotherapeut hilft mir nach dem Unfall.
items.sentence_translation: The physical therapist helps me after the accident.
items.grammar_tip: Follows the N-declension (den/dem Physiotherapeuten).

items.sentence_de: Die Physiotherapeutin zeigt mir neue Übungen.
items.sentence_translation: The physical therapist shows me new exercises.
items.grammar_tip: Feminine professional noun ending in -in.

items.sentence_de: Ich habe morgen einen Termin bei der Physiotherapie.
items.sentence_translation: I have an appointment at the physical therapy tomorrow.
items.grammar_tip: Feminine noun, stress is on the final '-ie'.

items.sentence_de: Wollen wir am Samstag ein Picknick machen?
items.sentence_translation: Do we want to have a picnic on Saturday?
items.grammar_tip: In German, you 'make' (machen) a picnic.

items.sentence_de: Ich bestelle eine Pizza mit viel Käse.
items.sentence_translation: I am ordering a pizza with a lot of cheese.
items.grammar_tip: The plural is 'Pizzen' or sometimes 'Pizzas'.

items.sentence_de: Das Plakat an der Wand ist sehr schön.
items.sentence_translation: The poster on the wall is very beautiful.
items.grammar_tip: Neuter noun; the plural adds -e.

items.sentence_de: Hast du schon einen Plan für das Wochenende?
items.sentence_translation: Do you already have a plan for the weekend?
items.grammar_tip: 'Einen Plan haben' is a very common expression.

items.sentence_de: Wir planen gerade unsere Reise nach Deutschland.
items.sentence_translation: We are currently planning our trip to Germany.
items.grammar_tip: Regular verb. The root is 'plan-'.

items.sentence_de: In der Klinik ist Platz für viele Patienten.
items.sentence_translation: There is space for many patients in the clinic.
items.grammar_tip: 'Platz' can mean space, room, a square in a city, or a seat.

items.sentence_de: Wie heißt das Wort im Plural?
items.sentence_translation: What is the word in the plural?
items.grammar_tip: Grammatical term for more than one.

items.sentence_de: Die Pluralendung von 'Hund' ist '-e'.
items.sentence_translation: The plural ending of 'Hund' is '-e'.
items.grammar_tip: Feminine noun ending in -ung.

items.sentence_de: Suchen Sie die richtige Pluralform im Wörterbuch.
items.sentence_translation: Look for the correct plural form in the dictionary.
items.grammar_tip: Compound: 'Plural' + 'Form'. All nouns ending in -form are feminine.

items.sentence_de: Zwei plus zwei ist gleich vier.
items.sentence_translation: Two plus two equals four.
items.grammar_tip: Used for addition in math.

items.sentence_de: Polen ist ein Nachbarland von Deutschland.
items.sentence_translation: Poland is a neighboring country of Germany.
items.grammar_tip: No article used for this country name.

items.sentence_de: Er interessiert sich sehr für internationale Politik.
items.sentence_translation: He is very interested in international politics.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -ik are typically feminine and singular only.

items.sentence_de: Der Polizist fragt nach meinem Ausweis.
items.sentence_translation: The police officer asks for my ID.
items.grammar_tip: N-declension: 'Ich sehe den Polizisten'.

items.sentence_de: Eine Polizistin steht an der Kreuzung.
items.sentence_translation: A female police officer is standing at the intersection.
items.grammar_tip: Feminine form of 'Polizist'.

items.sentence_de: Sprichst du Polnisch oder nur Deutsch?
items.sentence_translation: Do you speak Polish or only German?
items.grammar_tip: Languages in German are usually treated as neuter nouns but used without an article.

items.sentence_de: Ich hätte gerne ein Schnitzel mit Pommes.
items.sentence_translation: I would like a schnitzel with fries.
items.grammar_tip: Short for 'Pommes frites'; almost always used in the plural.

items.sentence_de: Fußball ist ein sehr populär Sport in Deutschland.
items.sentence_translation: Football is a very popular sport in Germany.
items.grammar_tip: A synonym for 'beliebt'.

items.sentence_de: Lissabon ist die Hauptstadt von Portugal.
items.sentence_translation: Lisbon is the capital of Portugal.
items.grammar_tip: Country name, neuter gender, usually no article.

items.sentence_de: In Brasilien spricht man auch Portugiesisch.
items.sentence_translation: In Brazil, people also speak Portuguese.
items.grammar_tip: Language name.

items.sentence_de: Das Verb steht meistens auf Position zwei.
items.sentence_translation: The verb is usually in position two.
items.grammar_tip: Used often in grammar to describe word order.

items.sentence_de: Das Ergebnis vom Test war zum Glück positiv.
items.sentence_translation: The result of the test was fortunately positive.
items.grammar_tip: Used for results or attitudes.

items.sentence_de: 'Mein' und 'dein' nennt man Possessivartikel.
items.sentence_translation: 'My' and 'your' are called possessive articles.
items.grammar_tip: Indicates possession or belonging.

items.sentence_de: Ich schreibe eine Postkarte aus dem Urlaub.
items.sentence_translation: I am writing a postcard from my vacation.
items.grammar_tip: Compound: 'Post' + 'Karte'.

items.sentence_de: Das Präfix 'ver-' ändert die Bedeutung.
items.sentence_translation: The prefix 'ver-' changes the meaning.
items.grammar_tip: A word part added to the beginning of a stem.

items.sentence_de: Ich mache im Sommer ein Praktikum bei Siemens.
items.sentence_translation: I am doing an internship at Siemens in the summer.
items.grammar_tip: The plural is irregular: 'Praktika'.

items.sentence_de: Dieses kleine Messer ist sehr praktisch für unterwegs.
items.sentence_translation: This small knife is very practical for on the go.
items.grammar_tip: Used to describe something useful.

items.sentence_de: Nach der Präposition 'mit' kommt immer der Dativ.
items.sentence_translation: After the preposition 'mit' always comes the dative.
items.grammar_tip: Small words like 'in', 'an', 'zu' that show relationships.

items.sentence_de: Die Präsentation war sehr interessant und klar.
items.sentence_translation: The presentation was very interesting and clear.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -tion are always feminine in German.

items.sentence_de: Heute präsentieren wir unsere neuen Ergebnisse.
items.sentence_translation: Today we are presenting our new results.
items.grammar_tip: Regular verbs in the plural 'wir' form usually end in -en.

items.sentence_de: Wir lernen heute das Präteritum im Unterricht.
items.sentence_translation: We are learning the simple past in class today.
items.grammar_tip: The Präteritum is more common in written German than spoken German.

items.sentence_de: Die Praxis ist am Wochenende leider geschlossen.
items.sentence_translation: The surgery is unfortunately closed on the weekend.
items.grammar_tip: Praxis refers to a doctor's office or medical practice.

items.sentence_de: Die Äpfel kosten zwei Euro pro Kilo.
items.sentence_translation: The apples cost two euros per kilo.
items.grammar_tip: 'Pro' is used exactly like 'per' for unit prices or rates.

items.sentence_de: Möchten Sie das Stück Käse einmal probieren?
items.sentence_translation: Would you like to try the piece of cheese?
items.grammar_tip: Use 'probieren' for tasting food or trying an action.

items.sentence_de: Dieses Produkt ist sehr gut für die Haut.
items.sentence_translation: This product is very good for the skin.
items.grammar_tip: Neuter nouns often end in -t; the plural adds -e.

items.sentence_de: Die Produktion findet in dieser großen Fabrik statt.
items.sentence_translation: The production takes place in this large factory.
items.grammar_tip: Like many -tion nouns, this refers to the process or industry.

items.sentence_de: Mein Professor ist sehr freundlich und hilft viel.
items.sentence_translation: My professor is very friendly and helps a lot.
items.grammar_tip: Masculine professions usually don't have a suffix.

items.sentence_de: Die Professorin erklärt die schwierige Aufgabe noch einmal.
items.sentence_translation: The professor is explaining the difficult task once more.
items.grammar_tip: Add -in to the masculine form to make it feminine.

items.sentence_de: Ich muss mein Profil im Internet aktualisieren.
items.sentence_translation: I have to update my profile on the internet.
items.grammar_tip: German uses 'Profil' for social media and online accounts.

items.sentence_de: Welches Programm benutzt du für die Arbeit?
items.sentence_translation: Which program are you using for work?
items.grammar_tip: This can mean a computer program or a TV schedule.

items.sentence_de: Wir arbeiten gemeinsam an einem neuen Projekt.
items.sentence_translation: We are working together on a new project.
items.grammar_tip: The plural of Projekt is Projekte.

items.sentence_de: Personalpronomen sind Wörter wie ich, du, er.
items.sentence_translation: Personal pronouns are words like I, you, he.
items.grammar_tip: In German, grammar terms are often neuter.

items.sentence_de: Wir trinken ein Bier, also sagen wir: prost!
items.sentence_translation: We are drinking a beer, so we say: cheers!
items.grammar_tip: Use 'Prost' when clinking glasses with friends.

items.sentence_de: Das Publikum klatscht nach dem Konzert laut.
items.sentence_translation: The audience claps loudly after the concert.
items.grammar_tip: This refers to the collective group of viewers.

items.sentence_de: Dein blauer Pulli sieht sehr bequem aus.
items.sentence_translation: Your blue pullover looks very comfortable.
items.grammar_tip: 'Pulli' is the short, casual form of 'Pullover'.

items.sentence_de: Im Winter trage ich jeden Tag einen Pullover.
items.sentence_translation: In winter I wear a jumper every day.
items.grammar_tip: The plural 'die Pullover' remains the same as the singular.

items.sentence_de: Am Ende des Satzes steht ein Punkt.
items.sentence_translation: At the end of the sentence is a period.
items.grammar_tip: 'Punkt' is also used for 'point' or 'item' on a list.

items.sentence_de: Pünktlichkeit ist in Deutschland sehr wichtig.
items.sentence_translation: Punctuality is very important in Germany.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -keit are always feminine.

items.sentence_de: Die Wohnung ist insgesamt achtzig qm groß.
items.sentence_translation: The apartment is eighty square meters in total.
items.grammar_tip: Abbreviation for Quadratmeter, used in housing ads.

items.sentence_de: Erzähl keinen Quatsch, das stimmt doch gar nicht!
items.sentence_translation: Don't talk nonsense, that isn't true at all!
items.grammar_tip: A common colloquial term for 'rubbish' or 'nonsense'.

items.sentence_de: Ich höre morgens immer eine interessante Radiosendung.
items.sentence_translation: I always listen to an interesting radio programme in the morning.
items.grammar_tip: Compounds with -ung are always feminine.

items.sentence_de: Kannst du das Rätsel auf dem Ratebild lösen?
items.sentence_translation: Can you solve the riddle on the picture puzzle?
items.grammar_tip: A compound of 'raten' (guess) and 'Bild' (picture).

items.sentence_de: Kannst du mein Alter richtig raten?
items.sentence_translation: Can you guess my age correctly?
items.grammar_tip: 'Raten' is an irregular verb: rät, riet, hat geraten.

items.sentence_de: Ich muss für den Ausweis zum Rathaus gehen.
items.sentence_translation: I have to go to the town hall for the ID.
items.grammar_tip: Compound of 'Rat' (council) and 'Haus' (house).

items.sentence_de: In der Schweiz spricht man auch Rätoromanisch.
items.sentence_translation: In Switzerland, they also speak Raetho-Romanic.
items.grammar_tip: Languages in German are usually neuter but used without articles.

items.sentence_de: Der Raum ist groß genug für das Treffen.
items.sentence_translation: The room is large enough for the meeting.
items.grammar_tip: Used for physical rooms/spaces, often in offices.

items.sentence_de: Bei schönem Wetter möchte ich gern rausgehen.
items.sentence_translation: In nice weather, I would like to go outside.
items.grammar_tip: A separable verb: 'Ich gehe heute Abend raus.'

items.sentence_de: Man muss schnell auf die E-Mail reagieren.
items.sentence_translation: One must react quickly to the email.
items.grammar_tip: Verbs ending in -ieren don't use 'ge-' in the past participle.

items.sentence_de: Seine Reaktion auf das Geschenk war sehr positiv.
items.sentence_translation: His reaction to the gift was very positive.
items.grammar_tip: Like all -tion nouns, it is feminine.

items.sentence_de: Es gab viele verschiedene Reaktionen auf den Film.
items.sentence_translation: There were many different reactions to the movie.
items.grammar_tip: Plural of Reaktion.

items.sentence_de: Wir müssen für die Hausaufgabe im Internet recherchieren.
items.sentence_translation: We have to research on the internet for the homework.
items.grammar_tip: Commonly used for looking up information.

items.sentence_de: Diese Redemittel helfen mir beim Sprechen sehr.
items.sentence_translation: These useful phrases help me a lot when speaking.
items.grammar_tip: Literal translation is 'means of speech'.

items.sentence_de: Wir müssen unbedingt über das Problem reden.
items.sentence_translation: We absolutely must talk about the problem.
items.grammar_tip: Similar to 'sprechen' but often more informal or focused on discussion.

items.sentence_de: Die Bücher stehen oben im großen Regal.
items.sentence_translation: The books are up in the large shelf.
items.grammar_tip: The plural is 'Regale'.

items.sentence_de: Man muss im Verkehr jede Regel beachten.
items.sentence_translation: One must follow every rule in traffic.
items.grammar_tip: Plural: Regeln.

items.sentence_de: Ich treibe regelmäßig Sport, meistens dreimal pro Woche.
items.sentence_translation: I do sports regularly, usually three times a week.
items.grammar_tip: This adverb describes a repeated routine.

items.sentence_de: Nimm deine Regenjacke mit, es regnet heute.
items.sentence_translation: Take your rain coat with you, it's raining today.
items.grammar_tip: Compound noun: Regen (rain) + Jacke (jacket).

items.sentence_de: Ich habe meinen Regenschirm im Bus vergessen.
items.sentence_translation: I forgot my umbrella on the bus.
items.grammar_tip: Schirm means 'screen' or 'shield'.

items.sentence_de: Der Regisseur gibt den Schauspielern neue Anweisungen.
items.sentence_translation: The director gives the actors new instructions.
items.grammar_tip: This refers to a film or theater director.

items.sentence_de: Die Regisseurin hat einen Preis für ihren Film gewonnen.
items.sentence_translation: The director won a prize for her movie.
items.grammar_tip: Feminine form of Regisseur.

items.sentence_de: Bitte bringen Sie die Sätze in die richtige Reihenfolge.
items.sentence_translation: Please put the sentences in the correct sequence.
items.grammar_tip: Commonly used in exercises to order items.

items.sentence_de: Wir wohnen in einem kleinen Reihenhaus mit Garten.
items.sentence_translation: We live in a small townhouse with a garden.
items.grammar_tip: 'Reihe' means row, so it's a 'row house'.

items.sentence_de: Ich lese gern einen spannenden Reisebericht über Italien.
items.sentence_translation: I like to read an exciting travelogue about Italy.
items.grammar_tip: Compound: Reise (travel) + Bericht (report).

items.sentence_de: Unsere Reiseführerin zeigt uns die alten Kirchen.
items.sentence_translation: Our travel guide is showing us the old churches.
items.grammar_tip: Refers to the person (female), not the book.

items.sentence_de: Ich packe meine Kleidung in die große Reisetasche.
items.sentence_translation: I am packing my clothes into the large holdall.
items.grammar_tip: Compound: Reise (travel) + Tasche (bag).

items.sentence_de: Spanien ist ein sehr beliebtes Reiseziel im Sommer.
items.sentence_translation: Spain is a very popular travel destination in summer.
items.grammar_tip: Ziel means 'goal' or 'destination'.

items.sentence_de: Es gibt viele schöne Reiseziele in Deutschland für Touristen.
items.sentence_translation: There are many beautiful travel destinations in Germany for tourists.
items.grammar_tip: 'In' is used for countries without articles.

items.sentence_de: In der Schule sprechen wir über verschiedene Religionen.
items.sentence_translation: In school we talk about different religions.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -ion are feminine.

items.sentence_de: Die Wohnung ist frisch renoviert und sehr sauber.
items.sentence_translation: The apartment is freshly refurbished and very clean.
items.grammar_tip: This is the past participle of the verb 'renovieren'.

items.sentence_de: Wir hören in der Kirche ein bekanntes Requiem.
items.sentence_translation: We are listening to a famous requiem in the church.
items.grammar_tip: A musical or religious composition for the dead.

items.sentence_de: Ich möchte gern einen Tisch für heute reservieren.
items.sentence_translation: I would like to book a table for today.
items.grammar_tip: Used for tables, rooms, or tickets.

items.sentence_de: Der Arzt schreibt mir ein Rezept für Medikamente.
items.sentence_translation: The doctor is writing me a prescription for medicine.
items.grammar_tip: 'Rezept' can mean both a medical prescription and a cooking recipe.

items.sentence_de: Die Blumen im Garten riechen wirklich sehr gut.
items.sentence_translation: The flowers in the garden smell really very good.
items.grammar_tip: Irregular: riecht, roch, hat gerochen.

items.sentence_de: Sie trägt heute einen kurzen, roten Rock.
items.sentence_translation: She is wearing a short, red skirt today.
items.grammar_tip: Don't confuse this with the music genre 'Rock'.

items.sentence_de: Er spielt die wichtigste Rolle in diesem Theaterstück.
items.sentence_translation: He plays the most important role in this play.
items.grammar_tip: Used for actors or functions in a group.

items.sentence_de: Zieh bitte eine Rollenkarte für das nächste Spiel.
items.sentence_translation: Please pull a role card for the next game.
items.grammar_tip: Used in language classes for role-play exercises.

items.sentence_de: Die Ampel ist rot, wir müssen jetzt warten.
items.sentence_translation: The traffic light is red, we must wait now.
items.grammar_tip: Basic color adjective.

items.sentence_de: Das Navi zeigt uns die schnellste Route an.
items.sentence_translation: The GPS shows us the fastest route.
items.grammar_tip: Pronounced like the French 'route'.

items.sentence_de: Mein Rücken tut nach der Arbeit oft weh.
items.sentence_translation: My back often hurts after work.
items.grammar_tip: The plural is identical to the singular: die Rücken.

items.sentence_de: Ich habe Rückenschmerzen, weil ich zu viel sitze.
items.sentence_translation: I have back pain because I sit too much.
items.grammar_tip: Always used in plural when referring to the condition.

items.sentence_de: In der Schule sind rund eintausend Schüler angemeldet.
items.sentence_translation: Around a thousand students are enrolled in the school.
items.grammar_tip: Used here to mean 'approximately'.

items.sentence_de: Wir lernen heute alles rund um das Thema Essen.
items.sentence_translation: Today we are learning everything all about the topic of food.
items.grammar_tip: Used to describe a general topic area.

items.sentence_de: Kannst du Russisch sprechen oder nur ein bisschen?
items.sentence_translation: Can you speak Russian or only a little bit?
items.grammar_tip: Language names are usually neuter and end in -isch.

items.sentence_de: Russland ist flächenmäßig das größte Land der Welt.
items.sentence_translation: Russia is the largest country in the world by area.
items.grammar_tip: Most countries are neuter and used without an article.

items.sentence_de: Ich muss meine Sachen für den Urlaub packen.
items.sentence_translation: I have to pack my things for the vacation.
items.grammar_tip: 'Dinge' is a synonym, but 'Sachen' is very common for personal items.

items.sentence_de: Möchten Sie Ihren Kaffee mit oder ohne Sahne?
items.sentence_translation: Would you like your coffee with or without cream?
items.grammar_tip: Usually refers to heavy/whipping cream.

items.sentence_de: Die Erdbeeren haben im Sommer ihre wichtigste Saison.
items.sentence_translation: Strawberries have their most important season in summer.
items.grammar_tip: Refers to a specific period of time (sports, harvest), not weather seasons (Jahreszeiten).

items.sentence_de: Er arbeitet im Winter als Skilehrer im Saison-Job.
items.sentence_translation: He works as a ski instructor in a seasonal job in winter.
items.grammar_tip: A job only available during a specific season.

items.sentence_de: Ich hätte gern zwei Scheiben Salami auf mein Brot.
items.sentence_translation: I would like two slices of salami on my bread.
items.grammar_tip: A very popular type of sausage in Germany.

items.sentence_de: Diese Salbe hilft sehr gut gegen den Ausschlag.
items.sentence_translation: This salve helps very well against the rash.
items.grammar_tip: A medicinal cream for the skin.

items.sentence_de: Mein Bruder möchte alte Münzen aus aller Welt sammeln.
items.sentence_translation: My brother wants to collect old coins from all over the world.
items.grammar_tip: The 'e' before 'l' is often dropped in the 'ich' form: ich sammle.

items.sentence_de: Am Samstag gehen wir oft zusammen im Park spazieren.
items.sentence_translation: On Saturday we often go for a walk together in the park.
items.grammar_tip: Days of the week are always masculine.

items.sentence_de: Hast du am Samstagabend Zeit für einen Film?
items.sentence_translation: Do you have time for a movie on Saturday night?
items.grammar_tip: Compound noun: Samstag + Abend.

items.sentence_de: Ich gehe samstags oft ins Kino.
items.sentence_translation: I often go to the cinema on Saturdays.
items.grammar_tip: Adverbs of time ending in -s indicate a repeated action.

items.sentence_de: Ich bin nach dem Essen sehr satt.
items.sentence_translation: I am very full after the meal.
items.grammar_tip: Use 'satt' for being full from food, not 'voll'.

items.sentence_de: Schreiben Sie bitte einen kurzen Satz.
items.sentence_translation: Please write a short sentence.
items.grammar_tip: The plural of Satz is Sätze.

items.sentence_de: Der Punkt steht am Ende vom Satzende.
items.sentence_translation: The period is at the end of the sentence.
items.grammar_tip: Compound noun: das Ende + der Satz.

items.sentence_de: Die Verben bilden eine deutsche Satzklammer.
items.sentence_translation: The verbs form a German sentence bracket.
items.grammar_tip: This refers to the position of verbs in German syntax.

items.sentence_de: Die Satzmelodie ist bei Fragen sehr wichtig.
items.sentence_translation: Intonation is very important in questions.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -ie are usually feminine.

items.sentence_de: Die Küche muss heute sauber sein.
items.sentence_translation: The kitchen must be clean today.
items.grammar_tip: The opposite is 'schmutzig'.

items.sentence_de: Ich muss am Wochenende die Wohnung saubermachen.
items.sentence_translation: I have to clean the apartment on the weekend.
items.grammar_tip: A separable verb: ich mache sauber.

items.sentence_de: Er spielt jeden Tag auf seinem Saxofon.
items.sentence_translation: He plays on his saxophone every day.
items.grammar_tip: Musical instruments are often neuter.

items.sentence_de: Es ist schade, dass du nicht kommst.
items.sentence_translation: It is a pity that you are not coming.
items.grammar_tip: Often used alone as an exclamation: 'Schade!'

items.sentence_de: Wir schaffen die Arbeit bis heute Abend.
items.sentence_translation: We will manage the work by tonight.
items.grammar_tip: In A1, 'schaffen' means to succeed or complete a task.

items.sentence_de: Der Schaffner kontrolliert die Fahrkarten im Zug.
items.sentence_translation: The conductor checks the tickets on the train.
items.grammar_tip: Professional nouns ending in -er are usually masculine.

items.sentence_de: Die Schaffnerin hilft den Fahrgästen am Bahnsteig.
items.sentence_translation: The conductor helps the passengers on the platform.
items.grammar_tip: Add -in to the masculine form to make it feminine.

items.sentence_de: Im Winter trage ich einen warmen Schal.
items.sentence_translation: In winter I wear a warm scarf.
items.grammar_tip: The plural is formed with -s.

items.sentence_de: Kannst du bitte die Kartoffeln schälen?
items.sentence_translation: Can you please peel the potatoes?
items.grammar_tip: A regular weak verb.

items.sentence_de: Wir schauen heute Abend einen Film.
items.sentence_translation: We are watching a movie tonight.
items.grammar_tip: Used often in Southern Germany/Austria for 'sehen'.

items.sentence_de: Mein Lieblings-Schauspieler kommt aus Berlin.
items.sentence_translation: My favorite actor comes from Berlin.
items.grammar_tip: Compound noun: Schau (show) + Spieler (player).

items.sentence_de: Die Schauspielerin ist im Theater sehr bekannt.
items.sentence_translation: The actress is very well known in the theater.
items.grammar_tip: Feminine version of Schauspieler.

items.sentence_de: Die Sonne scheint heute den ganzen Tag.
items.sentence_translation: The sun is shining all day today.
items.grammar_tip: Irregular past: schien, hat geschienen.

items.sentence_de: Ich schenke meiner Mutter Blumen zum Geburtstag.
items.sentence_translation: I am giving my mother flowers for her birthday.
items.grammar_tip: Takes dative (receiver) and accusative (gift).

items.sentence_de: Das Schiff fährt über den großen See.
items.sentence_translation: The ship travels across the large lake.
items.grammar_tip: Das Schiff, die Schiffe.

items.sentence_de: Das Kind schläft nachts sehr gut.
items.sentence_translation: The child sleeps very well at night.
items.grammar_tip: Vowel change: a becomes ä in 2nd/3rd person singular.

items.sentence_de: Wir brauchen beim Camping einen warmen Schlafsack.
items.sentence_translation: We need a warm sleeping bag when camping.
items.grammar_tip: Compound: schlafen + Sack.

items.sentence_de: Der Arzt verschreibt mir eine Schlaftablette.
items.sentence_translation: The doctor prescribes me a sleeping pill.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -e are mostly feminine.

items.sentence_de: In meinem Schlafzimmer steht ein großes Bett.
items.sentence_translation: In my bedroom there is a big bed.
items.grammar_tip: Rooms ending in -zimmer are always neuter.

items.sentence_de: Bitte schließen Sie das Fenster, es zieht.
items.sentence_translation: Please close the window, there is a draft.
items.grammar_tip: Opposite of 'öffnen'.

items.sentence_de: Ich habe seit gestern einen starken Schmerz.
items.sentence_translation: I have had a strong pain since yesterday.
items.grammar_tip: Often used in plural: Schmerzen.

items.sentence_de: Sie trägt sehr teuren Schmuck aus Gold.
items.sentence_translation: She wears very expensive gold jewelry.
items.grammar_tip: Used mostly in the singular.

items.sentence_de: Draußen liegt im Winter sehr viel Schnee.
items.sentence_translation: There is a lot of snow outside in winter.
items.grammar_tip: Uncountable noun.

items.sentence_de: Er schneidet das Brot mit einem Messer.
items.sentence_translation: He cuts the bread with a knife.
items.grammar_tip: Strong verb: schneiden, schnitt, geschnitten.

items.sentence_de: Es wird morgen in den Bergen schneien.
items.sentence_translation: It will snow in the mountains tomorrow.
items.grammar_tip: Usually used with the impersonal 'es'.

items.sentence_de: Ich bestelle im Restaurant ein Wiener Schnitzel.
items.sentence_translation: I order a Wiener Schnitzel in the restaurant.
items.grammar_tip: Plural is the same as singular.

items.sentence_de: Ich habe im Winter oft einen Schnupfen.
items.sentence_translation: I often have a cold in winter.
items.grammar_tip: Literally 'the sniffles'.

items.sentence_de: Kinder essen sehr gerne süße Schokolade.
items.sentence_translation: Children like to eat sweet chocolate.
items.grammar_tip: Feminine noun ending in -e.

items.sentence_de: Es regnet heute leider schon wieder.
items.sentence_translation: Unfortunately, it is raining once again today.
items.grammar_tip: Indicates annoyance or repetition.

items.sentence_de: Die Gläser stehen oben im Schrank.
items.sentence_translation: The glasses are up in the cupboard.
items.grammar_tip: The plural is Schränke.

items.sentence_de: Das Wetter am Wochenende war einfach schrecklich.
items.sentence_translation: The weather on the weekend was simply terrible.
items.grammar_tip: Synonym for 'furchtbar'.

items.sentence_de: Ich schreibe meiner Oma einen Brief.
items.sentence_translation: I am writing a letter to my grandma.
items.grammar_tip: Strong verb: schreiben, schrieb, geschrieben.

items.sentence_de: Auf meinem Schreibtisch liegt ein Computer.
items.sentence_translation: A computer is lying on my desk.
items.grammar_tip: Compound: schreiben + Tisch.

items.sentence_de: Ich kaufe Stifte in der Abteilung für Schreibwaren.
items.sentence_translation: I buy pens in the stationery department.
items.grammar_tip: Mostly used in the plural.

items.sentence_de: Sie ist ein echter Schuhfan und kauft viele.
items.sentence_translation: She is a real shoe fan and buys many.
items.grammar_tip: Colloquial term for someone who loves shoes.

items.sentence_de: Wir gehen heute in den neuen Schuhladen.
items.sentence_translation: We are going to the new shoe shop today.
items.grammar_tip: Compound: Schuh + Laden.

items.sentence_de: Es regnet nicht nur, es schüttet!
items.sentence_translation: It's not just raining, it's pouring!
items.grammar_tip: Used for heavy rain.

items.sentence_de: Er trägt heute eine schwarze Hose.
items.sentence_translation: He is wearing black pants today.
items.grammar_tip: Colors are adjectives and change endings before nouns.

items.sentence_de: Ich mache Urlaub in der Schweiz.
items.sentence_translation: I am going on vacation in Switzerland.
items.grammar_tip: Always used with an article: die Schweiz.

items.sentence_de: Wir schwimmen im Sommer gerne im See.
items.sentence_translation: We like to swim in the lake in summer.
items.grammar_tip: Past participle uses 'sein': ist geschwommen.

items.sentence_de: Meine kleine Schwester ist schon sechzehn.
items.sentence_translation: My little sister is already sixteen.
items.grammar_tip: Note the spelling: the 's' in sechs is dropped.

items.sentence_de: Die Fahrkarte kostet genau sechzig Euro.
items.sentence_translation: The ticket costs exactly sixty euros.
items.grammar_tip: The suffix -zig denotes tens.

items.sentence_de: Ich kaufe meine Kleidung oft im Secondhand-Laden.
items.sentence_translation: I often buy my clothes at the secondhand shop.
items.grammar_tip: Loan word from English with German 'Laden'.

items.sentence_de: Der Segellehrer zeigt uns das Boot.
items.sentence_translation: The sailing instructor shows us the boat.
items.grammar_tip: Compound: segeln + Lehrer.

items.sentence_de: Unsere Segellehrerin ist sehr nett und geduldig.
items.sentence_translation: Our sailing instructor is very nice and patient.
items.grammar_tip: Feminine version of Segellehrer.

items.sentence_de: Wir wollen im Urlaub auf der Ostsee segeln.
items.sentence_translation: We want to sail on the Baltic Sea during vacation.
items.grammar_tip: Verbs ending in -eln drop the 'e' in the 'ich' form (ich segle).

items.sentence_de: Ich sehe heute Abend einen guten Film.
items.sentence_translation: I am seeing a good movie tonight.
items.grammar_tip: Vowel change in 2nd/3rd person: du siehst, er sieht.

items.sentence_de: Ich wasche meine Hände mit Seife.
items.sentence_translation: I wash my hands with soap.
items.grammar_tip: Always feminine.

items.sentence_de: Hallo, ich bin Julia und das ist Mark.
items.sentence_translation: Hello, I am Julia and this is Mark.
items.grammar_tip: The most important irregular verb in German.

items.sentence_de: Der Mann sucht seine Brille im Büro.
items.sentence_translation: The man is looking for his glasses in the office.
items.grammar_tip: Possessive pronoun for masculine/neuter owners.

items.sentence_de: Öffnen Sie das Buch auf Seite zehn.
items.sentence_translation: Open the book on page ten.
items.grammar_tip: Can also mean 'side'.

items.sentence_de: Der Sekretär schreibt die Termine auf.
items.sentence_translation: The secretary writes down the appointments.
items.grammar_tip: Professional title.

items.sentence_de: Die Sekretärin arbeitet im Vorzimmer des Chefs.
items.sentence_translation: The secretary works in the boss's anteroom.
items.grammar_tip: Professional title (female).

items.sentence_de: Warten Sie bitte eine Sekunde.
items.sentence_translation: Please wait a second.
items.grammar_tip: Time measurement.

items.sentence_de: Ich habe den Kuchen selbst gebacken.
items.sentence_translation: I baked the cake myself.
items.grammar_tip: Emphasizes that someone did something personally.

items.sentence_de: In dieser Kantine gibt es nur Selbstbedienung.
items.sentence_translation: In this canteen, there is only self-service.
items.grammar_tip: Common in cafes/buffets.

items.sentence_de: Ich gehe nur sehr selten ins Fitnessstudio.
items.sentence_translation: I only go to the gym very rarely.
items.grammar_tip: Opposite of 'oft'.

items.sentence_de: Das neue Semester an der Uni beginnt bald.
items.sentence_translation: The new semester at the university begins soon.
items.grammar_tip: Mostly used for university terms.

items.sentence_de: Ich besuche am Freitag ein interessantes Seminar.
items.sentence_translation: I am attending an interesting seminar on Friday.
items.grammar_tip: The plural is Seminare.

items.sentence_de: Der Sieg war eine große Sensation.
items.sentence_translation: The victory was a great sensation.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns in -tion are always feminine.

items.sentence_de: Im September beginnt meistens der Herbst.
items.sentence_translation: Autumn usually begins in September.
items.grammar_tip: Months are always masculine.

items.sentence_de: Spricht man in Belgrad auch Serbisch?
items.sentence_translation: Do they also speak Serbian in Belgrade?
items.grammar_tip: Languages in German usually end in -isch.

items.sentence_de: Ich schaue jeden Abend meine liebste Serie.
items.sentence_translation: I watch my favorite series every evening.
items.grammar_tip: Often used for TV shows.

items.sentence_de: Kann ich bitte noch eine Serviette haben?
items.sentence_translation: Can I please have another napkin?
items.grammar_tip: Loan word from French, but feminine in German.

items.sentence_de: Der Sessel im Wohnzimmer ist sehr bequem.
items.sentence_translation: The armchair in the living room is very comfortable.
items.grammar_tip: Sessel is masculine, unlike Sofa (neuter).

items.sentence_de: Der Shop am Flughafen hat 24 Stunden offen.
items.sentence_translation: The shop at the airport is open 24 hours.
items.grammar_tip: Used often for smaller or specialized stores.

items.sentence_de: Am Samstag wollen wir in der Stadt shoppen.
items.sentence_translation: On Saturday we want to go shopping in the city.
items.grammar_tip: Specific to buying clothes/lifestyle items.

items.sentence_de: Möchtest du heute mit mir shoppen gehen?
items.sentence_translation: Would you like to go shopping with me today?
items.grammar_tip: Common leisure activity phrase.

items.sentence_de: Bist du dir ganz sicher bei der Antwort?
items.sentence_translation: Are you completely sure about the answer?
items.grammar_tip: Can mean both 'safe' and 'certain'.

items.sentence_de: Mein kleiner Bruder ist heute siebzehn Jahre alt.
items.sentence_translation: My little brother is seventeen years old today.
items.grammar_tip: Numbers from 13-19 end in -zehn in German.

items.sentence_de: Meine Oma feiert morgen ihren siebzig Geburtstag.
items.sentence_translation: My grandma celebrates her seventy birthday tomorrow.
items.grammar_tip: Tens in German usually end in -zig, but note 'siebzig' (not siebenzig).

items.sentence_de: Betonen Sie bitte laut den Silbenanfang bei diesem Wort.
items.sentence_translation: Please emphasize the beginning of the syllable in this word.
items.grammar_tip: German syllables often start with a consonant or a glottal stop.

items.sentence_de: Ich möchte gerne in einem Chor singen gehen.
items.sentence_translation: I would like to go sing in a choir.
items.grammar_tip: The verb 'singen' is irregular: singt, sang, hat gesungen.

items.sentence_de: Dieses Wort steht im Satz immer im Singular.
items.sentence_translation: This word is always in the singular in a sentence.
items.grammar_tip: Grammar terms are often masculine in German like 'der Singular'.

items.sentence_de: In dieser Situation weiß ich leider nicht weiter.
items.sentence_translation: In this situation, unfortunately, I don't know what to do.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -ion are always feminine in German.

items.sentence_de: Wir sitzen am Abend oft zusammen in der Küche.
items.sentence_translation: In the evening we often sit together in the kitchen.
items.grammar_tip: Use 'sitzen' for a state of being seated, and 'setzen' for the action of sitting down.

items.sentence_de: Mein Vater kauft sich ein neues Paar Ski.
items.sentence_translation: My father is buying a new pair of skis.
items.grammar_tip: Ski can be pronounced like 'Shee' or 'Skee' in German.

items.sentence_de: Wir machen im Februar einen langen Ski-Urlaub.
items.sentence_translation: We are taking a long skiing holiday in February.
items.grammar_tip: Compound nouns take the gender of the last word (der Urlaub).

items.sentence_de: Das Skifahren macht mir im Winter viel Spaß.
items.sentence_translation: Skiing is a lot of fun for me in winter.
items.grammar_tip: Gerund-like nouns formed from verbs are always neuter (das).

items.sentence_de: Wir machen morgens oft kurz Small Talk im Büro.
items.sentence_translation: We often have a short small talk in the office in the morning.
items.grammar_tip: German uses the English term 'Small Talk' for casual conversation.

items.sentence_de: Ein bisschen Small Talk ist gut für das Team.
items.sentence_translation: A bit of small talk is good for the team.
items.grammar_tip: Loan words from English are often masculine in German.

items.sentence_de: Dieses Jahr planen wir einen sportlichen Snowboard-Urlaub.
items.sentence_translation: This year we are planning an athletic snowboarding holiday.
items.grammar_tip: Like Ski-Urlaub, this is a compound noun with 'der Urlaub'.

items.sentence_de: Schwimmst du gern? Nein, nicht so gern.
items.sentence_translation: Do you like swimming? No, not so much.
items.grammar_tip: 'Nicht so gern' is a common way to express moderate dislike.

items.sentence_de: Erzähl mir mehr, denn so war das früher.
items.sentence_translation: Tell me more, because that is how it was in the past.
items.grammar_tip: The phrase uses 'war', the past tense of 'sein'.

items.sentence_de: Mein Sohn geht schon in die erste Klasse.
items.sentence_translation: My son is already in the first grade.
items.grammar_tip: The plural 'Söhne' changes the vowel 'o' to 'ö'.

items.sentence_de: Der Solist spielt ein langes Stück auf der Geige.
items.sentence_translation: The soloist plays a long piece on the violin.
items.grammar_tip: Male professions or roles often end in -ist.

items.sentence_de: Die Solistin singt heute Abend in der Oper.
items.sentence_translation: The soloist is singing at the opera tonight.
items.grammar_tip: Female versions of professions usually end in -in.

items.sentence_de: Was sollen wir heute für das Abendessen kochen?
items.sentence_translation: What are we supposed to cook for dinner today?
items.grammar_tip: 'Sollen' is a modal verb used for suggestions or duties.

items.sentence_de: Im Sommer ist es in Berlin sehr heiß.
items.sentence_translation: In summer it is very hot in Berlin.
items.grammar_tip: All seasons in German are masculine (der).

items.sentence_de: Unsere Firma plant ein großes Sommerfest im Juli.
items.sentence_translation: Our company is planning a big summer festival in July.
items.grammar_tip: 'Fest' is neuter, so compound words ending in -fest are neuter.

items.sentence_de: Ich brauche meine Sonnenbrille, weil die Sonne scheint.
items.sentence_translation: I need my sunglasses because the sun is shining.
items.grammar_tip: Though English uses plural 'sunglasses', German uses singular 'Brille' (f).

items.sentence_de: Vergiss bitte die Sonnencreme nicht, wir gehen zum Strand.
items.sentence_translation: Please don't forget the sunscreen, we are going to the beach.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -e are very often feminine.

items.sentence_de: Morgen wird das Wetter in München sehr sonnig.
items.sentence_translation: Tomorrow the weather in Munich will be very sunny.
items.grammar_tip: Adjectives describing weather often end in -ig.

items.sentence_de: Am Sonntag schlafe ich meistens bis zehn Uhr.
items.sentence_translation: On Sunday I usually sleep until ten o'clock.
items.grammar_tip: All days of the week are masculine (der).

items.sentence_de: Wir gehen am Sonntagnachmittag oft im Park spazieren.
items.sentence_translation: We often go for a walk in the park on Sunday afternoon.
items.grammar_tip: Times of day combined with weekdays follow the 'der' gender.

items.sentence_de: Iss jetzt, sonst wird dein Essen ganz kalt.
items.sentence_translation: Eat now, otherwise your food will get completely cold.
items.grammar_tip: 'Sonst' is used to show a consequence of not doing something.

items.sentence_de: Ich kaufe ein kleines Souvenir für meine Mutter.
items.sentence_translation: I am buying a small souvenir for my mother.
items.grammar_tip: This is a loanword from French and is neuter in German.

items.sentence_de: Ich koche heute Spaghetti mit einer Tomatensoße.
items.sentence_translation: I am cooking spaghetti with a tomato sauce today.
items.grammar_tip: Spaghetti is usually used in the plural in German.

items.sentence_de: Wir möchten nächsten Sommer nach Spanien in Urlaub.
items.sentence_translation: We want to go on vacation to Spain next summer.
items.grammar_tip: Most countries do not use an article in German unless followed by an adjective.
