items.sentence_de: Lernst du in der Schule auch Spanisch oder Französisch?
items.sentence_translation: Are you also learning Spanish or French at school?
items.grammar_tip: Languages are generally used without articles in these contexts.

items.sentence_de: Fußball spielen macht den Kindern viel Spaß.
items.sentence_translation: Playing football is a lot of fun for the children.
items.grammar_tip: The phrase 'Spaß machen' means 'to be fun'.

items.sentence_de: Wir gehen am Nachmittag im Wald spazieren gehen.
items.sentence_translation: We are going for a walk in the forest in the afternoon.
items.grammar_tip: 'Spazieren' is the verb for the action, 'gehen' is the auxiliary of movement.

items.sentence_de: Ein kurzer Spaziergang ist gut für die Gesundheit.
items.sentence_translation: A short walk is good for one's health.
items.grammar_tip: 'Einen Spaziergang machen' is a very common German collocation.

items.sentence_de: Vergiss nicht, dein Dokument am Computer zu speichern.
items.sentence_translation: Don't forget to save your document on the computer.
items.grammar_tip: 'Speichern' is used for digital data or saving water/energy.

items.sentence_de: Diese Wurst ist eine bekannte Spezialität aus Bayern.
items.sentence_translation: This sausage is a well-known specialty from Bavaria.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -tät are always feminine.

items.sentence_de: Wir spielen heute Abend ein neues Spiel zusammen.
items.sentence_translation: We are playing a new game together tonight.
items.grammar_tip: The plural of 'Spiel' is 'Spiele'.

items.sentence_de: Die Kinder spielen gerne auf dem großen Spielplatz.
items.sentence_translation: The children like playing on the big playground.
items.grammar_tip: 'Platz' is masculine, so 'Spielplatz' is also masculine.

items.sentence_de: In diesem Kaufhaus gibt es viele Spielwaren.
items.sentence_translation: There are many toys in this department store.
items.grammar_tip: 'Waren' refers to goods; 'Spielwaren' refers specifically to toy goods.

items.sentence_de: Mein Bruder ist Mitglied in einem Sportclub.
items.sentence_translation: My brother is a member of a sports club.
items.grammar_tip: German often uses the English 'Club' or German 'Verein'.

items.sentence_de: Ich trage beim Training immer meine blaue Sportkleidung.
items.sentence_translation: I always wear my blue sportswear during training.
items.grammar_tip: 'Kleidung' is a collective noun and usually used in the singular.

items.sentence_de: Der Sportler trainiert jeden Tag für den Marathon.
items.sentence_translation: The athlete trains every day for the marathon.
items.grammar_tip: 'Sportler' is both singular and plural in the masculine form.

items.sentence_de: Die Sportlerin gewinnt die Goldmedaille beim Laufen.
items.sentence_translation: The female athlete wins the gold medal in running.
items.grammar_tip: Remember to add -in for female versions of people.

items.sentence_de: Meine Schwester ist sehr sportlich und spielt Tennis.
items.sentence_translation: My sister is very athletic and plays tennis.
items.grammar_tip: Adjectives ending in -lich are very common in German.

items.sentence_de: Ich ziehe mir schnell meinen neuen Sportschuh an.
items.sentence_translation: I am quickly putting on my new trainer.
items.grammar_tip: Note that in German you often talk about shoes in the plural.

items.sentence_de: Ich besuche einen Kurs am Sprachinstitut der Universität.
items.sentence_translation: I am attending a course at the university's language institute.
items.grammar_tip: 'Institut' is neuter, making the whole compound neuter.

items.sentence_de: Der Sprachkurs findet immer am Montagabend statt.
items.sentence_translation: The language class always takes place on Monday evening.
items.grammar_tip: 'Kurs' is masculine (der Kurs).

items.sentence_de: Ich schicke dir später eine kurze Sprachnachricht.
items.sentence_translation: I'll send you a short voice message later.
items.grammar_tip: 'Nachricht' is feminine (die Nachricht).

items.sentence_de: In meiner Sprachschule lerne ich viele nette Leute kennen.
items.sentence_translation: In my language school, I get to know many nice people.
items.grammar_tip: 'Schule' is feminine (die Schule).

items.sentence_de: Wir sprechen im Unterricht nur Deutsch mit dem Lehrer.
items.sentence_translation: We only speak German with the teacher in class.
items.grammar_tip: 'Sprechen' has a vowel change: ich spreche, du sprichst, er spricht.

items.sentence_de: Der Arzt gibt dem Patienten eine kleine Spritze.
items.sentence_translation: The doctor gives the patient a small injection.
items.grammar_tip: In German, 'Spritze' is also the word for a syringe.

items.sentence_de: Die Spülmaschine ist voll und muss jetzt laufen.
items.sentence_translation: The dishwasher is full and needs to run now.
items.grammar_tip: Compound noun from 'spülen' (to wash/rinse) and 'Maschine'.

items.sentence_de: Wir gehen am Samstag ins Stadion zum Fußballspiel.
items.sentence_translation: We are going to the stadium for the football match on Saturday.
items.grammar_tip: The plural 'Stadien' is irregular (dropping the -on).

items.sentence_de: Berlin ist die größte Stadt in ganz Deutschland.
items.sentence_translation: Berlin is the largest city in all of Germany.
items.grammar_tip: The plural form is 'Städte' with an umlaut.

items.sentence_de: Wir machen im Mai eine Städtereise nach Wien.
items.sentence_translation: We are taking a city trip to Vienna in May.
items.grammar_tip: A trip that involves visiting multiple or specific cities.

items.sentence_de: Die Stadtführung beginnt um elf Uhr am Marktplatz.
items.sentence_translation: The city tour starts at eleven o'clock at the market square.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -ung are always feminine.

items.sentence_de: Im Stadtpark kann man im Sommer wunderbar entspannen.
items.sentence_translation: In the city park you can relax wonderfully in summer.
items.grammar_tip: Compound noun with 'der Park'.

items.sentence_de: Morgen machen wir eine Stadttour mit dem Bus.
items.sentence_translation: Tomorrow we are taking a city tour by bus.
items.grammar_tip: Similar to 'Stadtführung' but often implies a vehicle tour.

items.sentence_de: Ein Stadturlaub in Paris ist sehr romantisch.
items.sentence_translation: A city holiday in Paris is very romantic.
items.grammar_tip: Vacation spent exploring a urban environment.

items.sentence_de: Der Stapel Karten liegt oben auf dem Tisch.
items.sentence_translation: The deck of cards is on the table.
items.grammar_tip: Used for things piled on top of each other.

items.sentence_de: Der bekannte Star gibt heute Abend ein Konzert.
items.sentence_translation: The well-known star is giving a concert tonight.
items.grammar_tip: Used for celebrities (like in English) and also a type of bird.

items.sentence_de: Alle Läufer stehen jetzt bereit am Start.
items.sentence_translation: All runners are standing ready at the start now.
items.grammar_tip: Related to the verb 'starten'.

items.sentence_de: An welcher Station müssen wir aus dem Bus aussteigen?
items.sentence_translation: At which station do we have to get off the bus?
items.grammar_tip: Often used for stops on a subway or bus line.

items.sentence_de: Er arbeitet als Statist in einem neuen Kinofilm.
items.sentence_translation: He works as an extra in a new cinema film.
items.grammar_tip: A male background actor in a film or play.

items.sentence_de: Die Statistik zeigt, dass viele Menschen Sport machen.
items.sentence_translation: The statistics show that many people do sports.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -ik are feminine.

items.sentence_de: Sie möchte gerne als Statistin beim Theater arbeiten.
items.sentence_translation: She would like to work as an extra at the theater.
items.grammar_tip: The female form of 'Statist'.

items.sentence_de: Das Konzert wird morgen in der großen Halle stattfinden.
items.sentence_translation: The concert will take place tomorrow in the big hall.
items.grammar_tip: A separable verb: 'Das Konzert findet heute statt.'

items.sentence_de: Wo genau stehen die Blumen in der Wohnung?
items.sentence_translation: Where exactly are the flowers standing in the apartment?
items.grammar_tip: Use 'stehen' for things that are vertical or on their base.

items.sentence_de: Darf ich Ihnen eine kurze Frage stellen?
items.sentence_translation: May I ask you a short question?
items.grammar_tip: In German, you 'place' (stellen) a question rather than 'asking' it with 'fragen'.

items.sentence_de: Schreiben Sie bitte nur einen Stichpunkt pro Zeile.
items.sentence_translation: Please write only one bullet point per line.
items.grammar_tip: Literally 'sting point'.

items.sentence_de: Im Winter trage ich am liebsten warme Stiefel.
items.sentence_translation: In winter I prefer wearing warm boots.
items.grammar_tip: The plural of 'Stiefel' remains 'Stiefel'.

items.sentence_de: Hast du einen Stift für mich zum Schreiben?
items.sentence_translation: Do you have a pen for me to write with?
items.grammar_tip: A general word for any writing utensil.

items.sentence_de: Ja, das stimmt, der Termin ist morgen.
items.sentence_translation: Yes, that's true, the appointment is tomorrow.
items.grammar_tip: 'Das stimmt' is a common phrase to agree with someone.

items.sentence_de: Zu Weihnachten essen wir oft einen süßen Stollen.
items.sentence_translation: At Christmas we often eat a sweet 'Stollen'.
items.grammar_tip: A traditional heavy yeast cake with dried fruit.

items.sentence_de: Wir liegen den ganzen Tag am schönen Strand.
items.sentence_translation: We lie on the beautiful beach all day long.
items.grammar_tip: 'Am Strand' means 'at the beach'.

items.sentence_de: Wir trinken Cocktails in der Strandbar.
items.sentence_translation: We are drinking cocktails in the beach bar.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -bar are feminine.

items.sentence_de: Unsere neue Strategie ist sehr erfolgreich.
items.sentence_translation: Our new strategy is very successful.
items.grammar_tip: German nouns ending in -ie are usually feminine.

items.sentence_de: Ich habe heute viel Stress bei der Arbeit.
items.sentence_translation: I have a lot of stress at work today.
items.grammar_tip: Stress is a masculine noun used often in the singular.

items.sentence_de: Mein Arbeitstag war heute wirklich stressig.
items.sentence_translation: My workday was really stressful today.
items.grammar_tip: Adjectives describing qualities remain lowercase.

items.sentence_de: Ich möchte bitte ein Stück Kuchen.
items.sentence_translation: I would like a piece of cake, please.
items.grammar_tip: Stück is used for portions of food or units of items.

items.sentence_de: Die Studentin lernt heute in der Bibliothek.
items.sentence_translation: The female student is studying in the library today.
items.grammar_tip: Add -in to the masculine job title to make it feminine.

items.sentence_de: Ich gehe oft ins Fitness-Studio.
items.sentence_translation: I often go to the fitness studio.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -o usually take -s in the plural.

items.sentence_de: Sein Studium an der Universität dauert lange.
items.sentence_translation: His studies at the university take a long time.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -um often have plural forms ending in -en.

items.sentence_de: Dort steht ein freier Stuhl für dich.
items.sentence_translation: There is a free chair for you.
items.grammar_tip: Der Stuhl uses an umlaut in its plural: die Stühle.

items.sentence_de: Das Subjekt steht oft am Satzanfang.
items.sentence_translation: The subject is often at the beginning of the sentence.
items.grammar_tip: Grammar terms are often neuter in German.

items.sentence_de: Brasilien liegt in Südamerika.
items.sentence_translation: Brazil is located in South America.
items.grammar_tip: Continents usually don't take an article in German.

items.sentence_de: München liegt im Süden von Deutschland.
items.sentence_translation: Munich is located in the south of Germany.
items.grammar_tip: Compass directions are always masculine (der).

items.sentence_de: Das Konzert am Samstag war einfach super.
items.sentence_translation: The concert on Saturday was simply super.
items.grammar_tip: Super is used as an indeclinable adjective/adverb.

items.sentence_de: Ich kaufe Obst im Supermarkt.
items.sentence_translation: I buy fruit in the supermarket.
items.grammar_tip: Supermarkt is a compound noun: der Markt (masculine).

items.sentence_de: Meine neuen Nachbarn sind supernett.
items.sentence_translation: My new neighbors are super nice.
items.grammar_tip: German often adds 'super-' to adjectives for emphasis.

items.sentence_de: Die Suppe schmeckt heute sehr gut.
items.sentence_translation: The soup tastes very good today.
items.grammar_tip: Suppe is feminine: die Suppe.

items.sentence_de: Ich kaufe ein Suppenhuhn für die Brühe.
items.sentence_translation: I am buying a boiling chicken for the broth.
items.grammar_tip: Compound nouns take the gender of the last word (das Huhn).

items.sentence_de: Wir essen heute Abend leckeres Sushi.
items.sentence_translation: We are eating delicious sushi tonight.
items.grammar_tip: Foreign food words are often neuter in German.

items.sentence_de: Ich trinke meinen Tee ohne Zucker, nicht süß.
items.sentence_translation: I drink my tea without sugar, not sweet.
items.grammar_tip: Süß can describe food or people (cute).

items.sentence_de: Schokolade ist meine liebste Süßigkeit.
items.sentence_translation: Chocolate is my favorite sweet.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -keit are always feminine.

items.sentence_de: Ich trage heute ein graues Sweatshirt.
items.sentence_translation: I am wearing a gray sweatshirt today.
items.grammar_tip: English loanwords for clothing are often neuter.

items.sentence_de: Das Herz ist ein Symbol für Liebe.
items.sentence_translation: The heart is a symbol for love.
items.grammar_tip: The plural of Symbol is Symbole.

items.sentence_de: Die erste Szene im Film ist spannend.
items.sentence_translation: The first scene in the movie is exciting.
items.grammar_tip: Szene refers to a part of a play or a movie.

items.sentence_de: Im Sommer trage ich gerne ein T-Shirt.
items.sentence_translation: In summer I like to wear a t-shirt.
items.grammar_tip: Like many English imports, it is neuter.

items.sentence_de: Schreiben Sie die Wörter in die Tabelle.
items.sentence_translation: Write the words into the table.
items.grammar_tip: A 'Tabelle' is a data chart, not a piece of furniture.

items.sentence_de: Nehmen Sie die Tablette dreimal täglich.
items.sentence_translation: Take the pill three times daily.
items.grammar_tip: Medication words are often feminine.

items.sentence_de: Der Lehrer schreibt das Wort an die Tafel.
items.sentence_translation: The teacher writes the word on the blackboard.
items.grammar_tip: Die Tafel is used in classrooms for writing.

items.sentence_de: Ich wünsche Ihnen einen schönen Tag.
items.sentence_translation: I wish you a nice day.
items.grammar_tip: Days are masculine: der Tag.

items.sentence_de: Welche Tageszeit ist für Sie am besten?
items.sentence_translation: Which time of day is best for you?
items.grammar_tip: Tageszeit is a compound: die Zeit is feminine.

items.sentence_de: Ich gehe täglich eine Stunde spazieren.
items.sentence_translation: I go for a walk for an hour daily.
items.grammar_tip: Täglich is derived from 'Tag'.

items.sentence_de: Meine Tante wohnt in Berlin.
items.sentence_translation: My aunt lives in Berlin.
items.grammar_tip: Female relatives are feminine: die Tante.

items.sentence_de: Ich möchte eine Tasse Kaffee trinken.
items.sentence_translation: I would like to drink a cup of coffee.
items.grammar_tip: Cups for hot drinks are 'Tassen'.

items.sentence_de: Es ist heute tatsächlich sehr warm.
items.sentence_translation: It is actually very warm today.
items.grammar_tip: Used to emphasize that something is true.

items.sentence_de: Können wir bitte die Plätze tauschen?
items.sentence_translation: Can we please switch seats?
items.grammar_tip: Tauschen means to exchange or swap.

items.sentence_de: In dieser Stadt leben zehntausend Menschen.
items.sentence_translation: Ten thousand people live in this city.
items.grammar_tip: Tausend is used for the number 1,000.

items.sentence_de: Der Taxifahrer fährt mich zum Bahnhof.
items.sentence_translation: The taxi driver is driving me to the station.
items.grammar_tip: Masculine professions often end in -er.

items.sentence_de: Die Taxifahrerin kennt den Weg genau.
items.sentence_translation: The female taxi driver knows the way exactly.
items.grammar_tip: Feminine professions end in -in.

items.sentence_de: Die Taxifahrt zum Flughafen war teuer.
items.sentence_translation: The taxi ride to the airport was expensive.
items.grammar_tip: Die Fahrt is feminine, so Taxifahrt is too.

items.sentence_de: Unser Team arbeitet sehr gut zusammen.
items.sentence_translation: Our team works very well together.
items.grammar_tip: Team is a neuter noun in German.

items.sentence_de: Die moderne Technik hilft uns sehr.
items.sentence_translation: Modern technology helps us a lot.
items.grammar_tip: Technik is feminine: die Technik.

items.sentence_de: Der Techniker repariert die Waschmaschine.
items.sentence_translation: The technician is repairing the washing machine.
items.grammar_tip: The plural of Techniker is the same as the singular.

items.sentence_de: Die Technikerin prüft das Internet.
items.sentence_translation: The female technician is checking the internet.
items.grammar_tip: Add -innen for the plural of feminine professions.

items.sentence_de: Das Telefongespräch dauerte nur zwei Minuten.
items.sentence_translation: The telephone call lasted only two minutes.
items.grammar_tip: Das Gespräch is neuter.

items.sentence_de: Wie ist deine aktuelle Telefonnummer?
items.sentence_translation: What is your current telephone number?
items.grammar_tip: Die Nummer is feminine.

items.sentence_de: Der Teller steht auf dem Tisch.
items.sentence_translation: The plate is on the table.
items.grammar_tip: Der Teller is masculine.

items.sentence_de: Ich spiele am Wochenende gerne Tennis.
items.sentence_translation: I like playing tennis on the weekend.
items.grammar_tip: Sports usually don't take an article in German when playing them.

items.sentence_de: Treffen wir uns auf dem Tennisplatz?
items.sentence_translation: Shall we meet on the tennis court?
items.grammar_tip: Der Platz is masculine.

items.sentence_de: Der Teppich im Wohnzimmer ist blau.
items.sentence_translation: The carpet in the living room is blue.
items.grammar_tip: Teppich is masculine: der Teppich.

items.sentence_de: Wir frühstücken im Sommer auf der Terrasse.
items.sentence_translation: We have breakfast on the patio in summer.
items.grammar_tip: Terrasse is feminine: die Terrasse.

items.sentence_de: Benutzen Sie diesen Textbaustein für die E-Mail.
items.sentence_translation: Use this text block for the email.
items.grammar_tip: A compound of 'Text' and 'Baustein' (building block).

items.sentence_de: Ich möchte nächsten Winter nach Thailand fliegen.
items.sentence_translation: I want to fly to Thailand next winter.
items.grammar_tip: Most countries are neuter and don't need an article.

items.sentence_de: Wir gehen heute Abend ins Theater.
items.sentence_translation: We are going to the theatre tonight.
items.grammar_tip: Theater is neuter: das Theater.

items.sentence_de: Besuchen Sie das Theater-Festival in der Stadt?
items.sentence_translation: Are you visiting the theatre festival in the city?
items.grammar_tip: Neuter noun: das Festival.

items.sentence_de: Das Thema der heutigen Stunde ist Grammatik.
items.sentence_translation: The topic of today's lesson is grammar.
items.grammar_tip: The plural of Thema is Themen.

items.sentence_de: Die Texte sind thematisch geordnet.
items.sentence_translation: The texts are ordered topically.
items.grammar_tip: Adjective form of 'Thema'.

items.sentence_de: Der Therapeut hilft dem Patienten sehr.
items.sentence_translation: The therapist helps the patient a lot.
items.grammar_tip: Therapeut is a masculine noun.

items.sentence_de: Ich habe einen Termin bei meiner Therapeutin.
items.sentence_translation: I have an appointment with my female therapist.
items.grammar_tip: The feminine form ends in -in.

items.sentence_de: Der Ticketkauf am Automaten ist einfach.
items.sentence_translation: Buying tickets at the machine is easy.
items.grammar_tip: Der Kauf is masculine.

items.sentence_de: Hast du einen guten Tipp für mich?
items.sentence_translation: Do you have a good tip for me?
items.grammar_tip: Tipp is masculine: der Tipp.

items.sentence_de: Das ist eine wirklich tolle Idee!
items.sentence_translation: That is a really great idea!
items.grammar_tip: 'Toll' is a common A1 adjective for 'great'.

items.sentence_de: Ich esse gerne eine heiße Tomatensuppe.
items.sentence_translation: I like eating a hot tomato soup.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -suppe are feminine.

items.sentence_de: Die Qualität der Schuhe ist top.
items.sentence_translation: The quality of the shoes is top.
items.grammar_tip: 'Top' is used informally for 'excellent'.

items.sentence_de: Diese Mode ist im Moment topaktuell.
items.sentence_translation: This fashion is cutting-edge at the moment.
items.grammar_tip: Means 'very current'.

items.sentence_de: Ich bin heute total müde vom Sport.
items.sentence_translation: I am totally tired from sports today.
items.grammar_tip: Total is used for emphasis.

items.sentence_de: Wir machen eine Tour durch die Stadt.
items.sentence_translation: We are doing a tour through the city.
items.grammar_tip: Tour is feminine: die Tour.

items.sentence_de: Er trägt heute einen blauen Anzug.
items.sentence_translation: He is wearing a blue suit today.
items.grammar_tip: Tragen is an irregular verb (a -> ä in 2nd/3rd person).

items.sentence_de: Ich trainiere zweimal pro Woche im Fitnessstudio.
items.sentence_translation: I train twice a week in the gym.
items.grammar_tip: Verbs ending in -ieren don't use 'ge-' in the past participle.

items.sentence_de: Das Training beginnt um achtzehn Uhr.
items.sentence_translation: The practice starts at 6 PM.
items.grammar_tip: Training is neuter: das Training.

items.sentence_de: Mein großer Traum ist eine Weltreise.
items.sentence_translation: My big dream is a trip around the world.
items.grammar_tip: Der Traum has the plural 'Träume'.

items.sentence_de: In den Malediven war mein Traumurlaub.
items.sentence_translation: In the Maldives was my dream holiday.
items.grammar_tip: Compound: der Urlaub is masculine.

items.sentence_de: Ich treffe meine Freunde im Park.
items.sentence_translation: I am meeting my friends in the park.
items.grammar_tip: Treffen is irregular (e -> i in 2nd/3rd person).

items.sentence_de: Der Treffpunkt ist vor dem Kino.
items.sentence_translation: The meeting point is in front of the cinema.
items.grammar_tip: Der Punkt is masculine, so Treffpunkt is too.

items.sentence_de: Berlin ist eine bekannte Trendstadt.
items.sentence_translation: Berlin is a well-known trendy city.
items.grammar_tip: Die Stadt is feminine.

items.sentence_de: Einige deutsche Verben sind trennbar.
items.sentence_translation: Some German verbs are separable.
items.grammar_tip: Refers to verbs like 'aufstehen' (auf-stehen).

items.sentence_de: Was möchten Sie gerne trinken?
items.sentence_translation: What would you like to drink?
items.grammar_tip: Trinken is a strong verb: trinken, trank, getrunken.

items.sentence_de: Der Kellner bekommt ein gutes Trinkgeld.
items.sentence_translation: The waiter gets a good tip.
items.grammar_tip: Trinkgeld is a neuter noun (das). In Germany, a 5-10% tip is common.

items.sentence_de: Mein Sohn spielt jeden Tag Trompete.
items.sentence_translation: My son plays the trumpet every day.
items.grammar_tip: Musical instruments are usually used without an article when playing them.

items.sentence_de: Der Trompetenunterricht findet am Montag statt.
items.sentence_translation: The trumpet lesson takes place on Monday.
items.grammar_tip: In compound nouns, the last word determines the gender (der Unterricht).

items.sentence_de: Nehmen Sie bitte drei Tropfen ein.
items.sentence_translation: Please take three drops.
items.grammar_tip: Tropfen is often used for liquid medicine or eye drops.

items.sentence_de: Ich gehe jetzt nach Hause, tschüs!
items.sentence_translation: I'm going home now, bye!
items.grammar_tip: Tschüs is the most common informal way to say goodbye in Germany.

items.sentence_de: Sie trägt ein blaues Tuch um.
items.sentence_translation: She is wearing a blue shawl.
items.grammar_tip: Tuch can refer to a scarf, shawl, or even a simple cloth/rag.

items.sentence_de: Machen Sie bitte die Tür zu.
items.sentence_translation: Please close the door.
items.grammar_tip: Tür is a feminine noun (die). The plural is 'Türen'.

items.sentence_de: Wir machen im Sommer Urlaub in der Türkei.
items.sentence_translation: We are going on vacation to Turkey in summer.
items.grammar_tip: Unlike most countries, Turkey (die Türkei) always requires its article.

items.sentence_de: Er spricht sehr gut Türkisch und Deutsch.
items.sentence_translation: He speaks Turkish and German very well.
items.grammar_tip: Languages in German are typically used without articles.

items.sentence_de: Der Turm der Kirche ist sehr hoch.
items.sentence_translation: The tower of the church is very high.
items.grammar_tip: Turm is masculine (der). The plural involves an umlaut: die Türme.

items.sentence_de: Brauchen Sie eine Tüte für das Obst?
items.sentence_translation: Do you need a bag for the fruit?
items.grammar_tip: Tüte usually refers to plastic or paper bags from a shop.

items.sentence_de: Das ist ein ganz typisch deutsches Essen.
items.sentence_translation: That is a very typical German meal.
items.grammar_tip: Typisch is an adjective used to describe characteristic features.

items.sentence_de: Ich fahre mit der U-Bahn zur Arbeit.
items.sentence_translation: I take the subway to work.
items.grammar_tip: U-Bahn stands for 'Untergrundbahn' (underground train).

items.sentence_de: Wir sprechen oft über unsere alten Freunde.
items.sentence_translation: We often speak about our old friends.
items.grammar_tip: When used with 'sprechen', the preposition 'über' takes the accusative case.

items.sentence_de: Es gibt hier überall kostenloses WLAN.
items.sentence_translation: There is free Wi-Fi everywhere here.
items.grammar_tip: Überall means everywhere or in every place.

items.sentence_de: Ich muss mir das noch kurz überlegen.
items.sentence_translation: I need to think about that for a moment.
items.grammar_tip: Überlegen often uses 'sich' (dative) to mean 'to ponder/reflect'.

items.sentence_de: Die Party war eine große Überraschung.
items.sentence_translation: The party was a big surprise.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -ung are always feminine (die).

items.sentence_de: Morgen ist unser spezieller Überraschungstag.
items.sentence_translation: Tomorrow is our special surprise day.
items.grammar_tip: This is a compound: Überraschung + Tag.

items.sentence_de: Lies bitte zuerst die Überschrift vom Text.
items.sentence_translation: Please read the heading of the text first.
items.grammar_tip: Schrift comes from 'schreiben' (to write). Die Überschrift is the title.

items.sentence_de: Ich muss heute die Miete überweisen.
items.sentence_translation: I have to transfer the rent today.
items.grammar_tip: Überweisen is an inseparable verb used for bank transfers.

items.sentence_de: Diese Übung ist für mich sehr einfach.
items.sentence_translation: This exercise is very easy for me.
items.grammar_tip: -ung nouns are always feminine. The plural is -en.

items.sentence_de: Schreiben Sie die Sätze in das Übungsbuch.
items.sentence_translation: Write the sentences in the exercise book.
items.grammar_tip: A book for practicing exercises (Übung + Buch).

items.sentence_de: Wissen Sie die genaue Uhrzeit?
items.sentence_translation: Do you know the exact time of day?
items.grammar_tip: Uhrzeit refers to the specific time on the clock (e.g., 14:00).

items.sentence_de: Meine Nachbarin kommt aus der Ukraine.
items.sentence_translation: My neighbor comes from Ukraine.
items.grammar_tip: Like 'die Türkei', 'die Ukraine' always uses the feminine article.

items.sentence_de: Das Wort 'Bücher' hat einen Umlaut.
items.sentence_translation: The word 'Bücher' has an umlaut.
items.grammar_tip: Umlauts are the letters ä, ö, and ü in German.

items.sentence_de: Sie müssen am Hauptbahnhof in die U1 umsteigen.
items.sentence_translation: You have to transfer to the U1 at the main station.
items.grammar_tip: Umsteigen is a separable verb: 'ich steige um'.

items.sentence_de: Ich möchte dieses Hemd gerne umtauschen.
items.sentence_translation: I would like to exchange this shirt.
items.grammar_tip: Used specifically for returning an item at a shop for something else.

items.sentence_de: Nächsten Monat möchte ich in eine Wohnung umziehen.
items.sentence_translation: Next month I want to move into an apartment.
items.grammar_tip: Umziehen means to move houses or to change clothes (sich umziehen).

items.sentence_de: Der Umzug in die neue Stadt war anstrengend.
items.sentence_translation: The move to the new city was exhausting.
items.grammar_tip: Der Umzug refers to the process of moving house.

items.sentence_de: 'Ein' und 'eine' sind unbestimmte Artikel.
items.sentence_translation: 'Ein' and 'eine' are indeterminate articles.
items.grammar_tip: Unbestimmt means 'indefinite'. Der unbestimmte Artikel is 'a/an'.

items.sentence_de: Gestern gab es einen kleinen Unfall auf der Straße.
items.sentence_translation: Yesterday there was a small accident on the street.
items.grammar_tip: Unfall is masculine (der). It usually takes 'haben' or 'geben'.

items.sentence_de: Ich verstehe kein Ungarisch, nur Deutsch.
items.sentence_translation: I don't understand Hungarian, only German.
items.grammar_tip: Suffix -isch usually indicates a language or nationality adjective.

items.sentence_de: Die Fahrt dauert ungefähr zwanzig Minuten.
items.sentence_translation: The trip takes approximately twenty minutes.
items.grammar_tip: Synonym for 'etwa'. Used for estimations.

items.sentence_de: Es ist unhöflich, beim Essen zu telefonieren.
items.sentence_translation: It is impolite to phone while eating.
items.grammar_tip: 'un-' is a common prefix for negation (un- + höflich).

items.sentence_de: Er studiert Medizin an der Uni.
items.sentence_translation: He is studying medicine at the university.
items.grammar_tip: Short for 'Universität'. Common in spoken German.

items.sentence_de: Wir treffen uns nach der Vorlesung im Unicafé.
items.sentence_translation: We are meeting in the university café after the lecture.
items.grammar_tip: Café is always neuter (das).

items.sentence_de: Die Universität in dieser Stadt ist sehr alt.
items.sentence_translation: The university in this city is very old.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -tät are always feminine.

items.sentence_de: Man muss unregelmäßige Verben auswendig lernen.
items.sentence_translation: One must learn irregular verbs by heart.
items.grammar_tip: Irregular verbs change their stem vowels in various tenses.

items.sentence_de: Wir grillen heute Abend bei uns.
items.sentence_translation: We are barbecuing at our place tonight.
items.grammar_tip: 'Bei uns' is a fixed idiom meaning 'at our house/place'.

items.sentence_de: Unser Haus ist klein, aber sehr gemütlich.
items.sentence_translation: Our house is small but very cozy.
items.grammar_tip: The ending changes based on the gender of the noun (unser/unsere).

items.sentence_de: Unsere Hausmittel helfen gegen die Erkältung.
items.sentence_translation: Our home remedies help against the cold.
items.grammar_tip: Compound: Haus (home) + Mittel (means/remedy).

items.sentence_de: Die Toiletten befinden sich im Untergeschoss.
items.sentence_translation: The toilets are located in the basement level.
items.grammar_tip: Often abbreviated as 'UG' in elevators. Neuter (das).

items.sentence_de: Bitte unterschreiben Sie den Vertrag hier unten.
items.sentence_translation: Please sign the contract down here.
items.grammar_tip: Inseparable verb. The past participle is 'unterschrieben'.

items.sentence_de: Bitte unterstreichen Sie die wichtigen Wörter.
items.sentence_translation: Please underline the important words.
items.grammar_tip: Inseparable verb. It literally means 'to stroke under'.

items.sentence_de: Meine E-Mail-Adresse hat einen Unterstrich.
items.sentence_translation: My email address has an underscore.
items.grammar_tip: Used often when giving email addresses or technical details.

items.sentence_de: Der Arzt muss mein Knie untersuchen.
items.sentence_translation: The doctor must examine my knee.
items.grammar_tip: Used for medical examinations or inspections.

items.sentence_de: Ich bin gerade unterwegs zum Bahnhof.
items.sentence_translation: I am currently on the way to the station.
items.grammar_tip: Unterwegs means you are currently traveling or in transit.

items.sentence_de: Ich habe eine Urlaubsnachricht auf mein Handy bekommen.
items.sentence_translation: I received a holiday message on my mobile phone.
items.grammar_tip: Urlaub (vacation) + Nachricht (message).

items.sentence_de: Mallorca ist ein sehr beliebter Urlaubsort.
items.sentence_translation: Mallorca is a very popular holiday resort.
items.grammar_tip: A place (Ort) where you spend your vacation (Urlaub).

items.sentence_de: Olivia kommt aus den USA.
items.sentence_translation: Olivia comes from the USA.
items.grammar_tip: USA is plural in German: 'aus den USA' (dative plural).

items.sentence_de: Speichern Sie die Fotos auf dem USB-Stick.
items.sentence_translation: Save the photos on the USB stick.
items.grammar_tip: Masculine gender (der Stick). Plural: -s.

items.sentence_de: Es gibt eine Variation von diesem Rezept.
items.sentence_translation: There is a variation of this recipe.
items.grammar_tip: Words ending in -ion are always feminine (die).

items.sentence_de: Die Preise variieren je nach Saison.
items.sentence_translation: The prices vary depending on the season.
items.grammar_tip: Verbs ending in -ieren usually come from Latin/French origins.

items.sentence_de: Wir wollen uns für morgen Abend verabreden.
items.sentence_translation: We want to make plans for tomorrow evening.
items.grammar_tip: Usually used reflexively: 'sich verabreden'.

items.sentence_de: Ich habe heute eine Verabredung mit Anna.
items.sentence_translation: I have an appointment/date with Anna today.
items.grammar_tip: More informal than 'Termin'; often used for social meetings.

items.sentence_de: Wir müssen uns jetzt leider verabschieden.
items.sentence_translation: Unfortunately, we have to say goodbye now.
items.grammar_tip: Reflexive verb: 'sich verabschieden'.

items.sentence_de: Die Veranstaltung beginnt pünktlich um acht Uhr.
items.sentence_translation: The event begins punctually at eight o'clock.
items.grammar_tip: Refers to a planned public or social occasion.

items.sentence_de: In diesem Satz fehlt das Verb.
items.sentence_translation: The verb is missing in this sentence.
items.grammar_tip: Neuter noun (das). Plural: Verben.

items.sentence_de: Der Arzt legt einen Verband um den Arm.
items.sentence_translation: The doctor puts a bandage around the arm.
items.grammar_tip: Der Verband is masculine. Plural: die Verbände.

items.sentence_de: Verbinden Sie die Nomen mit den Artikeln.
items.sentence_translation: Connect the nouns with the articles.
items.grammar_tip: Common instruction in German language textbooks.

items.sentence_de: Können Sie mich bitte mit Frau Müller verbinden?
items.sentence_translation: Can you please connect me with Mrs. Müller?
items.grammar_tip: Also used for connecting phone calls.

items.sentence_de: Hier gilt ein absolutes Verbot für Autos.
items.sentence_translation: There is an absolute prohibition for cars here.
items.grammar_tip: Opposite of 'Erlaubnis' (permission). Neuter (das).

items.sentence_de: Wir müssen einen neuen Termin vereinbaren.
items.sentence_translation: We need to arrange a new appointment.
items.grammar_tip: Typically used for formal appointments (Termine vereinbaren).

items.sentence_de: Ich habe meinen Schlüssel zu Hause vergessen.
items.sentence_translation: I forgot my key at home.
items.grammar_tip: Vergessen is an irregular verb (er vergisst, hat vergessen).

items.sentence_de: Vergleichen Sie die Preise im Supermarkt.
items.sentence_translation: Compare the prices in the supermarket.
items.grammar_tip: Inseparable verb. Past participle: verglichen.

items.sentence_de: Die Verkäuferin im Laden ist sehr nett.
items.sentence_translation: The saleswoman in the shop is very nice.
items.grammar_tip: The masculine form is 'der Verkäufer'.

items.sentence_de: Er ist am Bein verletzt und kann nicht gehen.
items.sentence_translation: He is injured in the leg and cannot walk.
items.grammar_tip: Comes from the verb 'verletzen' (to injure).

items.sentence_de: Unsere Vermieterin wohnt im ersten Stock.
items.sentence_translation: Our landlady lives on the first floor.
items.grammar_tip: The person who owns the apartment you rent.

items.sentence_de: Ich vermisse meine Familie in der Heimat.
items.sentence_translation: I miss my family back home.
items.grammar_tip: Used for feeling the absence of someone or something emotionally.

items.sentence_de: Ich vermute, dass das Wetter morgen gut wird.
items.sentence_translation: I suspect that the weather will be good tomorrow.
items.grammar_tip: Similar to 'glauben' or 'annehmen' (to assume).

items.sentence_de: Die Verpackung von dem Müsli ist kaputt.
items.sentence_translation: The packaging of the muesli is broken.
items.grammar_tip: -ung nouns are always feminine.

items.sentence_de: Ich habe leider den Bus verpasst.
items.sentence_translation: Unfortunately, I missed the bus.
items.grammar_tip: Used for missing a train, bus, or an opportunity.

items.sentence_de: Wir haben viele verschiedene Obstsorten im Garten.
items.sentence_translation: We have many different types of fruit in the garden.
items.grammar_tip: Verschieden acts as an adjective meaning 'various' or 'diverse'.

items.sentence_de: Der Zug hat heute zehn Minuten Verspätung.
items.sentence_translation: The train is ten minutes late today.
items.grammar_tip: Feminine noun. Used specifically for transport being late.

items.sentence_de: Ich kann Sie leider nicht gut verstehen.
items.sentence_translation: Unfortunately, I cannot understand you well.
items.grammar_tip: Inseparable verb. Past participle: verstanden.

items.sentence_de: Ich werde versuchen, pünktlich zu kommen.
items.sentence_translation: I will attempt to come on time.
items.grammar_tip: The verb 'versuchen' is often followed by a 'zu + infinitive' construction.

items.sentence_de: Ich muss den neuen Vertrag heute unterschreiben.
items.sentence_translation: I have to sign the new contract today.
items.grammar_tip: Masculine nouns ending in -ag often form their plural with -äge.

items.sentence_de: Welches Programm sollen wir dafür verwenden?
items.sentence_translation: Which program should we use for that?
items.grammar_tip: 'Verwenden' and 'benutzen' both mean 'to use' and are often interchangeable.

items.sentence_de: Wir sehen uns heute Abend ein Video an.
items.sentence_translation: We are watching a video tonight.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns of foreign origin like 'Video' or 'Auto' often take -s in the plural.

items.sentence_de: Diese Jacke ist mir leider viel zu groß.
items.sentence_translation: Unfortunately, this jacket is much too big for me.
items.grammar_tip: 'Viel zu' is used with adjectives to express an excessive degree.

items.sentence_de: Ich habe heute viele Äpfel auf dem Markt gekauft.
items.sentence_translation: I bought a lot of apples at the market today.
items.grammar_tip: 'Viel' is used for uncountable nouns, 'viele' for countable plural nouns.

items.sentence_de: Es ist Viertel nach acht Uhr morgens.
items.sentence_translation: It is a quarter past eight in the morning.
items.grammar_tip: When telling time, 'Viertel' is used for 15-minute intervals.

items.sentence_de: Meine Tochter ist jetzt schon vierzehn Jahre alt.
items.sentence_translation: My daughter is already fourteen years old.
items.grammar_tip: Numbers from 13 to 19 end in '-zehn'.

items.sentence_de: Das Buch kostet genau vierzig Euro.
items.sentence_translation: The book costs exactly forty Euros.
items.grammar_tip: Tens in German (20, 30, 40...) typically end in '-zig' or '-ßig'.

items.sentence_de: Das Wort 'Auto' beginnt mit einem Vokal.
items.sentence_translation: The word 'Auto' starts with a vowel.
items.grammar_tip: The vowels in German are A, E, I, O, U, and the umlauts.

items.sentence_de: Der Bus ist heute Morgen sehr voll.
items.sentence_translation: The bus is very full this morning.
items.grammar_tip: 'Voll' is the opposite of 'leer' (empty).

items.sentence_de: Ich arbeite von Montag bis Freitag im Büro.
items.sentence_translation: I work from Monday till Friday in the office.
items.grammar_tip: Use 'von ... bis' to define a time span or range.

items.sentence_de: Der Unterricht wird in fünf Minuten vorbei sein.
items.sentence_translation: The class will be over in five minutes.
items.grammar_tip: This phrase uses the verb 'sein' (to be) + 'vorbei' (past/over).

items.sentence_de: Ich muss das Abendessen für die Gäste vorbereiten.
items.sentence_translation: I must prepare dinner for the guests.
items.grammar_tip: 'Vorbereiten' is a separable verb (Ich bereite vor).

items.sentence_de: Ich habe ihn erst vorgestern im Park gesehen.
items.sentence_translation: I only saw him the day before yesterday in the park.
items.grammar_tip: Gestern = yesterday; Vorgestern = day before yesterday.

items.sentence_de: Wir müssen vorher noch schnell einkaufen gehen.
items.sentence_translation: We have to go shopping quickly before.
items.grammar_tip: 'Vorher' refers to a time preceding the current topic.

items.sentence_de: Kannst du mir bitte die Geschichte vorlesen?
items.sentence_translation: Can you please read the story aloud to me?
items.grammar_tip: 'Vorlesen' is a separable verb and an irregular verb (liest vor).

items.sentence_de: Sie hat eine große Vorliebe für italienisches Essen.
items.sentence_translation: She has a great preference for Italian food.
items.grammar_tip: Feminine nouns ending in -e usually take -n in the plural.

items.sentence_de: Am Vormittag habe ich meistens sehr viel Zeit.
items.sentence_translation: In the morning (before noon) I usually have a lot of time.
items.grammar_tip: Time periods of the day are masculine (except 'die Nacht').

items.sentence_de: Ich trinke vormittags immer zwei Tassen Kaffee.
items.sentence_translation: I always drink two cups of coffee in the mornings.
items.grammar_tip: Adding -s to a time of day noun makes it an adverb meaning 'every...'.

items.sentence_de: Der Bäcker ist gleich da vorne an der Ecke.
items.sentence_translation: The bakery is right there in front at the corner.
items.grammar_tip: 'Vorne' is the opposite of 'hinten' (behind/at the back).

items.sentence_de: Das ist ein wirklich guter Vorschlag von dir.
items.sentence_translation: That is a really good suggestion from you.
items.grammar_tip: A 'Vorschlag' is something you suggest for others to consider.

items.sentence_de: Die Kinder wollen uns ein kurzes Stück vorspielen.
items.sentence_translation: The children want to act out a short play for us.
items.grammar_tip: 'Vorspielen' is a separable verb (Ich spiele vor).

items.sentence_de: Darf ich dir meinen Bruder kurz vorstellen?
items.sentence_translation: May I briefly introduce my brother to you?
items.grammar_tip: 'Sich vorstellen' is reflexive, but 'jemanden vorstellen' is transitive.

items.sentence_de: Ein großer Vorteil ist die zentrale Lage der Wohnung.
items.sentence_translation: A big advantage is the central location of the apartment.
items.grammar_tip: The opposite of 'Vorteil' is 'Nachteil'.

items.sentence_de: Wie lautet die passende W-Frage zu dieser Antwort?
items.sentence_translation: What is the appropriate w-question for this answer?
items.grammar_tip: W-questions start with words like Wer, Was, Wo, Wie.

items.sentence_de: Das W-Wort steht am Anfang von diesem Satz.
items.sentence_translation: The w-word is at the beginning of this sentence.
items.grammar_tip: Most question words in German start with 'W'.

items.sentence_de: Bist du schon lange wach oder schläfst du?
items.sentence_translation: Have you been awake for long or are you sleeping?
items.grammar_tip: 'Wach' is the opposite of 'schlafend' (sleeping).

items.sentence_de: Sie können ein Gericht von der Karte wählen.
items.sentence_translation: You can choose a dish from the menu.
items.grammar_tip: 'Wählen' can mean to choose or to vote.

items.sentence_de: Wir liefern die Ware innerhalb von drei Tagen.
items.sentence_translation: We deliver the merchandise within three days.
items.grammar_tip: 'Ware' refers to goods or products sold in a shop.

items.sentence_de: Im Sommer ist es in Deutschland oft warm.
items.sentence_translation: In summer it is often warm in Germany.
items.grammar_tip: 'Warm' is the opposite of 'kalt'.

items.sentence_de: Was ist los in Berlin am nächsten Wochenende?
items.sentence_translation: What's going on in Berlin next weekend?
items.grammar_tip: 'Was ist los' is a common way to ask what is happening.

items.sentence_de: Ich muss heute meine schmutzige Kleidung waschen.
items.sentence_translation: I have to wash my dirty clothes today.
items.grammar_tip: The verb 'waschen' changes its vowel in the 2nd/3rd person: du wäschst, er wäscht.

items.sentence_de: Unsere Waschmaschine ist leider seit gestern kaputt.
items.sentence_translation: Our washing machine has unfortunately been broken since yesterday.
items.grammar_tip: Compound nouns take the gender of the last word (die Maschine).

items.sentence_de: Können Sie mir bitte diesen Geldschein wechseln?
items.sentence_translation: Can you please change this banknote for me?
items.grammar_tip: 'Wechseln' is used for changing money or items.

items.sentence_de: Das Wort 'in' ist eine wichtige Wechselpräposition.
items.sentence_translation: The word 'in' is an important two-case preposition.
items.grammar_tip: Two-case prepositions take Accusative (movement) or Dative (location).

items.sentence_de: Kannst du mich bitte morgen um sieben wecken?
items.sentence_translation: Can you please wake me up at seven tomorrow?
items.grammar_tip: 'Wecken' is transitive (to wake someone else); 'aufwachen' is intransitive.

items.sentence_de: Kennen Sie den Weg zum Bahnhof?
items.sentence_translation: Do you know the way to the train station?
items.grammar_tip: 'Weg' is masculine. The plural is 'Wege'.

items.sentence_de: Mein Weg zum Job dauert etwa dreißig Minuten.
items.sentence_translation: My way to work takes about thirty minutes.
items.grammar_tip: 'Job' is a common informal word for 'Arbeit' in German.

items.sentence_de: Ich schicke dir eine Wegbeschreibung per E-Mail.
items.sentence_translation: I'll send you directions via email.
items.grammar_tip: Ending in -ung, this noun is always feminine.

items.sentence_de: Kannst du bitte deine Schuhe schnell wegräumen?
items.sentence_translation: Can you please put your shoes away quickly?
items.grammar_tip: 'Wegräumen' is a separable verb: räum... weg.

items.sentence_de: Mein Rücken wird mir morgen sicher wehtun.
items.sentence_translation: My back will certainly hurt tomorrow.
items.grammar_tip: 'Wehtun' is a separable verb and takes the Dative case (mir, dir, ihm...).

items.sentence_de: Im Dezember gehen wir oft auf den Weihnachtsmarkt.
items.sentence_translation: In December we often go to the Christmas market.
items.grammar_tip: 'Markt' is masculine, so 'Weihnachtsmarkt' is also masculine.

items.sentence_de: Auf diese Weise können wir das Problem lösen.
items.sentence_translation: In this manner we can solve the problem.
items.grammar_tip: The phrase 'auf diese Weise' means 'in this way/manner'.

items.sentence_de: Mein neues Hemd ist ganz weiß und sauber.
items.sentence_translation: My new shirt is completely white and clean.
items.grammar_tip: Color names are usually used as adjectives in lower case.

items.sentence_de: Haben Sie noch weitere Fragen zu diesem Thema?
items.sentence_translation: Do you have any further questions on this topic?
items.grammar_tip: 'Weitere' implies additional items of the same kind.

items.sentence_de: Wir wollen jetzt die CD fertig weiterhören.
items.sentence_translation: We want to continue listening to the CD until the end.
items.grammar_tip: The prefix 'weiter-' indicates the continuation of an action.

items.sentence_de: Können wir bitte nach der Pause weitermachen?
items.sentence_translation: Can we please continue after the break?
items.grammar_tip: 'Weitermachen' is separable: machen... weiter.

items.sentence_de: Welcher Tag ist heute? Heute ist Dienstag.
items.sentence_translation: Which day is today? Today is Tuesday.
items.grammar_tip: 'Welcher' acts like an article and changes endings based on gender and case.

items.sentence_de: Wem gehört dieses rote Fahrrad vor der Tür?
items.sentence_translation: To whom does this red bike in front of the door belong?
items.grammar_tip: 'Wem' is the Dative form of 'Wer'. The verb 'gehören' always takes Dative.

items.sentence_de: Wen hast du gestern auf der Party gesehen?
items.sentence_translation: Whom did you see at the party yesterday?
items.grammar_tip: 'Wen' is the Accusative form of 'Wer'. Use it for direct objects.

items.sentence_de: Das ist ein großes Haus. Wer wohnt denn da?
items.sentence_translation: That is a big house. Who lives there?
items.grammar_tip: 'Denn' is a particle here that makes the question sound more natural/interested.

items.sentence_de: Sofia wird im nächsten Monat dreißig Jahre alt.
items.sentence_translation: Sofia is turning thirty years old next month.
items.grammar_tip: 'Werden' is used to express changes in state or age.

items.sentence_de: Mein Auto ist kaputt und in der Werkstatt.
items.sentence_translation: My car is broken and in the workshop.
items.grammar_tip: The plural is 'Werkstätten'. It is a feminine noun.

items.sentence_de: Im Westen von Deutschland regnet es heute.
items.sentence_translation: In the west of Germany it is raining today.
items.grammar_tip: Compass directions are always masculine: der Norden, Süden, Westen, Osten.

items.sentence_de: Hast du schon den Wetterbericht für morgen gehört?
items.sentence_translation: Have you already heard the weather report for tomorrow?
items.grammar_tip: 'Wetterbericht' is a compound of 'Wetter' and 'Bericht' (report).

items.sentence_de: Ich wohne mit zwei Freunden in einer WG.
items.sentence_translation: I live with two friends in a flat share.
items.grammar_tip: WG stands for 'Wohngemeinschaft'. It is feminine.

items.sentence_de: Wie bitte? Ich habe Sie nicht genau verstanden.
items.sentence_translation: Excuse me? I didn't understand you exactly.
items.grammar_tip: Use 'Wie bitte?' when you didn't hear or understand something.

items.sentence_de: Wie lange dauert der Flug nach New York?
items.sentence_translation: How long does the flight to New York take?
items.grammar_tip: 'Wie lange' asks about the duration of time.

items.sentence_de: Wie viele Geschwister hast du eigentlich?
items.sentence_translation: How many siblings do you actually have?
items.grammar_tip: 'Wie viel' is for uncountable things, 'wie viele' for plural countable things.

items.sentence_de: Du warst im Urlaub. Wie war's denn?
items.sentence_translation: You were on vacation. How was it?
items.grammar_tip: 'War' is the past tense of 'sein'. 's' is short for 'es'.

items.sentence_de: Wir müssen uns bald unbedingt mal wieder treffen.
items.sentence_translation: We definitely need to meet up again soon.
items.grammar_tip: 'Wieder' means 'one more time' or 'again'.

items.sentence_de: Kannst du den Text in eigenen Worten wiedergeben?
items.sentence_translation: Can you recite the text in your own words?
items.grammar_tip: 'Wiedergeben' literally means 'to give back' but is used for repeating info.

items.sentence_de: Wie viel wiegen diese Äpfel in der Tüte?
items.sentence_translation: How much do these apples in the bag weigh?
items.grammar_tip: The past participle of 'wiegen' is 'gewogen'.

items.sentence_de: Heute ist es draußen sehr kalt und windig.
items.sentence_translation: Today it is very cold and windy outside.
items.grammar_tip: Adding '-ig' to 'Wind' makes it an adjective.

items.sentence_de: Im Winter fahren wir oft zum Skifahren.
items.sentence_translation: In winter we often go skiing.
items.grammar_tip: Seasons are always masculine (der Sommer, der Winter, etc.).

items.sentence_de: Ich brauche für den Urlaub eine neue Winterjacke.
items.sentence_translation: I need a new winter jacket for the vacation.
items.grammar_tip: 'Jacke' is feminine, so 'Winterjacke' is also feminine.

items.sentence_de: Spielst du wirklich so gut Gitarre wie er?
items.sentence_translation: Do you really play guitar as well as he does?
items.grammar_tip: 'Wirklich' is used to emphasize a fact or ask for confirmation.

items.sentence_de: Ich weiß leider nicht, wie er heißt.
items.sentence_translation: Unfortunately, I don't know what his name is.
items.grammar_tip: 'Wissen' is used for facts, while 'kennen' is used for people or places.

items.sentence_de: Wie ist bitte das Passwort für das WLAN?
items.sentence_translation: What is the password for the Wi-Fi, please?
items.grammar_tip: German uses the term WLAN (pronounced 'Vay-Lan') for Wi-Fi.

items.sentence_de: Eine Woche hat genau sieben verschiedene Tage.
items.sentence_translation: A week has exactly seven different days.
items.grammar_tip: Plural of 'Woche' is 'Wochen'. It is a feminine noun.

items.sentence_de: Was machst du normalerweise an diesem Wochenende?
items.sentence_translation: What do you normally do this weekend?
items.grammar_tip: 'Wochenende' is a neuter noun (das). The plural is also 'Wochenende'.

items.sentence_de: Welcher Wochentag ist heute eigentlich genau?
items.sentence_translation: Which day of the week is it exactly today?
items.grammar_tip: Wochentage (Monday-Saturday) are all masculine.

items.sentence_de: Guten Tag, Woher kommen Sie ursprünglich?
items.sentence_translation: Good day, where are you originally from?
items.grammar_tip: 'Woher' asks for origin. 'Sie' is the formal address.

items.sentence_de: Ich sehe dich draußen. Wohin gehst du?
items.sentence_translation: I see you outside. Where are you going?
items.grammar_tip: 'Wohin' asks for direction or destination.

items.sentence_de: Wie ist Ihre aktuelle Wohnsituation in Berlin?
items.sentence_translation: How is your current living situation in Berlin?
items.grammar_tip: This is a compound noun: Wohnen (living) + Situation.

items.sentence_de: Die Wohnung hat eine Wohnfläche von 60m².
items.sentence_translation: The flat has a living space of 60m².
items.grammar_tip: Fläche means area or space.

items.sentence_de: Welche Wohnform finden Sie am besten?
items.sentence_translation: Which form of housing do you find best?
items.grammar_tip: Housing forms include WG (flatshare) or single flats.

items.sentence_de: Bitte geben Sie Ihren aktuellen Wohnort an.
items.sentence_translation: Please state your current place of residence.
items.grammar_tip: Ort means place or location.

items.sentence_de: Ich habe heute eine gute Wohnungsanzeige gelesen.
items.sentence_translation: I read a good apartment advertisement today.
items.grammar_tip: Compound noun: Wohnung (apartment) + Anzeige (advertisement).

items.sentence_de: Die Wohnungssuche in München ist sehr schwer.
items.sentence_translation: The apartment search in Munich is very difficult.
items.grammar_tip: Suche means search; Wohnungssuche is feminine like die Suche.

items.sentence_de: Wir sitzen am Abend oft im Wohnzimmer.
items.sentence_translation: We often sit in the living room in the evening.
items.grammar_tip: Zimmer (room) is always neuter (das).

items.sentence_de: Dort am Himmel ist eine große Wolke.
items.sentence_translation: There is a big cloud in the sky.
items.grammar_tip: Wolke is feminine.

items.sentence_de: Ich will am Wochenende ins Kino gehen.
items.sentence_translation: I want to go to the cinema on the weekend.
items.grammar_tip: 'Wollen' is a modal verb. The first person singular is 'ich will'.

items.sentence_de: Ich kenne dieses deutsche Wort noch nicht.
items.sentence_translation: I don't know this German word yet.
items.grammar_tip: The plural is 'Wörter' for vocabulary and 'Worte' for speech.

items.sentence_de: Hören Sie den Laut am Wortanfang?
items.sentence_translation: Do you hear the sound at the beginning of the word?
items.grammar_tip: Anfang means beginning.

items.sentence_de: Der Buchstabe steht oft am Wortende.
items.sentence_translation: The letter is often at the end of the word.
items.grammar_tip: Ende (end) is neuter.

items.sentence_de: Ich muss jeden Tag neue Wörter lernen.
items.sentence_translation: I have to learn new words every day.
items.grammar_tip: Lernen is the verb for studying/learning.

items.sentence_de: Darf ich bitte Ihr Wörterbuch benutzen?
items.sentence_translation: May I please use your dictionary?
items.grammar_tip: Compound: Wörter + Buch (book).

items.sentence_de: Markieren Sie die Wortgruppe im Text.
items.sentence_translation: Highlight the word group in the text.
items.grammar_tip: Gruppe is feminine.

items.sentence_de: Achten Sie auf Vokale im Wortinnere.
items.sentence_translation: Pay attention to vowels inside the word.
items.grammar_tip: Innere is treated as a neuter noun here.

items.sentence_de: Schreiben Sie die Vokabeln in die Wortliste.
items.sentence_translation: Write the vocabulary in the word list.
items.grammar_tip: Liste is feminine.

items.sentence_de: Dieser Wortteil ist für die Grammatik wichtig.
items.sentence_translation: This word part is important for the grammar.
items.grammar_tip: Teil (part) is usually masculine.

items.sentence_de: Die Wunde am Bein tut weh.
items.sentence_translation: The wound on the leg hurts.
items.grammar_tip: Wunde is a feminine noun.

items.sentence_de: Das Wetter heute ist einfach wunderschön.
items.sentence_translation: The weather today is simply beautiful.
items.grammar_tip: Wunder (wonder) + schön (beautiful).

items.sentence_de: Haben Sie noch einen besonderen Wunsch?
items.sentence_translation: Do you have another special wish?
items.grammar_tip: Der Wunsch has the plural 'die Wünsche'.

items.sentence_de: Ich wünsche dir alles Gute zum Geburtstag.
items.sentence_translation: I wish you all the best for your birthday.
items.grammar_tip: Often used with dative objects (dir/Ihnen).

items.sentence_de: Du bist dran, du musst jetzt würfeln.
items.sentence_translation: It's your turn, you have to roll the dice now.
items.grammar_tip: Comes from 'der Würfel' (the cube/die).

items.sentence_de: Möchten Sie lieber Käse oder Wurst?
items.sentence_translation: Would you prefer cheese or sausage?
items.grammar_tip: Wurst is feminine in German.

items.sentence_de: Die Kinder essen gerne Würstchen mit Ketchup.
items.sentence_translation: The children like eating small sausages with ketchup.
items.grammar_tip: Words ending in -chen are always neuter.

items.sentence_de: Ich bestelle zwei Wiener Würstel zum Mittagessen.
items.sentence_translation: I'm ordering two Viennese sausages for lunch.
items.grammar_tip: Austrian/Southern German variation for Würstchen.

items.sentence_de: Besuchen Sie unsere Webseite unter www.dobart.de.
items.sentence_translation: Visit our website at www.dobart.de.
items.grammar_tip: German speakers say 'punkt' for the dot.

items.sentence_de: Ich mache jeden Dienstagabend Yoga im Park.
items.sentence_translation: I do yoga every Tuesday evening in the park.
items.grammar_tip: Yoga is usually used without an article.

items.sentence_de: Schreiben Sie bitte die richtige Zahl auf.
items.sentence_translation: Please write down the correct number.
items.grammar_tip: Zahl refers to the digit/numeral.

items.sentence_de: Das Passwort besteht aus Zahlen und Buchstaben.
items.sentence_translation: The password consists of numbers and letters.
items.grammar_tip: Standard components of passwords and IDs.

items.sentence_de: Mein linker Zahn tut sehr weh.
items.sentence_translation: My left tooth hurts a lot.
items.grammar_tip: Plural is 'Zähne'.

items.sentence_de: Ich habe morgen einen Termin beim Zahnarzt.
items.sentence_translation: I have an appointment at the dentist tomorrow.
items.grammar_tip: Zahn (tooth) + Arzt (doctor).

items.sentence_de: Die Zahnärztin untersucht heute meine Zähne.
items.sentence_translation: The dentist is examining my teeth today.
items.grammar_tip: Feminine form of Zahnarzt.

items.sentence_de: Bei Zahnschmerzen gehe ich sofort zum Arzt.
items.sentence_translation: When I have a toothache, I go to the doctor immediately.
items.grammar_tip: Used almost exclusively in plural.

items.sentence_de: Kannst du ein Haus für mich zeichnen?
items.sentence_translation: Can you draw a house for me?
items.grammar_tip: Zeichnen usually involves a pencil or pen.

items.sentence_de: Die Zeichnung an der Wand gefällt mir.
items.sentence_translation: I like the drawing on the wall.
items.grammar_tip: Nouns ending in -ung are always feminine.

items.sentence_de: Können Sie mir bitte den Weg zeigen?
items.sentence_translation: Can you please show me the way?
items.grammar_tip: Requires a dative object (meir/Ihnen) and accusative (den Weg).

items.sentence_de: Zeigen Sie bitte auf das richtige Bild.
items.sentence_translation: Please point to the correct picture.
items.grammar_tip: 'Zeigen auf' (+ accusative) means to point at something.

items.sentence_de: Achten Sie auf die Zeitangabe im Satz.
items.sentence_translation: Pay attention to the time indication in the sentence.
items.grammar_tip: Zeit (time) + Angabe (specification/statement).

items.sentence_de: Ich lese im Wartezimmer oft eine Zeitschrift.
items.sentence_translation: I often read a magazine in the waiting room.
items.grammar_tip: Zeitschrift is more focused on topics than a newspaper (Zeitung).

items.sentence_de: Wir schlafen im Urlaub in einem Zelt.
items.sentence_translation: We sleep in a tent on vacation.
items.grammar_tip: Das Zelt is neuter.

items.sentence_de: Das Hotel liegt sehr zentral am Marktplatz.
items.sentence_translation: The hotel is located very centrally at the market square.
items.grammar_tip: Commonly used for location/position.

items.sentence_de: Wir fahren heute mit dem Bus ins Zentrum.
items.sentence_translation: We are going to the center by bus today.
items.grammar_tip: The plural is irregular: Zentren.

items.sentence_de: Wir müssen den Schrank für den Umzug zerlegen.
items.sentence_translation: We have to disassemble the wardrobe for the move.
items.grammar_tip: Zer- prefix often indicates destruction or separation.

items.sentence_de: Ich schreibe die Telefonnummer auf einen Zettel.
items.sentence_translation: I write the phone number on a slip of paper.
items.grammar_tip: Der Zettel is masculine.

items.sentence_de: Bitte ziehen Sie eine Karte vom Stapel.
items.sentence_translation: Please draw a card from the stack.
items.grammar_tip: In games, 'ziehen' means to draw or pick.

items.sentence_de: Beata ist in eine neue Wohnung gezogen.
items.sentence_translation: Beata has moved into a new apartment.
items.grammar_tip: 'Ist gezogen' is the perfect tense of 'ziehen' meaning to move house.

items.sentence_de: Was ist Ihr berufliches Ziel für nächstes Jahr?
items.sentence_translation: What is your professional goal for next year?
items.grammar_tip: Das Ziel is neuter.

items.sentence_de: Am Sonntag gehen wir mit den Kindern in den Zoo.
items.sentence_translation: On Sunday we are going to the zoo with the children.
items.grammar_tip: Masculine: der Zoo.

items.sentence_de: Ich gehe jeden Morgen zu Fuß zur Arbeit.
items.sentence_translation: I go to work on foot every morning.
items.grammar_tip: Fixed phrase: always 'zu Fuß'.

items.sentence_de: Der Supermarkt hat am Sonntag leider zu.
items.sentence_translation: The supermarket is unfortunately closed on Sunday.
items.grammar_tip: 'Zu haben' or 'geschlossen sein' mean the same thing.

items.sentence_de: Ich bin heute Abend den ganzen Tag zu Hause.
items.sentence_translation: I am at home all day this evening.
items.grammar_tip: 'Zu Hause' (location) vs 'nach Hause' (direction).

items.sentence_de: Wir essen normalerweise um zwölf Uhr zu Mittag.
items.sentence_translation: We usually eat lunch at twelve o'clock.
items.grammar_tip: Literally 'at noon'.

items.sentence_de: Ich möchte heute ein gesundes Abendessen zubereiten.
items.sentence_translation: I want to prepare a healthy dinner today.
items.grammar_tip: A separable verb: 'ich bereite ... zu'.

items.sentence_de: Trinken Sie Ihren Kaffee mit oder ohne Zucker?
items.sentence_translation: Do you drink your coffee with or without sugar?
items.grammar_tip: Uncountable noun, masculine: der Zucker.

items.sentence_de: Zuerst frühstücken wir, dann gehen wir spazieren.
items.sentence_translation: First we have breakfast, then we go for a walk.
items.grammar_tip: Used to sequence events.

items.sentence_de: Dass wir uns hier treffen, ist ein Zufall.
items.sentence_translation: It is a coincidence that we are meeting here.
items.grammar_tip: Der Zufall (masculine).

items.sentence_de: Der Zug nach Berlin hat zehn Minuten Verspätung.
items.sentence_translation: The train to Berlin is ten minutes late.
items.grammar_tip: Masculine: der Zug.

items.sentence_de: Zum Glück habe ich meinen Schlüssel wieder gefunden.
items.sentence_translation: Luckily I found my key again.
items.grammar_tip: 'Glück' means luck/happiness.

items.sentence_de: Zum Schluss machen wir ein Foto von allen.
items.sentence_translation: At the end we take a photo of everyone.
items.grammar_tip: 'Schluss' means end or conclusion.

items.sentence_de: Wir trinken auf das neue Jahr – zum Wohl!
items.sentence_translation: We drink to the new year – cheers!
items.grammar_tip: A formal way to say 'Prost'.

items.sentence_de: Kannst du bitte das Fenster im Zimmer zumachen?
items.sentence_translation: Can you please close the window in the room?
items.grammar_tip: Separable verb: 'ich mache das Fenster zu'.

items.sentence_de: Zumba macht mir Spaß und hält mich fit.
items.sentence_translation: Zumba is fun and keeps me fit.
items.grammar_tip: Usually used without an article.

items.sentence_de: Ordnen Sie die Bilder den richtigen Wörtern zu.
items.sentence_translation: Match the pictures to the correct words.
items.grammar_tip: A separable verb: 'ich ordne ... zu'.

items.sentence_de: Wir müssen am Sonntagabend mit dem Auto zurückfahren.
items.sentence_translation: We have to drive back by car on Sunday evening.
items.grammar_tip: Separable verb using 'zurück-' (back).

items.sentence_de: Ich hoffe, wir können den Weg zum Hotel zurückfinden.
items.sentence_translation: I hope we can find our way back to the hotel.
items.grammar_tip: Separable verb.

items.sentence_de: Das Kleid passt nicht, ich muss es zurückschicken.
items.sentence_translation: The dress doesn't fit, I have to send it back.
items.grammar_tip: Common in online shopping.

items.sentence_de: Diese beiden Socken gehören leider nicht zusammen.
items.sentence_translation: Unfortunately, these two socks do not belong together.
items.grammar_tip: Used for things that form a pair or group.

items.sentence_de: Die Farbe und das Sofa passen gut zusammen.
items.sentence_translation: The color and the sofa fit well together.
items.grammar_tip: Often used for aesthetics or compatibility.

items.sentence_de: Es sind heute viele Zuschauer im Stadion.
items.sentence_translation: There are many spectators in the stadium today.
items.grammar_tip: Der Zuschauer (singular and plural are the same).

items.sentence_de: Eine Zuschauerin hat den Ball gefangen.
items.sentence_translation: A female spectator caught the ball.
items.grammar_tip: Feminine version of Zuschauer.

items.sentence_de: Ich war schon zweimal in den USA.
items.sentence_translation: I have already been to the USA twice.
items.grammar_tip: Number + -mal expresses frequency.

items.sentence_de: Bitte arbeiten Sie zu zweit an dieser Aufgabe.
items.sentence_translation: Please work in pairs on this task.
items.grammar_tip: 'Zu zweit' means 'as a pair of two'.

items.sentence_de: Ich brauche eine Zwiebel für die Suppe.
items.sentence_translation: I need an onion for the soup.
items.grammar_tip: Feminine noun: die Zwiebel.
